When Dolly Parton died, it was her nephew Bryan Seaver who broke the news to the world.

The Queen of Country had long trusted Seaver, the son of her sister Cassie Parton, as her head of security and handpicked him to make the announcement in a widely-shared video.

However, in the weeks since her August 25 death, a series of troubling allegations have led to Seaver being fired from his security role by Parton’s estate.

Danny Nozell, Parton’s longtime manager, filed a restraining order Tuesday against Seaver in a Tennessee court on behalf of She's Alive LLC, the company that now manages Parton’s business empire. The filing claimed that Seaver’s “terrorizing conduct made their continued retention untenable.”

As Variety reported, the filing went on to allege that Seaver threatened Nozell and various other employees in an attempt to extort money, calling himself a “killer” and “literally an international arms dealer and mercenary.” He allegedly added: “All I do is warfare.”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver has reportedly been fired as head of security ( Getty Images/Dolly Parton )

In a statement to TMZ, Seaver denied the allegation that he was attempting to extort money from the estate, but maintained other claims were simply taken out of context.

“I am a career soldier and military contractor and do conduct arms deals for foreign governments,” Seaver told the publication. “I am a security professional and I am a killer.”

He continued: “However, nothing in this lawsuit were threats and most of the comments I stand by. I was talking frankly in a private way with Danny who I thought was my friend and he fancies himself a gangster. A lot of these messages are two guys having rage talk and crying on the phone together while we were grieving.”

Seaver spent more than two decades as Parton’s head of security, succeeding his father Larry Seaver in the role. He runs Squadron Augmented Protection Services (SAPS), LLC, which describes itself as “the premier provider of critical security services in Nashville.”

As a child, Seaver often found himself on tour with Parton. Her 1993 song “Romeo” was reportedly written as a warning to the then-16-year-old Seaver about the dangers of getting his heart broken.

In Nozell’s legal filing, it is alleged that Seaver began a campaign of intimidation in the weeks leading up to Parton’s death in an attempt to obtain significant sums of money.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton died with a net worth of over $450 million, according to estimates ( Alamy/PA )

The documents contain reproductions of text messages allegedly sent by Seaver to Nozell, including one that threatens: “I’m going to destroy the entire brand if you don’t get these [Dollywood business partners] out of our bit. . . . I’m going to go to Billboard Magazine with my s***. Just like you. I’m going to ratf*** every [Dollywood business partner] entity I can possibly conjure.”

Another allegedly stated: “I’m not an entertainment person. I’m a killer. I sold 27 million $ worth of ammunition and arms to the Haitian Police on day Dolly died. Entertainment is not my game. I have spent my career breaking things and spying on African and Arab leaders. And protecting Dolly.”

A third was claimed to say: “I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f***ing pay me.”

Another reportedly claimed: “I am vengeance for my people for the next 50 years. I have no debt. I only own swords and guns. My children have 3 houses to live in forever. My wife owns everything. All I have is animosity and memory. But I’m going to spend the next times I have on earth ratf***ing anyone that has ever betrayed my family.”

In a separate statement to ABC News, Seaver described the restraining order against him as “spurious and simply a publicity stunt.”

He again suggested his words had been misconstrued, saying: “Dolly called me her killer. It was a joke we used around her camp. I was her ‘baby boy ninja’ and Danny Nozell took that text out of context to somehow imagine that I was threatening him. He’s always called me The Killer. I’ve never threatened anyone ... They are my friends and my brothers and colleagues.”

Seaver added: “I was fired. After the estate negotiated with me and my company for services in perpetuity and agreed to that service provision from my company. A week later they fired me for these contrived ‘threats.’”

SAPS had been responsible for security at various Parton properties, but footage from last week obtained by TMZ showed replacement guards taking over posts at Parton’s home in Nashville, as well as her museum and warehouse.

Parton died with a net worth of over $450 million, according to estimates.

News.title: Zelensky lashes out at EU
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky lashed out at the European Union over its moves to weaken sanctions on Russian oligarchs.

In his address to the UN General Assembly, the Ukrainian leader warned that beyond making life “more comfortable” for Russians, “it also gives the war more time for Putin to send poor people into the kill zone. So Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

His criticism came after France and Luxembourg successfully pushed for sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Russian oligarchs, on Tuesday.

Kyiv branded the decision “shameful and unjustifiable”. The men are known to share close ties to Vladimir Putin and have net worths of $14bn and $16bn, respectively.

In his fourth address to the UN as a wartime leader, Mr Zelensky said it was paramount that the international community increased pressure on the Kremlin to stop “the madness” of the war spreading.

Under pressure from Donald Trump to halt attacks on Russian energy targets, Mr Zelensky defended his country’s aerial offensive for successfully depriving Putin of revenue for his war.

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

‘End the war before winter’

Washington has recently attempted to revive the long-stalled negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. On Tuesday, Mr Zelensky implored Mr Trump to help Kyiv end the war “before winter”.

Mr Trump appeared optimistic, suggesting an agreement would happen “more quickly than people understand”.

Sergei Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Russia was prepared to negotiate for a lasting peace but would not “pause the war”.

Mr Zelensky sought to remind world leaders that the conflict was not constrained within Ukraine’s borders at a time when the global community was distracted by a myriad of conflicts and crises.

Citing the support of Iran and North Korea for Russia, he warned that Putin’s war kept “spreading further”.

“Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land, take more territory and take another country instead of simply stopping and running his own country,” Mr Zelensky said at the UN.

He noted that fighters from at least 47 countries were helping to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine and urged leaders to prevent their citizens from being dragged into the conflict.

After Mr Zelensky’s address, reports emerged that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s envoy, was on his way to the US where he would meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the Trump administration representatives.

Sources told Reuters that the meeting would take place in New ‌York on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, also confirmed Mr Trump had invited his Russian counterpart to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December.

News.title: Male contraceptives could hit pharmacies in ‘three to five years’, says WHO
News.content:
Game-changing contraceptives for men could be on pharmacy shelves as soon as 2029, according to the World Health Organization.

Speaking to the Telegraph, Dr James Kiarie, head of the UN agency’s contraception and fertility care unit, said he expects male birth control to be available in just a few years, in a major expansion of contraceptive options for men.

“In three to five years, we will actually have a method available, [so] men can be more than supporters of their female partners in using contraception – men can actually be users,” he said.

On Tuesday, the WHO released its first Target Product Profiles (TPPs) for these products, setting out guidelines for the desired and minimum standards any male contraceptive product must meet.

“[The TPPs] signals that this is a priority issue for the WHO,” said Dr Kiarie.

“Currently men do not have much option in terms of their contraceptive methods. They have to either use condoms… [or] they have to use withdrawal, which has a high failure rate, or they have to use vasectomy, which is a permanent method.”

At the moment, the most advanced new product is called NES/T. It is a daily hormonal gel that is applied to the shoulders and upper arms, and suppresses sperm production without affecting testosterone levels.

Other candidates include injectable hydrogels that block sperm travel, an approach that has been described as a “reversible vasectomy”. ADAM, developed by Contraline, is in phase 1 trials while Next Life Sciences is set to trial a similar product called Plan A.

A third option is YCT-529 – the first non-hormonal, daily male birth control pill. It is currently in phase 1b and 2a clinical trials.

Dr Kiarie said it was important to have multiple options as “there’s no one size fits all” approach, but warned development could take longer than five years if clinical trials face unexpected hurdles.

News.title: England learn more in scrappy Sri Lanka win than in summer of white-ball walkovers
News.content:
You do not expect spinners to dominate at Chester-le-Street, but this hot summer has produced strange events, none more so than Jacks recording the second-best figures by an England spinner in one-day international cricket having previously only taken three wickets in 16 games at home.

Sachindu Colombage, Sri Lanka’s debutant leggie who was playing club cricket in East Anglia a year ago, laid down a marker as he impressed with three for 44 starting with the wicket of Root, his first dismissal in one-day international cricket since February.

England’s 89-run win was completed by Jacks taking three for none in four balls as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 176, their run chase a timid effort when they had a sniff of victory after restricting England to 265 and preventing them from hitting a six for the first time in an innings since 2019.

Vice-captain Jacks has evolved under Harry Brook’s leadership from an opening batsman to middle-order finisher who can chip in with the ball. “He is just a good leader with bat ball and in the field. He is buying into everything we want to do,” Brook said. “We are always talking about adapting to conditions and he has done it really well since coming back in. He could have moaned and groaned about batting in the middle order and playing as an all-rounder but has accepted that will be his place for a long time.”

Brook thought England made “just about par” on a very dry pitch and was reluctant to shower too much praise on batting consultant Kevin Pietersen, whose spin class the day before concentrated on making runs on a slow surface. “It will take time, more than one day. He’s not a miracle worker but it helps the more opportunity we get,” Brook said.

England were stretched and Pietersen will be happy. He told them to think about their approach, that in this type of game “rotation of strike is incredibly important”. He was right, they ran well, apart from Rehan Ahmed, and did not hit a six in an innings for the first time in seven years.

When England batsmen tried to force the pace they perished. Ben Duckett, Root and Brook all had opportunities to build an innings without seeing it through and it required Jacks to tip the total to more than 250. He batted within himself at first, but hit four fours in a row in the 47th over in a late burst that took England to a winning score.

News.title: Africa faces new threat as chronic disease rate leaps
News.content:
Chronic ailments like heart disease, cancers and diabetes now account for almost half of deaths in Africa and will soon overtake the continent’s infectious disease toll, new research has found.

Between 1990 and 2023 the proportion of deaths caused by non-communicable diseases (NCDs) almost doubled, from 25 per cent to 45 per cent, with heart disease and strokes now the leading killers.

The shift is not unexpected: public health experts have long warned that although African countries are making huge strides cutting infectious disease deaths through vaccinations, better sanitation and improved healthcare, lifestyle changes pose a new threat.

But the continent is not necessarily ready to tackle this “epidemiological transition”, researchers warned, in a study published in the Lancet Global Health journal on Tuesday.

“Although the epidemiological transition is well recognised, the speed and scale of NCD growth in Africa is particularly concerning,” they wrote.

“Health systems face increasing demands for chronic disease management, yet low-resource settings remain poorly equipped, underfunded, and unable to provide adequate preventive or treatment services.”

News.title: Zika mosquitoes still breeding in London
News.content:
Invasive mosquitoes capable of carrying Zika and dengue are still breeding in London, weeks after they were detected reproducing in Britain for the first time.

Although the tropical mosquitoes have previously hitch-hiked into the UK, they have never before been spotted breeding – raising concerns that rising temperatures are making the country more inhabitable for the disease-ridden insects.

In a bid to curb the threat, specialist teams from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) were deployed to destroy the larvae and ramp up surveillance and trapping.

But small colonies are still being detected in the area, Dr Jolyon Medlock, head of medical entomology and zoonoses ecology at the agency, told the Telegraph on Tuesday.

“We’re doing source reduction, removing suitable habitats, treatment of drains, and community engagement, and mass-trapping to hoover any of the mosquitoes that are around,” Dr Medlock said. “We’re still picking up small numbers of these mosquitoes now.”

Unlike native British mosquitoes, the Aedes aegypti are capable of spreading tropical diseases like Zika virus, dengue, and yellow fever. They are typically found in Africa and Asia.

Yet, after a homeowner sent images to the Mosquito Watch website, the UKHSA realised a small colony had established itself in the British capital.

News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said spending outstripped tax receipts by £18.3bn in August, £3.5bn more than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Reacting to the figures, Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier Budget than Andy Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor would need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

The Government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, according to the ONS, the biggest August figure since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest – £2bn more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, 7pc more than a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see substantial tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and National Insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew. They have risen to £3.8bn so far this financial year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said: “Labour has lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

ACHRAF HAKIMI will stand trial for rape after losing his bid to have the case thrown out.

It was announced in June that the PSG and Morocco star would go on trial for an alleged assault on a woman in February 2023.



Hakimi, who vehemently denies the allegation, tried to get the case thrown out by lodging a motion to dismiss it with a French appeals court.

But on Wednesday, the Cour de cassation rejected his bid to have the case struck off, meaning The Atlas Lions’ talismanic skipper will have to go in the dock to address the allegation.



After the ruling, the woman’s lawyer, Rachel-Flore Pardo, said: “After three and a half years of legal battle, after being slandered and dragged through the mud by Achraf Hakimi‘s defence, my client is determined to obtain justice and will fight to the end.

“She sincerely hopes that this trial will help other women and further crack the fortress of denial and impunity surrounding sexual violence, even in the world of men’s football.”

Hakimi’s lawyer, Fanny Colin, told Le Monde when approached for comment: “The facts reproached to Achraf Hakimi, which he has firmly contested from the first day, have not been examined by the Cour de cassation.

“They will be during the trial, in the course of which all the elements in defence of Mr Achraf Hakimi will be publicly and contradictorily presented.

“Mr Hakimi, who has nothing to hide, has for his part fully cooperated with the police and judicial authorities and will continue to do so on the occasion of the forthcoming trial.”

Hakimi, who is in contention to win the Ballon d’Or, has maintained his innocence since the allegation was made against him.



In an interview with Canal+ last September, he said of the accusation last September: “For me, it’s the hardest thing that’s ever happened to me.

“And the truth is, it’s the hardest blow I’ve ever suffered. I think it was pretty hard for me, and it still is, because when they keep telling lie after lie, it hurts.

“It hurts for my family, for my children, who are young and don’t know what the internet or reading is.

“I know that at some point in their lives they’ll read things, and for me, seeing that something about their father has been written and on top of that, it’s a lie, is not very pleasant, and I honestly wouldn’t wish that on them.



“I think my lawyer told me so. We knew this could happen. We’re calm. I know what I’ve been accused of. It’s a lie. I know who I am. I know I haven’t done anything.

“And I never would. I asked to speak to the police, to them, to explain my version.

“Always when they’ve needed me for anything… What’s more, they have my DNA.

“Whatever they needed, I was available, unlike the person accusing me, who didn’t make things easy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thanks to the police’s work, we’ve been able to find quite a few good things.



“The truth is, I’m calm. I know I’m in good hands with my lawyer. Justice is doing its work, and I hope the truth comes out soon.”

Sports.title: Premier League’s fastest players of 2025/26 so far with Liverpool new-boy Bradley Barcola already speediest star

THE first five weeks of the 2026/27 Premier League season have come thick and fast.

The final whistle has already been blown for 50 of the 380 games.



But what is going even quicker than the rapid pace of the fixtures are the global talents tearing up the pitch every matchday.

Manchester City may be top of the league table after Arsenal were embarrassed at Brighton, but it’s Liverpool who sit top of the pile in the speed rankings.



In fact, City have NO players featuring in the top 15 list at all, and Arsenal can only lay claim to 14th-placed Cristhian Mosquera at 21.64 miles per hour.

Bradley Barcola signed a five-year deal to become the club’s second-most-expensive signing ever at Anfield.



And the 23-year-old reached a mindblowing top speed of 22.32 mph just SIX minutes into his FIRST Prem appearance at Ipswich, where the Reds secured a 2-0 victory.

But even though Barcola tops this season’s speed rankings as of present, his effort is still short of the Prem’s top ten fastest speeds since 2020/21.

Micky van de Ven comes top of those rankings with a crazy speed of 37.

The rankings are incredibly close, with only 0.7mph separating top and bottom of the list.



But Barcola has a clear lead at the top, putting more distance between himself and the rest of the pack than each player and their nearest ranking rival.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Manchester United’s Bryan Mbeumo is 0.35mph behind in the pace race with a jaw-dropping speed of 21.97mph, following his performance in the 2-2 draw with Everton earlier this month.

Mbeumo’s 47th-minute goal handed United the lead before Tyrique George’s equaliser.

Unfortunately for the Red Devils, they were forced to settle for a point after Ainsley Maitland-Niles injury-time equaliser cancelled out Benjamin Sesko’s late effort.



Shaky Fulham’s Gonzalo Garcia (21.97mph) pinches bronze in the table, while Hull’s Robinho Vaz (21.92mph) places fourth.

The question of whether the Premier League is getting quicker seems easy to answer with 40 per cent of the 15 ranked stars NOT featuring in the league last season.

Not only with Barcola – but also Garcia after his summer move from Real Madrid and Vaz’s temporary switch from Roma to the newly-promoted side.

It’s not only those in attack who can chase someone down.



The likes of Coventry right-back Milan Van Ewijk (21.9mph) – who is level with Chelsea’s Pedro Neto – brings a rapid new identity to those further back in the field.

Brentford’s Kristoffer Ajer (21.79mph), Aston Villa’s Ian Maatsen (21.72mph), and Sunderland’s Reinildo (21.66mph) all make a good case for the defence.

Of course, Mosquera too.

And while other rankings will look top-heavy with the ‘Big Six’ coming to dominate the party, the pace race has not seen that happen, with Newcastle boasting the most players of any side in the fastest 15 with three.



Jacob Murphy (21.84mph) comes top of that trio.

And new-signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21.82mph) sits between the pair in the latest era of the Toon.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vows to carry on playing for Portugal and targets 1,000-goal landmark
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo vows to carry on playing for Portugal and targets 1,000-goal landmark

Cristiano Ronaldo has decided to keep playing for Portugal at the age of 41, despite suffering huge disappointment at the World Cup and facing increased criticism over his performances

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo is still going at the age of 41 (Image: Fadel SENNA / AFP via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has hit back at his critics and vowed to carry on playing for Portugal as he nears 1,000 career goals.

‌



Ronaldo's future in international football was in doubt following the World Cup, but the 41-year-old is playing on after Jorge Jesus replaced Roberto Martinez as manager. Ronaldo has 146 goals in 233 appearances for his country and is approaching a personal landmark.

‌



The Al-Nassr striker sits on 979 career goals for club and country ahead of Portugal beginning their Nations League campaign against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night. While he has denied that his decision to continue playing for Portugal was driven by his own goal tally, Ronaldo did admit he'd like to reach four figures while on international duty.

‌



Portugal were dumped out of the World Cup by bitter rivals Spain in the last 16 and the 1-0 defeat did give Ronaldo pause for thought. Asked if he considered retiring, he replied: “Yes I did.

‌



"Of course, I’m always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also. I’m a thinker. You have to think. This is why you see me here now. It means I will continue.

“I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I’m not doing anything here.

“I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.”

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Jesus has taken over as Portugal boss (Image: Patricia de Melo Moreira / AFP via Getty Images)

The veteran forward now wants to help bring through the next generation. “I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired… in 10 years," he joked.

“I’m happy with myself. It doesn’t matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good.”

‌



Ronaldo's place in the starting XI has become a hot topic of debate in Portugal. He insists that it doesn't bother him. "I said it quite often at home with my friends. I’ve been playing football for so many years, I have been welcome almost everywhere, apart from a few exceptions," Ronaldo said.

“I feel the Portuguese fans like me, but I do understand that some TV channels want to criticise me – they’ve tried to kill me, but only with a shotgun.

“They are dying for me not to come to the national team anymore, but I can still move away from it. Anyway, I am used to it. For over 20 years I have been doing this, but my memories are with people who love me.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane opens up on true impact of England's World Cup heartbreak vs Argentina
Sports.content:
Harry Kane insists England must put the “hurt” of the last World Cup behind them. Kane admits the pain of losing to Argentina last summer was even worse for him personally than missing the penalty against France in the 2022 quarter final.

Three Lions captain Kane admitted they did not show their “true selves” against Argentina in the semi-final but says they must use that as motivation in the future.

England start their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday and Kane wants to start a new chapter after the pain in the United States.

Kane said: “You have no choice. You have to move on. I am so passionate about England, especially because I have been on this journey now. I have been to the finals, I have been to semi-finals and been so close.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Each one hurts in a different way. This one hurt, for sure. More than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened. It was not us as a team.

“It was not the team we wanted to be or said we would be. Sometimes you maybe go against your beliefs and it feels 10 times worse than losing your way when you accept it, take it on the chin and move on. It is tough and it will still be tough.

‌



“But leading up to the next major tournament for example, they are feelings that if you use them in the right way, you can use them to motivate you and you can say ‘I can go one step further’. And that is what we need to try and do.”

The disappointment comes from England having it within their grasp. They were 1-0 up against Argentina, they were on top and yet let it slip in the dying minutes against an ageing team which was not as good as when they won it coup years previously.

But Kane also explained the questions in their minds about where they went wrong and also how they can improve in the longer term.

Kane said: “I think those are the questions that we need to kind of discuss amongst ourselves and answer ourselves, as players and as coaching staff ‘how how can we be better in those moments? How can we be ourselves more in those moments?’

‌



View 4 Images Kane consoles Jude Bellingham after England's defeat to Argentina (Image: Getty Images)

“It's something that we haven't quite been able to do in latter stages of tournaments against the bigger nations and the better nations.

“And it may be a mixture of things - it may be personalities. It may be mentality. It may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games. I think it's conversations that we need to have as as a group and team.”

Incredibly, England will have played the last three world champions in their last three games by the time they finish Saturday’s showdown with Spain.

‌



They lost to Argentina, they beat France in the third place play-off and then face Spain. It is a big test for Thomas Tuchel’s men and Kane says it will also act as part of the “healing process.”

Kane said: “It kind of is. But you have to heal while getting on with it. In life in general, whenever there's like big major events in business or in sport, you have time to process it, you have time to talk about it.

View 4 Images Kane is now back in the England camp for the first time since the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

“In football, you don't have that. In football, before you know it's the next one, and now we're focused on Nations League, so it's a hard balance because you're trying to get over it and learn from it, but also we play the world champions on Saturday and it's a big, important game.”

‌



England boss Tuchel welcomed the group back to St George’s Park with a team meeting, every member of staff was also welcomed into the room with a clear message that they cannot let the disappointment of the way the summer ended distract from their progress.

Kane added: “The general messaging is that we continue what we've been building. I think sometimes after a tournament, it's easy to say we start fresh or it's a new start, but I don't think it is that.

“I think it's a continuation, he’s been here for two years. A lot of the squad have been together and at the World Cup, so let's continue what we've done because we have done a lot of good things.

“It’s easier said than done, but if we can get better at that I think we'll show an even better version of ourselves. So that was kind of the general meeting really. We're still going to talk about the summer and talk about good and bad. That will happen naturally over the next year.”

‌



Heartbroken Kane could not bear to watch the World Cup final - even though he was in the same city. He flew from Miami after the third place play-off straight to New York to see his family, play golf and relax after the campaign.

But Kane admitted he did not watch Spain defeat Argentina and made himself busy by hitting the golf course before going on a family holiday.

View 4 Images Kane was left heartbroken after England's defeat to Spain (Image: Getty Images)

Kane said: “I didn’t watch it. Funnily enough, I was in New York playing golf, I flew straight to New York straight after the third and fourth play-off, spent a couple of days there, would like to say hiding in New York but New York was the busiest place in the world at that point.

‌



“But to be honest, I have got some friends there, I was out and about and whether it was on the golf course or restaurants, the support and the amount of people that came up to me and said how proud they were of England and me and the team.

“Those are the moments that you start to appreciate everything you have been through. And a lot of Americans as well, the amount of impact it had in America and with their sports as well, although I wasn’t in New York for the reason I wanted to be in New York.

“It was a nice eye-opener of there is stuff to be proud of and you have got to hold your head up high and move on, it was quite a nice couple of days just switching off.”

Kane said the best medicine after the World Cup heartbreak was just enjoying some much-needed family time.

‌



He added: “The first time I saw them, they were so excited to see me. It does bring you straight back to that world. I am playing football with my son out on the grass, going out on the trampolines with my daughters, back to being a dad.

“Sometimes it is hard to make that switch but whoever is in the room who is a dad knows it happens naturally. They are the most important things to get back to enjoying that life.”

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim's final sack pay-out revealed - and why Man Utd saved huge sum
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim's final sack pay-out revealed - and why Man Utd saved huge sum

Manchester United have confirmed their financial results for the 2025/26 campaign with those numbers having included the millions that they were forced to pay Ruben Amorim

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim is now with AC Milan (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United were forced to fork out over £8million to sack Ruben Amorim - but still managed to save millions. The Portuguese coach left Old Trafford in January this year following a disappointing 14-month spell with the club.

‌



The Red Devils endured their worst-ever Premier League season with Amorim at the helm, finishing 15th in the 2024/25 campaign, while they also lost in the Europa League final. Amorim only lasted until January the following year and left with United following a draw with Leeds.

‌



It was suggested that his deteriorating relationship with the United hierarchy led to his eventual exit. He still had 18 months remaining on his deal.

‌



United’s accounts have now confirmed how much they had to pay to cut that deal short. United have confirmed their exceptional items for the year were £8.2m, which is made up by the severance package that they agreed with their former boss, as well as his coaches Carlos Fernandes, Adelio Candido, Emanuel Ferro and Jorge Vital.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Despite that eye-watering amount, United have not actually been hit with as severe a bill as first expected. Amorim’s initial severance package was around £16.7m but that would be significantly reduced should he find a new job.

He was eventually appointed by AC Milan in the summer and has the Italian giants sitting fifth in Serie A. Amorim has recently promised that he would not be making the same mistakes that he made at Old Trafford with his new employers.

“A great victory,” Amorim said after last weekend’s win against Lecce. “I liked the movement, especially the attacking depth. We managed the game and read the opponent well.

‌



“These are different times, but we're improving. Today the players had more freedom; in recent games we were a bit too static, stuck.

View 2 Images Amorim was sacked after a miserable 14-month spell with Man United (Image: Getty Images)

“I can't repeat my mistakes from Manchester. If we don't have the characteristics to play a certain way, we have to adapt.

‌



“We'll go back to building with three, but we'll see. Here in Italy, the coaches are very good, especially at going after other teams one-on-one.”

Speaking previously, he said that not even the Pope would have been able to change his mind on his coaching philosophy.

When it comes to United, they appointed former midfielder Michael Carrick as Amorim’s replacement on an interim basis. He led the club back into the Champions League during his first season at the helm, albeit his first full campaign has been slightly trickier, with the Red Devils sitting 12th after just one win from their opening five games.

Sports.title: Eric Cantona teams up with Gary Lineker as Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe slammed again
Sports.content:
Eric Cantona teams up with Gary Lineker as Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe slammed again

Gary Lineker and Eric Cantona have both slammed Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe over recent days, following his latest comments bemoaning immigration

View 2 Images Eric Cantona and Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politics do not align (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Eric Cantona has joined Gary Lineker in calling out Sir Jim Ratcliffe after the Manchester United co-owner said: "Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem". The four-time Premier League winner even claims he would not have moved to Old Trafford from Leeds United in 1992 had Ratcliffe been a minority shareholder at the time.

Cantona, 60, is the INEOS founder's favourite player. Ratcliffe, 73, even named the company he established to acquire a 25% stake in United, Trawlers Limited.

It is a reference to Cantona's famous quote: "When the seagulls follow the trawler, it's because they think sardines will be thrown into the sea."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

However, the admiration is very much one-sided due to their differing politics. After being asked by well-known United fan Pete Boyle in a video shared on TikTok whether he would have been willing to sign for a club part-owned by Ratcliffe, Cantona said: "No."

After being encouraged to expand on his blunt response to the hypothetical question posed, the interviewee went on to add: "Of course not.

"You know what I think about all of this, with this kind of politics. I cannot understand how someone like this can say something like that when he's one of the club's owners."

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe is not popular with his favourite player Eric Cantona (Image: Bo Amstrup/EPA/Shutterstock)

Cantona continued: "Football is a very popular sport. Football is made - all the greatest players come from different waves of immigration. Everywhere, in France, in England, everywhere.

"In France, for instance, the greatest players all come from different waves of immigration. I made a documentary on that, French Football: An Immigrant History.

"Raymond Kopa, in the fifties, was the son of Polish immigrants who came to France, worked in France, and worked hard in France. And then the Italians, Italians like Platini. And then the Spanish, like me, my mother came from Spanish refugees. I cannot accept this kind of thing."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Latest news and analysis via the MEN’s Manchester United Facebook page

These comments come days after Lineker branded Ratcliffe a 'not particularly pleasant human being' who is 'even worse than the Glazers'.

He said on The Rest is Football podcast : "I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe.

"He's clearly... I don't think he's a particularly pleasant human being, and it's a bit of a shambles of a football club the way it's being run at the moment. So, well done to the Glazers on that one, deflecting everything away from them!"

Sports.title: Arsenal discover penalty error as Premier League panel unanimously agree
Sports.content:
Arsenal discover penalty error as Premier League panel unanimously agree

Arsenal beat Sunderland in the Premier League earlier this month but were on the receiving end of a controversial penalty decision

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta was furious after the penalty was awarded against Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Premier League's Key Match Incidents panel has ruled it was an incorrect on-pitch decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal earlier this month. The Gunners secured all three points against the Black Cats with a 2-0 victory at the Stadium of Light, with plenty of controversy during the game.

‌



Sunderland were awarded a penalty after Ezri Konsa was judged to have fouled Dan Ballard during a corner, with referee John Brooks pointing to the spot and the decision was checked and upheld by VAR. Enzo Le Fee went on to miss the penalty, with David Raya saving the spot-kick, and Arsenal opened the scoring a few minutes later with a long-range effort from Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



Mikel Arteta was furious with the decision, despite Sunderland missing the penalty, and it has now been the subject of a review from the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel. The panel agreed 5:0 in favour of the wrong decision being made to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal.

‌



However, there was a 3:2 split in favour of there not being enough evidence that supported VAR intervening to overrule the original decision made by the referee. The independent panel is made up of three former players or coaches, one representative from the Premier League, and one from Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees).

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



A statement on the decision read: “The panel unanimously felt that the referee's call of a penalty for a holding offence was incorrect. Although it was a very untidy challenge in which Konsa initially had arms around Ballard, Ballard engages in a holding action, which pulls Konsa onto him, so they both fall to the floor.

“The non-VAR intervention was supported, 3:2, with the majority considering that the on-field decision was not a clear and obvious error, given the combined actions from both players.”

Arsenal’s second goal against Sunderland came from the penalty spot with a strike from Bukayo Saka, who was fouled by Reinildo in stoppage time.

‌



“The on-field award of a penalty was supported with an initial holding action by Reinildo followed by a genuine attempt to challenge for the ball - tripping Saka inside the penalty area,” the statement read.

View 2 Images Sunderland were awarded a penalty in controversial circumstances (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta expressed his anger about the decision to award Sunderland a penalty at the Stadium of Light, with the Arsenal boss labelling the decision as “unbelievable”.

‌



“Look, the first question that we have to discuss is, and this is not acceptable at this level, because it was a beautiful game of football, with two teams, with an atmosphere in this stadium, it was unbelievable,” Arteta told reporters after the game.

“With Sunderland they are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players, they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that, because it was a lot in a really difficult week, after Chelsea and Napoli.

“And on top of that, we have to go through what we've done today, that in my opinion is not acceptable. And I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how we even think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don't know what to think, really.”

Sports.title: Six Arsenal stars set for extra training with Mikel Arteta during international break
Sports.content:
Six Arsenal stars set for extra training with Mikel Arteta during international break

Mikel Arteta is set to be without an array of his Arsenal stars, with the international break having brought Premier League action to a halt but the Gunners’ boss is still keen to get out on the training pitch

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is set to get back on the training pitch (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta will be putting Arsenal’s non-internationals to work over the next few weeks as he aims to make the most of the enforced break.

‌



Premier League action has been brought to a pause due to the first international break of the campaign. And it might have come at the best possible time for Mikel Arteta and his staff following the 3-0 defeat to Brighton in their most recent outing.

‌



In an ideal world, Arteta would have all of his players available to find out exactly what went wrong at the Amex. Unfortunately, a whole array of stars have flown away to all corners of the globe after getting call-ups from their national teams.

‌



But that does not mean that Arteta will not be on the training pitch over the coming weeks. Ben White is set to remain with Arsenal for the international break after an intriguing turn of events.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He was not originally called into the England squad, albeit Thomas Tuchel did confirm that he wanted to work with the defender. White was then forced out through injury and will now rest but could potentially train under Arteta.

Fellow defender Piero Hincapie has also been nursing a small groin issue and has been left out of the Ecuador squad as a consequence. After being named on the bench against Brighton, he could complete an individual training plan over the coming weeks.

Arteta could also have a couple of goalkeepers to call upon throughout the international break. Illan Meslier is set to be available, while Kepa has not been called up by Spain - albeit he was spotted leaving the Amex alongside David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi so could opt for a return to his homeland over the break.

‌



The final player who Arteta could look to work with is Noni Madueke. Despite having gone to the World Cup, the wideman was not selected for Tuchel in his latest camp so will be aiming to sharpen up over the coming weeks.

View 2 Images Ben White and Noni Madueke are set to stay in North London (Image: Getty Images)

There is a question mark over the availability of Kai Havertz. The forward was named in Jurgen Klopp’s first Germany squad but the ex-Liverpool boss has been somewhat unconventional and named two separate selections.

‌



Havertz is one of those who will drop out for the second round of fixtures, albeit it remains to be seen whether he opts to return to North London or not. If he does, Havertz would be another first-team star available for training.

Speaking about the international break before the defeat at Brighton, Mikel Arteta said: “Let's see, it's something that we'll have to experience. As you've seen, different national teams, different managers have taken different approaches in terms of the numbers that they have put in the squad.

“So it's going to be really important to have good communication with them so they understand where our players are, what we expect, what they expect as well. And work together, that's the best way always.”

Sports.title: Man Utd announce record revenues but debt rises as Old Trafford grass goes on sale for £125!
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce record revenues but debt rises as Old Trafford grass goes on sale for £125!

Manchester United have announced their fourth quarter and full year fiscal 2026 results with the Reds recording record revenues after Sir Jim Ratcliffe's cost-cutting measures

View 3 Images Manchester United have announced their latest financial results (Image: Bo Amstrup/EPA/Shutterstock)

Manchester United recorded record revenues in their latest financial results. United say that the club continue to benefit from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's operating cost and headcount reductions, alongside the improved third-place Premier League finish during the 2025/26 season.

‌



Despite recording a full year operating profit of £22.6million, United once again posted an overall loss for the year of £43m, compared to £33m the year before.

‌



United's revenue, however, rose by 1.7 per cent compared to 2024/25, which the club believe shows they are on the right track given they had no European football and no training kit sponsor in place. In total, United posted record revenues of £677.6m, up from £666.5m in the previous full year.

‌



The club feel that more "financial discipline" is needed to stabilise the business after they recorded a loss. United have said that the sacking of Ruben Amorim earlier this year contributed to losses. However, the latest results reveal that the departure of Amorim and his staff cost just £8.2m, which is significantly less than the £36.6m United forked out after firing staff, including his predecessor Erik ten Hag, last season.

Roy Keane points finger after JJ Gabriel quit bombshell with reminder about Man United starlet READ MORE :

Debt levels at United, meanwhile, are also still rising, though it is part down to the change in interest rates and the refinancing of some bonds in June of this year.

United believe "non-current borrowings" now stand at £577.6m, up from £471.9m last year. The Reds also have a revolving credit facility, which is similar to a credit card, and that stood at £100m at the end of June 2026.

‌



Meanwhile, United's matchday income dropped by £6.8m, which is no surprise given the Reds had 10 fewer games at Old Trafford last season, due to no European football and being knocked out of the FA Cup and Carabao Cup at the first hurdle.

Once more, United's wage bill fell, down to £302m, and United said that was "primarily due to changes in the make-up of the men’s first team squad, combined with savings associated with headcount reduction programs implemented over the previous two fiscal years."

View 3 Images Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada revelaed record revenues (Image: Getty)

‌



United Chief Executive Officer Omar Berrada said: "We are pleased to have secured record revenues and adjusted EBITDA which demonstrates the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football. This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years.

"It also proves Manchester United's enduring popularity and commercial strength. While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.

"With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men’s and women’s teams during the summer window and our men’s team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We have also strengthened commercially and have welcomed Betway as our new Training Kit partner and SumUp as our new Sleeve partner; two excellent organisations which we are delighted to be working with, alongside our kit supplier, adidas and front of shirt partner, Snapdragon.

"Our other main area of focus is our plan to develop a new 100,000-seater stadium. We have now completed the major milestone of securing the land which will form part of the proposed location of the new stadium."

‌



Alongside this, United laid a new pitch at Old Trafford for the first time in 14 years in the summer, and the old surface has been cut into 7cm x 7cm squares. Those have been put in acrylic cubes and sent out to supporters who want them in a smart black casing for £125 each.

View 3 Images Manchester United are selling chunks of the Old Trafford grass (Image: UtdDistrict/X)

"Take home a piece of Old Trafford with this official turf cube, perfect for fans who want a keepsake from one of the most famous pitches in the world. Carefully preserved, this piece of turf makes a priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of match days alive.

‌



"Perfect for gifting to passionate Reds, this turf cube makes a great addition to desks or can be displayed in a cabinet with other Manchester United collectables."

United believe the purchasable turf is a 'one-in-a-lifetime' item for fans, with club members and season ticket holders offered access before others in an email.

The Red Devils have made a disappointing start to the 2026/27 season. They have won just one of their opening five Premier League matches, drawing two and losing two. United made a winning start to life back in the Champions League by thrashing Sabah 4-0 but they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Sports.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
Sports.content:
Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.

Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonny Clayton ended Luke Littler's clean sweep at the World Series of Darts Finals. Credit: @OfficialPDC.

"It's a real difficult situation," Smith said. "I can't speak for Luke because I'm not him and I wasn't in his position, I wasn't on stage at the time. I didn't really experience the whistling too much. I try not to rise to it because I know you're just going to get more stick.

"My manager once said to me, if you look at Michael van Gerwen, he never reacts, not once will he ever react to the crowd. He'll always thank them and he never really gets too much stick and he's very professional about how he does things. So, I admire him for that and I try and learn off of other people.

"I had a bit with Kevin Doets, obviously the crowd, rightly so, they're cheering their local guy on. Same with Gian [van Veen], they're doing exactly the same, but I think if you're aggressive towards the crowd and you're letting them know that it's affecting you and you're making them unhappy, it's not a good thing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Ross Smith feels he is ready to play in the Premier League.

"I tried to, with Gian, I had more banter with them, you know what I mean? Just like thumbs up to them, but smiling, not in an aggressive way and they sort of laugh with you, it's not a problem.

"I think it's how you can react on stage, if you're aggressive towards them, it's going to create problems for you. But like I said, I can't really comment on Luke because I wasn't playing in the games with Luke and I don't know what he actually went through, but they can be brutal at times."

Nicholson: Maybe Littler can learn from others

Former world championship quarter-finalist Paul Nicholson praised Smith's approach, and suggested that Littler could benefit from learning from some of his rivals.

Nicholson, who himself was known for often having fractious interactions with crowds, also pointed to the way 2021 world champion Gerwyn Price has adapted his behaviour on stage.

Following on from Smith's comments, Nicholson said: "That's a really, really good way of looking at it, what Ross has just said, because from my standpoint, I tried to be aggressive because I wanted to be different and it was something that I had my entire career for, more than 10 years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Paul Nicholson has backed Luke Littler's reduced schedule for the rest of the season.

"Gerwyn Price has taken years to figure it out. Now he gives the smile with the aggression, and the crowd are with him more than they ever have been.

"So, it just goes to show that Ross is looking at this right, in order to make sure that his career is in the right place moving forward.

"So, we learn from mistakes, but we actually learn from what other people are going through as well. We don't want to see Littler not going to events, but maybe he can learn from what other people are doing as well."

What could the rest of Littler's year look like? World Grand Prix* (Leicester) Sept 28-Oct 4 European Championship* (Dortmund) October 22-25 Players Championship 31 (Den Bosch) October 28 Players Championship 32 (Den Bosch) October 29 Players Championship 33 (Leicester) November 4 Players Championship 34 (Leicester) November 5 Grand Slam of Darts* (Wolverhampton) November 14-22 Players Championship Finals* (Minehead) November 27-29 *denotes major

Why whistling is worse than booing for players

Nicholson also explained why Littler and other players may become particularly frustrated at being whistled.

He added: "We have seen Littler have some banter with the crowd, which we're all for by the way, because we want people to have that connection. One of the greatest things about this sport is that there is a connection between the fans and the stars.

"But what we have at the minute is a trend of people using whistling as a way to make themselves feel heard. Dart players don't like it because it's piercing. It gets in your ear and it happens in a very short, sharp way, and it comes from nowhere.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Webster and Michael Bridge discuss Luke Littler's concerns over crowd whistling at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam, the potential impact on his future and whether more can be done to tackle the issue.

"You don't know if it's going to come when you're throwing a match dart, a leg dart, or even going for a treble. If it comes out of nowhere, it can put you off and your shoulder jolts, and you don't want that.

"A boo is a lesser frequency and it's more mundane, you can handle them a lot better. But these short, sharp whistles, which is what they are, they're horrible.

"And the worst thing is, if it happens once, you are thinking about whether it's going to happen again, and you can't fully focus."

Sports.title: Sedlacek wins first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30
Sports.content:
Karel Sedlacek secured his first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30, beating Scott Williams 8-7 despite a late scare as he closed in on victory.

It was a thrilling encounter, with Sedlacek outlasting Williams' barrage of high scores, which included nine maximums, but both players struggled to close out the victory, with the Czech missing five match darts.

Sedlacek would ultimately claim victory, becoming the first Czech player to win a PDC tour title. But after mounting an epic comeback, winning two of the final three legs, Williams cut a furious figure after the match, shaking hands with his opponent and the officials before throwing his darts onto the ground.

Sedlacek would go 7-5 up before nerves set in, with the 47-year-old needing to check out on 24 to win, before missing a trio of match darts, allowing Williams to pull back a leg.

The momentum turned to Williams, who hit two 140s in the resulting leg, before he pulled the contest back to 7-7.

Image: Scott Williams almost staged an incredible comeback, pulling level at the end after going 7-5 down

In the deciding leg, it looked as though the Englishman was set to produce a remarkable comeback victory, hitting a maximum to leave himself 112 to win the match, but he too stumbled, hitting five on his second dart when a single 20 would have double 16.

Williams shook his head and exclaimed, 'you're kidding me', before hitting 15 with his final dart.

It left Sedlacek the chance to check out from 32, first missing double 16 inside, subsequently missing double eight, before he finally sealed the match.

Sedlacek, who hit a match-high checkout of 164 in the ninth leg, finished the final with a checkout success of 34.8 per cent, while Williams ended with 36.8 per cent.

Sports.title: Sky Sports to show England men's tour of South Africa this winter
Sports.content:
Sky Sports and Cricket South Africa have extended their longstanding partnership, with Sky Sports and NOW to exclusively broadcast the England men's three-Test and three-ODI tour of South Africa this winter.

England's three-Test series against South Africa will take place across December and January, marking England's first Test tour of South Africa in seven years.

The series follows England's first-ever home Test series whitewash of Pakistan and will be Stephen Fleming's first series in charge as England men's Test head coach.

The Test series will be followed by three ODIs in January, as England prepare for the ICC Men's World Cup 2027, which will take place across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia in October and November next year.

Sky Sports will broadcast live coverage of a packed schedule of international cricket from South Africa, with Australia men's tour getting under way this Thursday with the first of three ODIs in Durban, followed by three Tests.

The schedule will then continue with tours involving Bangladesh, India Women and Australia Women through to April.

Sky Sports has broadcast cricket from South Africa for more than three decades, including live coverage of every England men's Test series in the country during that period.

The agreement further strengthens Sky Sports' position as the home of cricket, broadcasting all home England men's and women's international and domestic cricket, with the men's Ashes on home soil next summer set to be a major highlight.

Sports.title: Ronaldo eyes scoring 1,000th goal for Portugal after considering international retirement
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring from international football after the World Cup before deciding to extend his Portugal career.

Ronaldo - who turns 42 in February - will win his 234th cap against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday, with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus confirming that the former Manchester United and Real Madrid will start the Nations League fixture.

Some commentators have suggested the game at the Jose Alvalade Stadium - the home of Ronaldo's first club Sporting - could be his international farewell, but the five-time Ballon d'Or winner said he will finish when "I feel like I'm not doing anything here".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Head coach Ange Postecoglou clashed with a journalist who accused Ronaldo of doing 'nothing' for Al Nassr in the last three matches that culminated in the 4-0 defeat against Al Ain in the AFC Champions League

Age seemed to have caught up with Ronaldo this summer during a World Cup when many of the game's greatest stars shone on its biggest stage, leading to speculation that his international career had run its course.

Asked if he considered leaving Portugal after the World Cup, Ronaldo said: "Yes I did. Of course, I'm always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also.

"I'm a thinker. You have to think. This is why you see me here now. It means I will continue.

"I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

"I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

"This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games."

Leading Portuguese newspaper A Bola ran a poll prior to the Wales game inviting readers to select their team, and Ronaldo failed to make the starting XI.

Ronaldo said: "I said it quite often at home with my friends. I've been playing football for so many years, I have been welcome almost everywhere, apart from a few exceptions.

"I feel the Portuguese fans like me, but I do understand that some TV channels want to criticise me.

"They are dying for me not to come to the national team anymore, but I can still move away from it.

"Anyway, I am used to it. For over 20 years I have been doing this, but my memories are with people who love me."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We look back at Ronaldo's most outrageous flicks and tricks from his spells in the Premier League with Manchester United

Ronaldo, playing for Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia, currently has 979 career goals.

He denied that he is obsessed with reaching 1,000 goals, although he did add he would love to reach the landmark in Portugal colours.

"Scoring my 1,000th goal for the national team would be the ‌culmination of something - a beautiful story," he said. "It wouldn't be the end of it, but it would be a beautiful story.

"I've already admitted that I want to get there, and I will get ‌there. An obsession? No. The rest is about enjoying it, enjoying every day.

"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired... in 10 years.

"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good."

Bellamy: Who gets 1,000 goals? It's just silly

Craig Bellamy believes Cristiano Ronaldo's name will be etched in football history for "hundreds and hundreds of years" as his Wales side prepare for Portugal in their Nations League opener.

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus has confirmed 41-year-old Ronaldo will start at the Jose Alvalade Stadium in Lisbon on Thursday night, winning his 234th cap and seeking to add to his 146 international goals.

"Seriously? Who gets a thousand goals? We're not counting youth football or anything," said Bellamy.

"It's just silly and I hope he gets it. But I hope he gets nothing against us.

"The type of impact on the game that he's been able to sustain, for him to still keep going, you just have to sit in awe. That's the honest truth, the guy is incredible.

"He's had to adapt his game of course, but he's at his most dangerous when he is not in the game. You've never been able to sleep on the pitch with this guy.

"We're talking about one of the greatest players of all generations, not just this generation, of all generations.

"His name will go down in history for hundreds and hundreds of years. That's the impact he's had."

Sports.title: Hamilton defends Ferrari amid ‘doom and gloom’ criticism
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari's season can still rank as a "huge achievement" if they finish in the top three of the Drivers' Championship, asking critics to "look at the positives" of the team's year despite recent setbacks.

Hamilton and Ferrari's hopes of winning this years world title have faded in recent races, with the Briton not finishing on the podium since the British Grand Prix at the start of July.

A first race retirement of the season last time out in Madrid saw third-placed Hamilton fall over 100 points back on championship-leading Kimi Antonelli for the first time this season, with the seven-time champion all-but conceding the title.

Antonelli's overall lead at the top of the standings is 81 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

Asked about his own championship prospects heading into weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the season's 15th of a scheduled 23 rounds, Hamilton said: "Well, I mean, he's 101 points ahead of me.

"Just in two races he gained something like 40-odd points on me, and we've been working so hard to gain just a couple of points here and there.

"There is still a long way to go and I think the focus for me is, if we can hold on to second - if not somehow catch Mercedes - for the constructors', I think that would be remarkable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

"I think it's also just having to think about where we were last year and where we've come to this year and whilst it sometimes seems doom and gloom, you actually have to look at the positives."

Ferrari endured a winless 2025 campaign and slipped to fourth in the Constructors' Championship, with Hamilton himself experiencing a difficult first campaign in red with no podiums for the first time in his career.

But he won for the first time at June's Spanish Grand Prix, with Charles Leclerc triumphing two races later at Silverstone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton celebrated his first Ferrari victory in style after winning the Barcelona-Catalunya GP, throwing his trophy into the air before the champagne spray began.

Hamilton added: "We've been fighting, we've had wins and podiums, the team have done an incredible job in terms of bringing upgrades, so you really have to acknowledge the good things that we've done this year.

"I know lots of people focus on the negatives. For me, again, if I can battle with George and somehow get ahead of him, which would be very difficult as Mercedes are the leaders... if at the end of the year, managing to stay in the top three, even second, I think would be a huge achievement for us as a team."

Hamilton is 20 points behind Russell, his former Mercedes team-mate, in the standings.

'I believe we can make improvements'

Ferrari have consistently looked competitive early on in race weekends but the team's recent results have often been compromised by operational and strategic issues within their own control.

"I think there's positives to take out of the last few races, it's just they haven't been, I would say, the best in terms of execution and we've not had the best results," said Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix.

"But the positives we take forwards and we try and learn from the areas we weren't as good. I believe we can make improvements and I think we have.

"I'm excited for this weekend."

Russell: I feel confident I can fight for victories again

The Spanish Grand Prix a fortnight ago also saw Russell fall a season-high margin behind Antonelli, who has won the last two grands prix to take his tally to eight overall in an extraordinary second campaign of F1 so far.

Russell, the pre-season title favourite, has spoken openly about his difficulties in meshing his natural driving style to the all-new 2026 cars but believes the situation is improving, saying in Baku on Wednesday that "I've been making very good progress and feel confident I can fight for victories again".

He underlined the importance of continuing that trend all through the rest of this season ahead relatively stable winter of regulations into 2027.

"I think it is very important to try and resolve some issues, which, as I mentioned before, I think I've been pleased with that progress since the summer break," said Russell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player F1 drivers share their opinions following the announcement that the Monaco Grand Prix will get a Sprint race next year.

"The race pace, which was a weakness, has been substantially better and has been in the mix every single race since the break.

"And I now feel more comfortable that I can fight for great results.

"Let's see from now until the end of the season how the points could fall out. But next year is going to be pretty similar. Not much has changed with the chassis, not much has changed with the power units. Maybe the tyres are going to be slightly different from what we hear. So, it's important I continue to build."

Although he has effectively ruled himself out of title contention, Russell says his approach to each race weekend will not change.

"I'm going to keep fighting every single race until it's mathematically impossible," he stressed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli says the team has all eyes on its long-awaited upgrade package arriving in Malaysia

"But it doesn't change how I go about my job. I want to try and win every single race and put it on pole every single race. That's my goal.

"That's what I'm working towards every single weekend, and what happens thereafter will be. And there's obviously a huge deficit, but it's not even really a consideration right now. It's just the performance is the biggest priority."

Sports.title: Pirotton vows to be 'matador' against 'money cow' Fisher
Sports.content:
Michael Pirotton is ready to shock Johnny Fisher when they fight at London’s Copper Box Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

The "Romford Bull" is hugely popular with an impassioned fan base, while his Belgian opponent is comparatively unknown.

But Pirotton is convinced he can use that element of surprise.

"I'm nobody in boxing," the Belgian told Sky Sports. "Nobody knows about me.

"That's my only advantage," he continued. "I know I'm supposed to lose.

"In the scenario I'm supposed to lose that fight. He's going to come full of confidence with his people and I know he's training hard. I have to be ready for whatever he brings. I'm going to be ready. I'm ready."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher looks ahead to his fight against Michael Pirotton and praise his support network that has carried him this far

Fisher is a strong, come-forward fighter. "He's really aggressive and I can move. It's a classic heavyweight match-up. A bull against a matador. Let's see who wins," Pirotton said. "The horns in my belly, or if he ends up on the barbecue.

"The pressure is on his shoulders," the Belgian added. "He's just the money cow. He didn't grab anything he had. I know whatever happens I've grabbed everything I have."

He maintains the struggles he's faced in his career will help him outlast Fisher.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Pirotton discusses why he feels more ready than ever to take on Johnny Fisher and discusses what he'll need to do to take the win

"They will find out. I don't brag before," Pirotton said. "But I'm confident. I don't brag before, I dance after, that's what I do.

"I'm glad for everything, that tough journey with some bad stuff happening to me. Because it enfused a deep sense of stoicism in me. What happens is going to happen and I'm still going to be Mike and I'm still going to be proud of what I do.

"I don't have a destination. I just have a path and I'm walking. I'm bleeding now but I keep walking and you're going to see."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher faces off with his opponent Michael Pirotton ahead of their heavyweight clash at the Copper Box on Saturday - live on Sky Sports

Pirotton, who's never been dropped or stopped in his career, does have a warning for Fisher.

"I'm not over and it's not over until I say it's over and Johnny … he's a tough guy, he's strong guy, he's a decent guy, but he can't knock me out," he said.

"I'm able to punch. But I've never been able to punch like I'm really able to punch. And now I feel free to unleash my power."

Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.
