Sports.title: Erling Haaland has caused surprise food boom in Norway
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's influence reached new heights during the World Cup - it has even caused a surge in carrot sales in Norway.

If the Manchester City talisman wasn't a superstar before, this summer catapulted him into a new stratosphere as his goalscoring exploits and unique personality made him a household name.

3 Haaland finished as the World Cup's third-top scorer on his tournament debut Credit: Getty

On the pitch, Haaland led Norway to a World Cup quarter-final, firing in seven goals in six games before being knocked out by England.

And his profile only grew away from it, with the goal machine's lifestyle - which includes meditation and his unfiltered social media activity - earning him a whole new fanbase.

Haaland was easily the most viral player of the competition, whose Instagram following grew from 40million to 60million during it.

Haaland inspires Norway again

The 'Haaland effect' is showing no signs of slowing down in Norway, with reports that he is now inspiring a boom in carrot consumption.

According to reports, carrot sales have increased by 25 per cent in the Scandinavian nation in recent weeks, and isn't hard to trace the root cause.

The vegetables are a known favourite of Haaland's, who has previously been spotted snacking on them while signing autographs and he recently starred in a commercial promoting them.

During the World Cup, he featured on every Norwegian television channel in an advert for vegetable wholesaler Bama - a vegetable wholesaler, where he drives a truck and eats carrots.

Norwegian Nutrition Advisor Iselin Sagen told talkSPORT on the carrot boom: "The sales went up in July. We have never seen this record in July before.

"Also the sales were very good in August. And we know that there were two things going on at the same time in July.

"We had a big campaign with Haaland running before every match. He drives the trucks, eats the carrots and asks for more carrots.

3 Haaland has continued his goalscoring form into the new season, scoring five goals in his first five Premier League outings Credit: Getty

"And the supermarket also had bunched carrots on offer all summer.

"So, I cannot prove that it was him. But he is a huge role model in Norway and he was right in the middle of it."

This isn't the first time the 26-year-old's diet has caught the eye, having previously stunned fans by revealing he consumes 6,000 calories per day - which includes heart, liver and a cheat meal of kebab pizza.

But Sagen revealed Haaland's background, having grown up in the small farming town of Bryne, has likely led to his love of carrots too.

She said: "I really do think that Erling Haaland loves Norwegian vegetables.

"He grew up in a district where there are many farmers in Bryne, a small place in Rogaland district."

3 Haaland was inspirational for Norway at the World Cup, and he is a huge influence off the pitch too Credit: Getty

While the vegetables are in fact a staple in Norway, Sagen had little doubt that Haaland was behind their recent popularity, who is known to prefer bunched carrots with greens still attached.

The nutritionist continued: “We eat a lot of carrots in Norway. That's one of the most eaten vegetables in Norway.

"But we did know that bunched carrots with the grass on - that was having a low sale before this campaign, and this year.

"We were thinking about what's happening with the bunched carrots, [that] we should sell more.

"But when you ask how much is it [the increase], it's around 600 tonnes more carrots sold in July 2026 compared to 2025. And that's around one or two carrots more per person - we have five and a half million people in Norway."

Sports.title: Damning Kyle Walker verdict after being dropped by Burnley for last Championship game
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker has been a massive part of Burnley's terrible start to the season and deserved to be dropped for their last game.

This is the view of Joe Redmond from the Turfcast Podcast, who backed the decision not to play the club captain during their 1-1 draw at home to Burnley last weekend.

3 Walker is Burnley's club captain due to his vast experience Credit: Getty

The former England international is into his second season as a Burnley player with the Clarets sitting bottom of the Championship.

Burnley started the season as one of the favourites for promotion, but after eight games, they are the only team in the division without a win.

The Clarets have drawn four and lost four, including conceding a late equaliser at the weekend at home to the Rams.

It leaves them three points off safety and nine points off the final play-off place, which is eighth this year.

Walker has been playing as a centre-back for the majority of the season but after the 3-1 defeat at Swansea in September, he was dropped and didn't make it off the bench for the second time in the league this year.

On Burnley boss Nicky Hayden's decision to exclude Walker, Redmond told talkSPORT's EFL All Access podcast: ""No, "I think it was the correct decision to drop him personally.

"I do think he's been poor this season. He should be able to have a great influence on the squad, he has won literally everything that there is to win in club football.

"You cannot have a career better than Kyle Walker's, really. He has done everything. And obviously you've got to respect what he's achieved in the game and things like that. But ultimately, he has been a massive part of the problem.

"I do think some of it as well. I do feel sorry for Kyle as well in a certain aspect because he's been played out of position. Against Swansea, for example, we have three right-backs on the pitch. Obviously, Connor Roberts was at left back.

"Kyle Walker was at centre back. And Oliver Sonne was at right back. So I don't think it is just down to Kyle's poor performances, but I do think he has played poorly. I think it was the right decision to drop him against Derby.

3 Hayen is under increasing pressure and had declared the Derby match a must-win Credit: Getty

"And of course, the goalkeeper as well, Max Weiss, who had an absolute howler against Swansea and has done for the majority of the season. But Kyle has been poor. And if he hears this, I know that he would admit that as well. He would say that he has not been up to the standards that he would set himself.

"I did think it was a little surprising in the sense that he did a lot of media in the week leading up to it. He met up with the fan advisory board, he met up with some staff.

"He did loads of interviews with the rights holders saying, 'Yeah, we need to be better. We need to improve. We need to man up' is a term that he used just for him to be dropped. So that element of it was a little bit surprising.

"But I think what I said on my channel is when you look at the performances through the course of the season, has Kyle done enough to deserve to start against Derby County? For me, it is a no."

Clarets under pressure

Hayen has already admitted that he isn't sure he'll keep his job for too much longer.

When asked if he feared for his role following the draw to Derby, he said: "I understand the frustration of the fans; I understand that they're really disappointed – also, in myself, that they're fuming. I completely understand and I know how it goes in football, but... I'm honest and I tell the truth and I'm not hiding behind it.

3 Burnley's bad start to the season has been characterised by lots of poor defensive errors Credit: Getty

"There are a lot of reasons [for Burnley's poor start to the season] and you take this into account or you don't, and that's up to other people to decide...

"If we have 11 players, everyone thinks they're fit and they're fresh and they go for [it] 100 per cent, but the reality sometimes is different and you only know when you are on the inside.

"But I know I cannot claim a lot at the moment. I know that I'm responsible for it and if they [the club] make the decision that it's not good enough, then we'll see.

"But... I'm resilient; I was always a fighter. I will keep on fighting and... I'm 100 per cent sure that we can turn it around with these [next] three weeks, but we'll see what happens."

Burnley now have three weeks until they are back in action when they play Watford, who are also struggling.

And Hayen plans to take the Clarets away to a warm-weather training camp despite having eight players on international duty.

“So we will have a few days off for the players, where they really can switch off for football, leave the negativity behind and come back with fresh energy.

“We also have a running programme, because for us it's like a new pre-season, even if it's three weeks, but it will be important.

“So it's like you start with the running sessions, then we go on a camp, and then we have the preparation towards Watford.

“I can say again it's a must-win game, but this will be a week and a game where we want to show a really new face and a totally different one than now.”

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha reveals how Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has given him new tools to destroy defenders
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha reveals how Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has given him new tools to destroy defenders

Rio Ngumoha has his sights set on starring at Euro 2028, and Andoni Iraola’s influence could be key to this.

After a breakthrough 2025/26 season which culminated in a senior England debut, the Liverpool starlet's impressive start to this campaign has now earned him another international call-up.



5 Ngumoha is the youngest player in the England squad for their Autumn internationals Credit: Getty

Ngumoha was named in Thomas Tuchel's 27-man squad for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League fixtures.

It represents a chance for the 18-year-old to make his competitive debut, having made his senior bow in a friendly win over New Zealand in June.

This followed Ngumoha's inclusion in England's pre-World Cup training camp, despite not featuring in their 26-man squad going to the tournament.



And after being earmarked as a star for the future with an impressive international debut, the teenager is now looking to stake his claim for a starting berth over the three weeks.

Ngumoha: I'm here to compete

Following his latest England inclusion, Ngumoha sat down with talkSPORT to discuss his goals for the international break.



With this his first involvement in a Three Lions squad, having previously been a training player for the pre-World Cup camp, the youngster revealed news of his call-up sparked huge celebrations in his family.

He told talkSPORT: "My mum was next to my brother - so I just called them and then they just started screaming down my phone.



“So it was an amazing moment."

But Ngumoha isn't just there to make up the numbers, as he insisted he is targeting a key role for England which will see him battle the likes of Marcus Rashford, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers for a starting berth on the left wing.

The Liverpool winger continued: “I've just got to come here and show what I can do to everyone and just make sure everyone just understands who I am.

5 Ngumoha looked a real livewire on his England debut against New Zealand in June Credit: Getty

"I'm not here just to be like a side part - I want to be a mainstay in the team and hopefully I can stay.



“But there's good competition everywhere. So it's about competing with the best players in the world now."

Euro 2028 dream

With his immediate goal breaking into Tuchel's starting XI ahead of some huge names, Ngumoha's long-term aim is ambitious too.

The prospect of a home European Championships in 2028 is sure to provide extra motivation for all English players, and not least Ngumoha, who will be almost 20 when it comes around.

Asked about the possibility of a home Euros, he admitted: “I'd definitely like to be a part of the squad.



“I think if I just keep doing what I'm doing, whether it's with the national team or at club level, if I just keep showing who I am and how I play and keep getting goals and assists and helping the team win trophies, then definitely I'd like to be a part of the team and hopefully we can go all the way as well.”

5 Ngumoha has continued to excite with his dribbling ability and direct style Credit: Getty

Iraola influence

Ngumoha's latest England call-up comes after after his continued involvement for Liverpool under new head coach Andoni Iraola.

The exciting winger burst onto the scene after being handed his big break by former boss Arne Slot, making 29 appearances last term and scoring twice in the Premier League.



He has remained a regular fixture since Iraola's arrival, featuring five times in all competitions this term, starting on three occasions.

And Ngumoha revealed the Spaniard's influence has helped him add a new string to his bow by playing him on the right wing, as well as his favoured left side.

Discussing life under the Spaniard, he told talkSPORT: “It's been good.

"The gaffer at Liverpool has really been helpful. And all the coaching staff as well - I can't speak highly enough of them.



5 Andoni Iraola heads into the international break still unbeaten as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

“But I'm enjoying it. I'm playing left-wing, right wing as well. So it's given me another tool to destroy defenders."

Tuchel earns Ngumoha praise

Having handed Ngumoha his senior England debut at just 17 in the summer, Thomas Tuchel has made no secret that he is a huge fan.

After calling up the youngster for the September internationals, Tuchel shared his first impressions of him, as he said: “Rio was very impressive at this kind of age. He was explosive, he was adventurous, he was strong and one-on-ones like a true winger.



He added: “We are very excited about his potential and about his natural courage and adventurous style of play."

And Ngumoha was equally complimentary of the England boss, saying: “I don't even know what to say about the manager, Thomas.

“He's really helpful. And I think him picking me shows his belief in me, and how exciting and 'explosive' he thinks I am.

5 Thomas Tuchel could well see Ngumoha add to his one and only England cap in the coming weeks Credit: Getty



“All I can do now is just show him again why I should be here for the many more camps and why he thinks I should be a big part of the team and help the team."

Ngumoha could make his first England start when they face Spain at Wembley in the Nations League on Saturday night, live on talkSPORT, kick-off 7:45pm.

England face Czechia on two occasions during this international break and also take on Croatia with these matches also live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Manager’s mic drop moment could see Premier League club return to Europe for first time in eight years
Sports.content:
Manager’s mic drop moment could see Premier League club return to Europe for first time in eight years

Everton have been predicted to finish in a European position despite only having 18 outfield squad players.

David Moyes' side are only one of fives to remain unbeaten in the Premier League since the beginning of the season.

3 Moyes has led the Toffees to an unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign, so far Credit: Getty

The Toffees have had two wins and three draws from their first month of the campaign.

However, Evertonians will not be getting their hopes up following the anti-climax and downfall of recent years.

Everton were sat three points off a Champions League place but the season ended painfully as they went on to not win any of their final seven games.

Everton finished 13th, four points behind Brighton, who qualified for the Conference League, and five off Sunderland, who joined Bournemouth and Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

On the 'No BS' podcast, Max Scott said: "I'm giving Everton an A grade and I'm giving the board a D. Moyes is an A for what went well, but it would be even better if the board got their act together.

"That's the reality. What I love about Everton so far this season is that it is a case in point as to why David Moyes is still a top-tier manager.

"I don't care that some Evertonians don't quite like him or West Ham fans, I don't care what they think about his brand of football."

Everton's strong start, which also include two Carabao Cup victories, had been based on a solid defence.

Moyes' side have kept five clean sheets in seven matches overall and got the three points in their last match Ipswich with a 1-0 win.

Fury at board from Toffees fans

Despite a great start, Evertonians are experiencing a deep frustration against their owners, The Friedkin Group.

3 Everton fans have been hesitant on whether Moyes can help the team progress Credit: AFP

The Toffees released a portrait image of their squad for the season and it featured only 18 outfield players alongside only three goalkeepers, sparking concerns they'll lack resources as the season progresses.

Fans and the Everton Fans' Forum slammed the club’s recruitment after TFG pocketed over £100 million on deadline day.

They sold star player Iliman Ndiaye, top scorer Beto, Tim Iroegbunam, and Nathan Patterson, while a deal for Folarin Balogun collapsed.

Additionally, owner Dan Friedkin has faced fierce criticism for never attending a match or visiting Liverpool since completing the takeover in December 2024.

To make matters worse, the hierarchy had to call off a proposed £40million deal to sell midfielder and academy ace Harrison Armstrong following a backlash from the club's fans.

Supporters sang Armstrong's name throughout a draw at Bournemouth in August and said there would be a 'riot' if their brightest prospect was sold.

3 Armstrong has made five appearances and has one assist to his name this season Credit: Getty

Everton tipped for Europe despite setbacks

Scott added: "They are unbeaten in a Premier League, which so far has been uber competitive, with only a squad of 18 players.

"With the disappointment of the transfer window, with the whole Harrison Armstrong debacle, Moyes picked Armstrong, essentially put up two fingers to the board and then revved up the fans who started singing and they kept him at the football club.

"This is why you should never sleep on David Moyes. Never underestimate him. And I said at the start of the season, my prediction was that they'd get some form of European football.

"And despite all of the odds and all of the bad decisions from the club, they're on for that. I mean, I'm looking at the table now, they're seventh.

"They're ahead of Chelsea and all the multi-millions they've spent, ahead of United, ahead of Tottenham. I mean, I think they're a great example of if you've got the right manager, then you will go places."

Olly Clink responded: "Yeah, well-organized, hardworking, battle-hardened...

"And you mentioned that game against Bournemouth where he picked Harrison Armstrong. And it was after that game in the post-match press conference where he says, 'the fans know they've got an Evertonian as the manager.'

Scott added: "Yeah, it's like a mic drop moment."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says he’s happy to sit on the bench as he makes retirement admission
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo says he’s happy to sit on the bench as he makes retirement admission

Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted that he considered stepping away from international football after the World Cup.

The Portuguese superstar endured yet more World Cup heartbreak in the summer as his nation were dumped out by Spain.



3 The World Cup has remained out of reach for Ronaldo Credit: Getty

Ronaldo led the line throughout, but they were no match for eventual champions La Roja, who saw them off in the round of 16.

Mikel Merino scored the only goal of the game, and Roberto Martinez departed.

Martinez had already announced that he wouldn't be staying on as manager of the Portuguese national team, but it was another failure for Ronaldo and co.



But new gaffer Jorge Jesus has called up the 41-year-old for this extended international break.

Portugal are in action four times over the three weeks, starting off against Wales in the Nations League.



And ahead of that contest at the Estadio Jose Alvalade, Ronaldo was asked if he'd considered calling it a day.

His response was very honest as he said: "Yes. I considered stepping away. I am always thinking about my future. I'm a thinker. This is why you see me here.



"I had a conversation with our president and our coach. I believe I can still help the national team reach to where they want. Also outside of football. This is a new generation, a young generation."

He added: "The critics will always be there... the most important thing is I know who I am. I know why the young kids especially love Ronaldo.

"I will continue to do that. I will continue to do that when I retire in ten years... I'm a happy person".

3 Ronaldo's legacy with the national team won't ever be surpassed but some feel he should call it a day



He also made it clear that he'll do whatever Jesus requires of him, even if it means he's not on the pitch.

Ronaldo said: “Whatever the coach needs from me with the national team, whether that means playing, coming off, coming on, coming off again, or even not playing at all... I am available.

"The pride I feel in representing Portugal is greater than that of any other international player”.

And for Ronaldo, there are two things left he'd like to achieve; winning the Nations League and reaching 1000 career goals.



On that, he said: “The missions now are two: winning the Nations League and reaching 1000 career goals”.

Continuation of an era

As it stands, the Al Nassr striker has appeared an incredible 233 times for Portugal and has scored 146 goals.

3 Ronaldo grabbed three goals at the World Cup to extend his record of scoring in every one Credit: Getty

This makes him the highest goalscorer at national level in men's professional football.



In terms of honours, he has the European Championship and Nations League to his name.

But the World Cup has more than likely evaded him, given he'll be 45 by the time the next one rolls around.

He has scored 11 times across the six World Cups that he's played in.

But Ronaldo refuses to deny that he could go on and on, saying: “Will this be my final chapter? Maybe, I don’t know. This could be my final season. But I don’t know.

“If my body allows me to, and if my mind does too, and if I’m still in good shape, then I don’t know. I don’t know what will happen”.



The race to 1,000 goals

That 1,000 career goal mark is getting closer and closer for Ronaldo.

The forward is on 979 career goals for club and country, and he has three for Ange Postecoglou's Al Nassr this season so far.

But if you look at his previous scoring rate in Saudi Arabia, Ronaldo has scored over 30 in each of his years there.

So, if he sticks to that rate, the 1,000 goals target will fall at some point this season.

And he can get there a bit quicker with a solid opening to the Nations League.



Portugal take on Wales, Norway on two occasions as well as Denmark with their first match against Wales on Thursday night, kick-off 7:45pm.

Sports.title: Idrissa Gana Gueye invests in top flight club with ex-Liverpool star in surprise announcement
Sports.content:
Idrissa Gana Gueye invests in top flight club with ex-Liverpool star in surprise announcement

Former Premier League midfielders Idrissa Gana Gueye and Lucas Leiva have become the latest athletes to invest in Le Mans FC.

It follows the club's return to the French top-flight earlier this year following a 17-year thanks to two successive promotions.



3 Former Everton and Aston Villa star Gueye has invested in Le Mans FC alongside ex-Liverpool man Lucas Credit: Getty

Le Mans had dropped as low as the sixth-tier after they were liquidated in 2013.

However, they now find themselves rubbing shoulders with the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Marseille once again.

Gueye and Lucas invest in Le Mans FC

There are also notable names within the club's group of investors, who have now been joined by Gueye and Lucas.



Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic are already shareholders.

Meanwhile, former Formula 1 drivers Felipe Massa and Kevin Magnussen have both invested.



Brazilian businessman Georgios Frangulis, who is engaged to world No.2 tennis ace Aryna Sabalenka, is also an investor.

Ex-Everton and Aston Villa man Gueye has now joined the club to help strengthen Le Mans' ties with African football.



The 36-year-old is Senegal's all-time leading appearance maker with 135 caps to his name.

Having left the Toffees in the summer, Gueye joined Saudi Pro League side Al Diriyah last month.

3 Le Mans were promoted to Ligue 1 after a 17-year absence last season Credit: AFP

Gueye and Lucas statements

In a statement, Gueye explained: "I am proud to join the Le Mans FC project as an investor.



"The club has a strong identity, genuine ambition, and a clear commitment to talent development.

"I look forward to putting my experience in French, English, international, and African football to work for the project and helping to strengthen its ties with Senegal and West Africa, particularly through the For Hope Campus."

Meanwhile, Lucas will work within player recruitment and development at the Stade Marie-Marvingt.

The Brazilian added: "I am very proud to join Le Mans FC alongside OutField and to be part of this new chapter for the club.



"Football has shaped my life and given me the opportunity to experience the sport at the highest level. Today, I want to put everything I've learned throughout my career to use in ambitious projects with a clear vision for the future.

"I deeply believe in what Le Mans FC is building. There is a history, an identity and real potential here, but above all, a shared ambition to build something sustainable and successful in the long term.

3 Leiva is set to work within recruitment and player development at Le Mans Credit: Getty

"For me, becoming a partner in this project means believing in its vision, contributing to its future, and helping Le Mans FC take the next steps in its history."



Lucas had spells with Brazilian club Gremio, Liverpool and Lazio before retiring in 2023.

The 39-year-old also won 24 senior caps for Brazil during his playing career.

Le Mans are currently ninth in Ligue 1 after claiming their first win of the season against Lorient on Saturday.

Patrick Videira's side face PSG at the Parc des Princes on October 10 in their first game after the international break.

Sports.title: Arsenal teenager joins Premier League rival just a year after poaching him from EFL club
Sports.content:
Arsenal teenager joins Premier League rival just a year after poaching him from EFL club

Academy star Mishel Nduka has left Arsenal after just one year to join Manchester City.

The 16-year-old joined the Gunners in the summer of 2025 on a scholarship deal from Championship club Charlton Athletic.

2 Nduka is a very highly rated teenage star Credit: Getty

The midfielder had the option to stay in north London with the offer of a deal from Arsenal.

But he turned it down to accept a scholarship contract from Man City instead.

Nduka is seen as a hot prospect for the future and has represented England at youth level and is currently away with their under-17 squad.

Arsenal offered a competitive salary to Nduka, but he has picked the Etihad over the Emirates. He will sign a professional deal with City once he turns 17 in April.

Nduka impressed enough to play for the Under-18s plenty of times last year and made the step up to Premier League 2.

He is expected to mainly play for Man City's Under-18s having come off the bench at the weekend for his new club.

The Citizens won 6-0 and have made a fantastic start to the season, sitting top of the table with a maximum 18 points from their first six matches.

Another starlet slips past Arsenal

Nduka is another talented player who has picked Man City over Arsenal this year.

The most obvious example is Jeremy Monga, who left Leicester City to join City over Arsenal.

The talented forward had looked set to join the Gunners in the summer with the two clubs agreeing a fee for the winger.

2 Monga has headed out to join Swansea City for some valuable first-team football Credit: Manchester City

But Arsenal felt it was too high, and they wanted to re-negotiate.

That allowed City to swoop in for Monga, and they agreed to pay the League One side an initial £10million with an additional £2.5m in add-ons.

That made Monga the most expensive 16-year-old in Premier League history.

And in the end, Monga decided that the pathway at City to the first team was clearer.

Speaking after his Man City debut during pre-season, he said: "It [Arsenal interest] was very strong because it was very close to me going there, very close.

"The main decision was probably the pathway and the club itself. They've been so successful that it was a no-brainer when City call. It's every child's dream to win trophies and be at the top with the best.

"Once I get the opportunity I just need to show myself, and once I do that, everything will take care of itself. I feel like, to me personally, I see myself at City more. I see myself in blue."

Sports.title: Jim White corrects Arsenal fans who made Fabian Hurzeler clip go viral
Sports.content:
Jim White has made it clear that Fabian Hurzeler didn't just go into the talkSPORT studio because Brighton beat Arsenal.

The German joined White and Simon Jordan on Tuesday morning and reflected on Brighton's start to the season and their 3-0 win over the Gunners.



3 Brighton have claimed some massive scalps since the German arrived at the Amex Credit: Getty

The Seagulls ended Arsenal's 100 per cent start to their Premier League title defence in emphatic fashion.

However, due to the proximity to the win over Arsenal, many Gunners fans accused Hurzeler of embarking on a media tour.

But that has been dismissed by White.

Speaking on White and Jordan, he said: "I noticed that a clip of Fabian talking about how Brighton went about in attempting to beat Arsenal...



"And they were successful in doing so, winning 3-0, and I noticed there was a pile-on from Arsenal fans saying that Hurzeler was on tour, suggesting he was doing a media tour because they had beaten Arsenal.

"But just for all of you out there who did jump on that, you totally wasted your time posting these comments because the interview yesterday was organised way before that match was played at the weekend.



"So, he was always coming in during this international break, so if Arsenal had won at the weekend, Fabian Hurzeler would have still been sat in that seat."

Jordan added: "The timing happened to work out as a very apt time for us."



3 Brighton are unbeaten in all competitions this season Credit: Getty

How did Brighton beat Arsenal?

The champions arrived at the Amex expecting a hard game, but it proved to be way beyond that.

Pascal Gross opened the scoring with a drilled right-footed effort from the edge of the area.

That lead was doubled just before half time as Charalampos Kostoulas was given time to pick his spot from distance.



And in the second half, Chema Andres headed home from a corner.

In the interview with talkSPORT, Hurzeler made it clear how they got the win.

He said: "We focused on us, really. We wanted to win the small battles first, what I mean is win the first header, win the first tackle, win the first throw-in, win the first corner.

"It sounds a little bit old school but it really was our approach because when you win these small battles, then you grow into the game.

"Then you can maybe create a bigger chance, then you can create a bigger win of scoring a goal. But first of all, it's getting into this game, having this commitment to our style of play, to our principles, and then winning the small battles.



"When you win the small battles, the players gain confidence, the players create self-belief, the players really trust each other. We grew into this game, and we also had the right moments on our side."

3 Brighton turned in one of the most complete performances of the season Credit: Getty

Good but not perfect

As much as Hurlezer was happy with his side's win and performance, he wants more.

"Our philosophy is we want to play intense football, having a good balance between defensive ability and controlling the game in possession.



"Therefore, if you want to control the game in possession, you need to have this intensity to win the ball back as quickly as possible.

"You need players who have this commitment to our pressing and I think that was definitely key - they played, we scored, and that was our commitment from the first second.

"Was it a perfect game? I'm a perfectionist, I wouldn't say it was a perfect game.

"There's still things to improve. But, overall, our challenge now will be to make these kind of exceptional performances normal. This is the challenge we have now.



"We have this phrase, 'We want to challenge the establishment'. Challenging the establishment doesn't mean to challenge them in one-to-one games, you have to challenge them when you're not playing against them.

"So, we have to be consistent in performances and these kind of performances, they have to get normal for us and that, I think, is the biggest challenge we can set ourselves."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he considered RETIRING from Portugal duty after the World Cup as he opens up on pursuit of 1,000 career goals
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he considered RETIRING from Portugal duty after the World Cup as he opens up on pursuit of 1,000 career goals

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed he considered retiring from international duty after the World Cup but stressed he will 'always be available' to help the Portuguese national team.

Ronaldo, 41, had refused to confirm whether he would continue representing Portugal after his fifth and final World Cup in the summer, where the national team suffered a limp 1-0 defeat in the last-16 to eventual champions Spain.

Despite the expectation that Ronaldo would retire from international football, the forward was named in new manager Jorge Jesus's first 25-man squad for their upcoming Nations League matches against Wales, Denmark and Norway.

Speaking ahead of their opening match with Wales, Ronaldo admitted he nearly called time on his career with the national team.

'Yes, I'm always thinking about my decisions, I think about everything. You see me here, so I decided to continue,' Ronaldo said at a press conference.

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted he considered retiring from international football this summer

Ronaldo, 41, had been non-committal over his future with Portugal after their World Cup exit

'There is a new young generation, but for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.

'Whenever they say they don't want me in the national team, I will be the first one to go. When I think I am not adding anything to the team, or that I create an atmosphere, I will be the first to go. I will take my suitcase and leave.

'The Portuguese count on me, that's why I'm still here, just look at the numbers, I'm sure you can make some calculations, I'm still doing well.

'The day they don't count on me, no problem, I will leave. I will always be the No 1 fan of this federation.'

Ronaldo insisted he is only focused on the 'present moment' after being asked whether he would be continuing until next summer – when the Nations League finals will take place – or until the 2028 European Championships.

He acknowledged there are critics that 'try to kill me' but said he is motivated by people who still want to keep seeing him play.

'I cannot be 100 per cent honest, sometimes I have to be politically correct,' Ronaldo said.

'I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they've tried to kill me – with a shotgun – but I can still move away from it.

Ronaldo acknowledged reaching 1,000 career goals was a target but said it is not an obsession

'I am used to it, I have been doing this for more than 20 years, I'm quite used to it. What I can control, I will. What I can't, I won't.'

The Al-Nassr forward, who has scored 146 goals in 233 games for Portugal, was questioned about his desire to reach the 1,000 career goal mark.

Ronaldo, who is 21 goals short of the staggering milestone, declared that while it was a target he was not obsessed by it.

'It would be the cherry on the top of the cake to score my 1,000th goal with the national team. It would be the culmination of a beautiful story.

'I said I wanted to reach that target and I will reach that target. But I don't have an obsession. If you are obsessed with something, you won't get it.'

Jesus confirmed Ronaldo will start against Wales on Thursday, with the new boss describing the veteran forward as 'a symbol of Portugal'.

Sports.title: Harry Kane reveals Declan Rice sent him a voice note explaining his absence as he sends warning to England's five drop-outs - and insists stars will hold inquest over Argentina defeat
Sports.content:
Harry Kane believes England’s five World Cup drop-outs are losing out on vital preparation time for the 2028 European Championships. Kane is no stranger to the matter of players withdrawing from England camps. In November 2024 the England captain delivered a resolute message to the nine players who had declared themselves unavailable through injury for the final two games of Lee Carsley’s spell as interim coach. ‘I think England comes before anything,’ said Kane back then. ‘England comes before club.’ Almost two years on, Thomas Tuchel’s first England squad following the World Cup will be missing Arsenal’s Declan Rice and Cole Palmer of Chelsea – who played 90 minutes for their clubs at the weekend – as well as Manchester United duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo and Newcastle full-back Tino Livramento. Kane said: ‘We spend so much time at club level together and building on the pitch, off the pitch. You don't get that luxury with international football. ‘So, for me, personally, just every moment together [matters], every camp together, just to get to know players, get to know how people play tactically, how the manager wants us to play. Harry Kane and Lewis Hall compete for the ball in training at St George's Park ‘All these things are really important as before we know it, we will be in the summer and then we will be in the Euros in 2028. ‘It seems we are far away from the Euros, we're far away from Nations League final next summer, but we're not. 'We have two weeks now, we have a week in November. We have a week or so in March, and then we’re hopefully playing a Nations League semi-final and final in June, and then it's the same next season. ‘So, although it seems far away, I think actually it’s not a long time at all.’ Two years ago, Kane accused his missing team mates of taking advantage of an opportunity to essentially have a break. This time he didn’t go anywhere near as far. 'I've spoken about this before and I don't want to make it a big thing,’ said Kane. ‘Everyone has their own situation. I know how tough the summer was and I know especially in the Premier League how gruelling that schedule is. ‘I trust all the boys. I spoke to Dec, for example. He sent me a voice note. I know Dec goes far and beyond for the club and country, so I know how much he gives and I know he's been struggling for a while with his issues. Declan Rice is sitting out England's four Nations League fixtures amid what Kane described as a 'gruelling' Premier League schedule ‘From our point of view, I think the togetherness that we have will not be shaken through people not being here right now. All it does is give other people opportunity to impress the manager.’ Kane is 33 now and will match Peter Shilton’s England appearance record of 125 if he plays in all four games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia (twice) over the next fortnight. Sitting in his training gear at St George’s Park today, the Bayern Munich striker looked in the shape of his life, something underlined by his status as one of the Ballon d’Or favourites ahead of the ceremony in London next month. Mentally, however, the scars of an ultimately disappointing World Cup are taking longer to heal. Kane revealed that he chose not to watch the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, flying to New York to play golf as soon as England’s third-place play-off win had been secured against France the day before. In his mind, questions remain unanswered. The most pertinent one revolves around the way that England played in defeat to Argentina in their semi-final in Atlanta. ‘This one hurt for sure more than any other one,’ said Kane. Kane admitted the defeat by Argentina hurt more than any other in his career ‘I'd say even more than when I missed the penalty against France in Qatar because of the manner in which it happened. ‘It felt like it wasn't us as a team out there. It wasn't the team that we wanted to be and said we'd be. ‘I think sometimes when you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing doing it your way and accepting it and taking it on the chin and moving on.’ England’s retreat to their own penalty box after taking the lead against Argentina is something that continues to vex England supporters and indeed their coach. As such, it felt natural to ask Kane why it happened. ‘I think those are the questions that we need to kind of discuss amongst ourselves and answer ourselves, as players and as coaching staff,’ said Kane. ‘How can we be better in those moments? How can we be ourselves more in those moments? Through qualifying campaigns and a lot of games in tournaments, we play with a certain intensity and we play in in a good way. ‘It's something that we haven't quite been able to do in latter stages of tournaments against the bigger nations and the better nations and it may be a mixture of things. It may be personalities. It may be mentality. It may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games. ‘But I think it’s a conversation that we need to have as a group. We wanna try and take that next step because I think that would be an important one.’ England’s 24-man squad – Tuchel has replaced two of the missing group with Everton’s James Garner and Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White – gathered at their Staffordshire base on Monday and immediately sat down for a briefing with the head coach. Thomas Tuchel is ready for the next phase of his time as England boss having fallen short in the World Cup semi-final Tuchel’s public reflections on seven weeks in America last Friday were fascinating without ever being consistently enlightening. But it’s clear from what he said to his players this week that he has identified problems transferring training performances to matchday familiar to a series of England managers who have passed before. Kane revealed: ‘I think it's trying to translate how well we train into games. ‘It’s easier said than done, but if we can get better at that I think we'll show an even better version of ourselves. So that was kind of the general meeting really. ‘We're still going to talk about the summer and talk about good and bad. That will happen naturally over the next year. ‘We have to heal while getting on with it. In life in general, whenever there's like big major events, you have time to process it, you have time to talk about it. ‘In football, you don't have that. In football, before you know it's the next one, and now we're focused on Nations League. ‘So it's a hard balance because you're trying to get over it and learn from it. But also we play the world champions on Saturday and it's a big, important game.’

Sports.title: Harry's American dream: England captain Kane plans to 'seriously look' at becoming an NFL kicker... and opens door to finishing career in the MLS
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has his eye on a career in the NFL when he eventually stops playing football.

England captain Kane – tipped to be next month’s Ballon D’or Winner - believes he may have ‘five or six years’ left in the professional game and will match Peter Shilton’s all-time appearance record of 125 caps if he plays in all four of his country’s forthcoming Nations League games.

But the 33-year-old revealed on Wednesday that he already has his eye on trying out as an American Football specialist place kicker.

A two-handicap golfer, Kane has given up on his previous ambition of joining the professional ranks but said: ‘That [the NFL] is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously.

‘It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years but the NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one.

‘I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure and technique. If I did that, in terms of training, I would be closer to that more than any other sport.

Harry Kane says taking penalties could help him succeed as an NFL kicker

‘If I was to do it, it is something I would take seriously. I would take six months to a year to try and practise before. Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that, it might be a thing where you could connect the two seasons.

‘It is in the back of my mind because right now, I am feeling that I want to play as long as I can here.’

Playing in the MLS is also something Kane has not talked about before and it appears the Bayern Munich striker is starting to consider what the back end of his career may look like.

For now, he is concentrating on sorting out the final details of a new contract in the Bundesliga.

Kane was subject of interest from Barcelona in the summer but said: ‘Bayern and I are still talking. We're in good talks, I'll be honest.

‘We're fairly close. There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there and I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement.

‘I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment. Like I touched on a bit earlier, at this level, I want to just be at this level, and push this level for as long as possible.’

Kane, pictured with wife Katie at Oktoberfest in Munich, is talking with Bayern over a new deal

Having just had the season of his life with club and country, Kane revealed a new strict diet has played its part.

‘The biggest thing was after games having a few sweets to eat or something that isn’t good for you,’ he said.

‘But last year, especially, I was ultra-strict. With the World Cup on the horizon, I knew how hot it was going to be, how demanding it was going to be.

‘The fact I took out some of that stuff and then was performing the way I was performing and having my best season ever, it became addictive and I just carried on through the World Cup into this season.

‘Ultimately I think all those little details do add up and when I talk about extracting as much as I can from this period of my career, these are the things that are going to help me.’

Sports.title: How Premier League clubs are exploiting their most loyal fans - the season ticket tricks used by Chelsea and Man United, the subtle ways 'old-school' supporters are being swapped out for tourists, 'hospitality' rip-offs and why the worst is yet to come
Sports.content:
The railing that once hoisted the Holmesdale Fanatics flag at Selhurst Park has gone. The distinctive and raucous Crystal Palace ultras group? Disbanded.

The flagpole remained in place for the first home game of the season, just 24 hours after the group announced their dissolution, but had vanished by the following match.

Selhurst has felt a little lifeless ever since. The ceaseless noise from the 400-man section behind the goal in the Holmesdale Road End is no more.

When Daily Mail Sport asked the Holmesdale Fanatics for an explanation, they declined and redirected us to their initial statement, where they criticise the ‘draconian restrictions’ imposed on supporters.

Those restrictions extend well beyond Selhurst Park. Across the country, the football fan experience is changing, replaced by a game that is increasingly commercialised and gentrified.

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to insiders across the Premier League and beyond, industry experts and, most importantly, loyal supporters themselves to uncover just how the modern-day fan is being exploited – and why the worst may yet be to come...

Crystal Palace's distinctive and raucous Holmesdale Fanatics group has disbanded, leaving Selhurst Park a little lifeless

It is a sign of the wider exploitation and disenfrachisement of old-school, matchgoing supporters

Times are tough for football fans of all stripes, but season-ticket holders are feeling the pinch more than anyone. Premier League regulations now restrict those fans from sharing their season tickets with fellow supporters, family and friends.

At the start of the season, digital tickets became mandatory, supposedly to improve stadium security, prevent ticket touting and streamline entry into stadiums.

Manchester United have used digital ticket enforcement to identify what they describe as ‘suspicious activity’ and curb ticket touting, banning 685 season ticket holders as a result. However, fears remain that innocent fans using the ticket sharing system have been caught up in the clean-up operation.

A cynic would argue the new policy presented a fresh opportunity for clubs to squeeze supporters and monetise them sharing their season ticket.

Rather than the trusty plastic card which supporters could hand over to friends if they were not attending a match or wanted to split the cost of a season ticket, fans must now resell their tickets through official club channels – which clubs can make a profit from – or share them using the club’s ticketing platform, with access often commanding a membership fee.

At Chelsea, for example, to share a ticket the recipient must be a member, with prices beginning at £15. Meanwhile, Crystal Palace allow season-ticket holders to share their match ticket with non-members but charge a one-off £50 fee for the privilege.

Manchester United offer a ‘ticket sharing’ membership which allows supporters to receive forwarded tickets from season-ticket holders – charging £30 per person.

There are, in fairness, valid safety concerns behind this development. The Premier League partly introduced the scheme to ensure match attendees can be identified, which helps the enforcement of banning orders and detection of high-risk supporters.

But the self-serving, avaricious clubs have opportunistically commercialised supporters' autonomy over their own tickets.

At Manchester City, season tickets must be used for 16 Premier League home games, ten of which must be attended by the named individual, or the ticket will be cancelled

Across town, United have used digital ticket enforcement to identify what they describe as ‘suspicious activity’ but fears remain that innocent fans have been caught up in the clean-up

Things are unlikely to get better anytime soon. One senior football executive told Daily Mail Sport that clubs view season tickets as a ‘discounted rate’, blocking a conveyor belt of high-spending corporate and tourist spectators attending one-off games that would generate more revenue. They added that clubs could look to reduce the number of their season tickets.

That perspective was echoed by football finance expert and host of The Price of Football Podcast Kieran Maguire, who told Daily Mail Sport: ‘The bigger brands see season-ticket holders as bed blockers because tickets can be sold at a higher price to international fans and those desperate to see their club but who can only manage it once a year due to logistical challenges.

‘If we take the case of Liverpool, Anfield has gone from 44,000 to 61,000 capacity, but there was hardly any increase in season-ticket sales. It is far more lucrative to target the corporate market or the day-fan market as opposed to someone who is a local Red and unlikely to go to the megastore and drink in the ground beforehand because they go to the pub with their mates, sit at the same table and have the same chats.

‘These people, of course, are the bedrock of football fans. For political reasons, clubs won’t want to be seen to be reducing season tickets. But I don’t think we will see an increase going forward unless they are for corporate seats.

‘In some of the more desirable areas of the stadium, the clubs might not convert season tickets that haven’t been renewed into new season tickets despite long waiting lists.'

That shift has already begun, with United relocating around 500 fans sat behind the dugout at Old Trafford to the top of the North Stand to increase hospitality tickets in what United describe as a ‘high value area of the stadium’.

At Manchester City, meanwhile, season tickets must be used for 16 Premier League home games, ten of which must be attended by the named individual, or the ticket will be cancelled. Some fans argued the move breaches the Equality Act as pregnant women, mothers or disabled people could struggle to attend for prolonged periods.

To make matters worse, season-ticket waiting lists are becoming increasingly exploitative. Arsenal’s exceeds 110,000 people, meaning the club would need to turn over every season ticket three times before reaching the bottom. With the current wait time estimated at around 20 years and a £50 deposit required to join, it is difficult to envisage many supporters ever securing one.

There is therefore logic in closing the waiting list – as Liverpool have done – rather than asking supporters to part with their hard-earned cash for a ticket they may never receive. However, clubs' passive income would take a hit. Arsenal say they regularly review the waiting list and would consult supporters on any proposed changes.

Liverpool supporters recently successfully protested ticket price hikes of 3 per cent for three consecutive seasons

English football is shifting towards a matchday experience built around tourists rather than hardcore supporters. Americans fans used to taking in entertainment that goes beyond the game itself

Aside from their wallets being raided, the fan experience is also declining as English football culture shifts towards a matchday experience built around tourists rather than hardcore supporters. American fans, in particular, are accustomed to taking in entertainment that goes beyond the game itself.

Tourism dilutes the home support. At Selhurst Park, people were spotted wearing Erling Haaland Norway shirts in the home end during Manchester City’s 4-1 win over Palace in August.

And when Palace travelled to Craven Cottage earlier this month, Daily Mail Sport observed Chicago Fire and Brazil shirts in Fulham's newly redeveloped Riverside Stand, with some spectators even whipping out their phones to record themselves when the visitors scored. A similar picture is painted weekly across Premier League stadiums.

Fan experience has played a significant role in the breakdown in relations between Palace and the Holmesdale Fanatics. The fan group want an organic atmosphere inside the stadium, while the club have veered towards an artificial one.

Before kick-off, the HF had found themselves competing with Natasha Bedingfield’s Unwritten - among other pop songs - blared over the recently upgraded PA system.

There is an internal directive to ensure the stadium looks attractive on television; hence the introduction of fireworks and pyrotechnics when the players enter the pitch. But manufacturing a look is precisely what the HF stand against.

Perhaps the pomp and circumstance makes football clubs more marketable to international audiences.

The Premier League’s own economic and social impact report from July 2026 boasts that the top flight drew over a million international fans to matches in the 2023-24 season, with a trip-related spend of £903million. Those numbers are projected to rise continuously.

The Premier League say the top flight drew over a million international fans to matches in the 2023-24 season, with a trip-related spend of £903million

Palace's Holmesdale Fanatics want an organic atmosphere inside the stadium, while the club have veered towards an artificial one

Daily Mail Sport spoke to one US-based neutral who regularly flies over to attend Premier League games. Among the thousands he has spent on tickets already this season, he paid £350 for a general admission ticket to watch Ipswich take on Liverpool at Portman Road, purchased through a third-party reseller.

Clubs discourage buying third-party tickets as they do not receive the benefits besides the money spent in the stadium on merchandise, food and drink – although it does indicate the extravagant prices international fans are willing to pay for a £38 ticket, splashing nine times over the odds.

It has not gone unnoticed at Premier League clubs that World Cup stadiums in the United States were 99.7 per cent full despite extortionate general admission prices. That spells danger for domestic supporters.

Sites like Seat Unique and Sportsworld have partnerships with Premier League clubs including Manchester City, Manchester United and Everton and market padded seat packages suitable for tourists. For Manchester City’s Champions League match against Paris Saint-Germain next month, Sportsworld are selling a £279 padded seat package which non-members can purchase – the only requirement is they are not in away colours.

'Westview' at Stamford Bridge is similar. The package ranges from £225 to £625 per game depending on the prestige of the fixture for a padded seat and a market hall style concourse with no food or drink included.

It is barely a hospitality package, besides sitting in a swankier area of the stadium. Simply put, Westview allows Chelsea to sell extortionately priced tickets to non-members, enabling the club to benefit directly from the tourist trade. These visitors are also likely to spend money on food and drink and visit the megastore.

Some Premier League clubs have even been spotted bringing the megastore to fans, with merchandise staff now carrying trays of baseball caps and scarves around the pitch and concourses to cater to the tourist market.

The Premier League needs to captivate an international audience but it should not come at the expense of ordinary fans.

Last year, the Football Supporters' Association said: ‘Football is becoming a luxury good for some, pricing out working-class communities, young supporters and families who represent the future heartbeat of the game. Record broadcast revenues – the 2025-28 deal is worth £12.25billion – and packed corporate hospitality sections tell us that financial sustainability does not depend on pricing out traditional supporters.’

Yet the cheapest ticket for a Category A game in nine of the 20 Premier League grounds exceeds £50, while general admission season tickets range from £380 to £3,192. Newcastle offer the cheapest season ticket, and Fulham’s is the most expensive.

Coventry City are one of the few clubs that have looked out for their supporters in recent years

‘Football is becoming a luxury good for some, pricing out working-class communities, young supporters and families who represent the future heartbeat of the game,' say the FSA

Although the outlook for fans appears bleak, there are rays of positivity to cling on to. Coventry City deserve praise for rewarding loyalty. In 2023, the club committed to giving supporters who bought a season ticket a free one should they reach the Premier League. This season, some 5,000 fans are benefiting from that scheme.

The £30 price cap for away fans has been extended until the end of the 2027-28 season – providing good value for the most loyal supporters.

And despite the widespread rip-off, fans can still fight back. Liverpool supporters had success at the end of last season after the club announced season ticket price hikes of 3 per cent for three consecutive seasons. But a protest at Anfield – where supporters raised yellow cards – prompted the club to reconsider, raising prices for this season and freezing them for 2027-28.

In light of the European Super League debacle, Premier League clubs created fan advisory boards to ensure that supporters' concerns were heard. Now, however, those bodies must stop being symbolic – and ensure English football remembers its most loyal fans represent the heart of the game.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly reveals Buddhist concept that helps him combat nerves - as he bids for first England cap in almost a year
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly reveals Buddhist concept that helps him combat nerves - as he bids for first England cap in almost a year

Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly has opened up the Buddhist concept that helps him keep a clear head.

Turning 20 on Saturday, Lewis-Skelly has built reputation for an ice-cool composure - and the England international was recently quizzed on whether the Arsenal defender has a set routine for tackling big-match nerves.

‘There’s a Buddhist concept; it’s about the monkey mind,' he told the Men In Blazers media network. ‘It’s practically about the restless mind, how you can jump from concern to concern.’

‘So whenever I feel a type of weight, for me it’s important to bring my nervous system down and to bring stillness back to my mind, to be calm. Whether it is through breathing techniques, music or talking with other people; I just feel like it is important I always remain calm.’

Lewis-Skelly - who was all smiles in a white jumper and dark-framed glasses as he reported for England duty at St George’s Park - also revealed he is a strong believer in practising mindfulness, and values having a good circle around him.

‘It is definitely the people around me that help me with these types of principles and concepts,' he said. 'But it just comes from practising mindfulness, because I want to touch on how important the mind is.’

Myles Lewis-Skelly reported for England duty in a smart white jumper

... and trains with England at St George's Park ahead of four Nations League clashes

He also opened up on filling a journal each morning and evening.

'Journaling helps me to understand what brings me joy, what brings me happiness, what takes away my joy, what takes away my happiness,’ he added. ‘It just allows me to be more intentional about what I am thinking. It does translate on the pitch.’

Alongside Ezri Konsa, Bukayo Saka, and Eberechi Eze, Lewis-Skelly is among the four Arsenal players named in the England squad for the upcoming international friendlies.

The Arsenal left-back will see familiar faces as world champions Spain have called up David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi for this week’s heavyweight clash at Wembley.

With manager Thomas Tuchel adding him to the England squad as a midfielder, there were no surprises when he revealed his preferred position.

'I am a midfielder,' he said. 'But, at the end of the day, it is all down to the team’s needs. No player, no individual, is bigger than the team’s goal. Whatever I have to do to help the team, I will do it.'

The 19-year-old last played for England in October 2025 against Latvia in a World Cup qualifier.

Lewis-Skelly was just eight when he first arrived at Arsenal’s Hale End Academy. When asked if he had the chance to tell his younger self what it really takes to make it, he said: 'You just have to enjoy what you do. You can't lose that love. You can't lose that passion, that desire for what you do, because once that love is out of the window, you may as well choose a new profession. Stay loving and stay true to your passion.'

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney hits out at Benjamin Sesko for wearing 'little stupid shinpads' as Man United legend questions striker's shin injury in brutal takedown
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney hits out at Benjamin Sesko for wearing 'little stupid shinpads' as Man United legend questions striker's shin injury in brutal takedown

Wayne Rooney has questioned why Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko sat out the club's 1-1 draw away at Fulham with a shin injury.

Rooney took to his podcast Stick to United to voice his displeasure with Sesko's absence from Sunday's game, implying that the Slovenian's shin injury was not serious enough to rule him out.

'Shin? Has he broken it?' said Rooney. 'You can hurt your shin, you can take tackles... I bet he's wearing them little stupid shinpads as well.'

The former United skipper did not stop there, later going on to say, 'If you're trying to play No9 [for Man United] and you've got a must-win game and you've got a sore shin and you're not playing... that's a big part of the problem.'

Later on in the show he reflected on his time at United, saying: 'Unless you physically can't play, you play when you're injured. I remember before games we used to get injections and the doctor used to put them in your arse.'

Wayne Rooney did not mince his words when criticising the Slovenian international

Sesko has enjoyed purple patches in his short time at Old Trafford but has been unable to pick up consistent form

Two more former United players, Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt, also voiced their concern over the striker's omission from Sunday's squad.

On their podcast, The Good, The Bad & The Football with Paddy McGuinness, Scholes aligned with his ex-teammate's view, saying: 'If it isn't broken, just wear your shinpads.' Butt then added: 'You're a player - you either break your shin or you don't play!'

Paul Scholes (left) and Nicky Butt (right) agreed with Rooney that Sesko should have played through the injury

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, the comments by Butt and Scholes did not go down well in Slovenia, with Leeds defender Jaka Bijol backing Sesko to rise above it.

‘I hope and believe that Beni knows how to distance himself from this kind of pressure,’ he said. ‘When things aren't going your best on the pitch and you have certain doubts, reading things like this can make your confidence even worse.

‘He shouldn't pay too much attention to it, since we all know what quality he has. He himself knows what kind of footballer he is, and I think he always shows it with incredible things on the pitch.’

Another of Sesko's compatriots, Zan Vipotnik of Swansea, also spoke out in defence of the forward as he said: 'It's not easy for him. Recurring physical problems are bad, and to add to that it messes with your head... I really hope and believe his absence from the pitch will be as short as possible and that things will turn for the best very soon.'

Sports.title: Man United reveal how much money they've SAVED with sacked boss Ruben Amorim taking over at AC Milan - as they try to rake in more cash by selling bits of the pitch for £125!
Sports.content:
Manchester United saved £8.5million when Ruben Amorim took over as head coach of AC Milan, the club’s latest financial results have revealed. United reported in May that the total compensation due to Amorim and his staff could rise to a maximum of £16.7m. But his appointment as Milan boss in June meant United have paid £8.2m, less than half that figure. Wednesday’s results also revealed that the cost of financing United’s debt has now rocketed past the £1billion mark since the Glazer family’s leveraged takeover. The club’s annual figures show that United paid £69.6m – an increase of £48.4m or 228.3 per cent from the previous year – in interest and other finance costs. The overall debt itself still stands at more than £1bn despite the cost-cutting measures imposed by minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos which contributed to United turning a £18.4m operating loss into a £22.6m over the last year. It consists of £577.6m of historic debt from the Glazer takeover in 2005, £111.4m owing on the club’s revolving credit facility and outstanding transfer fees. Ineos co-owned Man United have announced record revenue of £677.6m for the 2025-26 season The Americans’ £790m buyout has been the biggest factor in United bleeding over £1bn in the last two decades, and that infuriates fans who are fiercely opposed to the Glazers’ ownership and increasingly disillusioned with the Ratcliffe regime. After spending just £163m in the transfer market this summer – substantially less than many of their rivals – United are 12th in the Premier League table after one win in five games. The club are also at odds with large sections of the fanbase over their attempts to increase revenue and, more recently, crack down on ticket touts. It has also emerged that emails have been sent out to members and season ticket holders offering them the chance to buy miniature squares of the Old Trafford turf – which was re-laid in the summer for the first time in 14 years – for £125. United laid a new playing surface at the 'Theatre of Dreams' for the first time in 14 years over the summer, and the old pitch has been cut into 7cm x 7cm squares. Those squares have been packaged in acrylic cubes and are being sent out to supporters who want them in a smart black casing. The United website reads: 'Take home a piece of Old Trafford with this official turf cube, perfect for fans who want a keepsake from one of the most famous pitches in the world. 'Carefully preserved, this piece of turf makes a priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of match days alive. The sacking of Ruben Amorim in January cost the club £8.5million in compensation 'Perfect for gifting to passionate Reds, this turf cube makes a great addition to desks or can be displayed in a cabinet with other Manchester United collectibles.' The club have described the purchasable turf as a 'one-of-a-kind collector’s item' to club members and season-ticket holders in an email offering them 'exclusive' early access. Despite the huge debt and costs of servicing it, United are still committed to building a new £2bn stadium. The latest financial results revealed that the club spent £63.5m in June on a 25-acre triangle of land located 350 metres away from Old Trafford. While United were able to announce record revenues of £677.6m despite not playing in Europe last season, they reported an overall net loss of £43m – up from £33m last year – which sources say demonstrates the importance of maintaining financial discipline. Chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘We are pleased to have secured record revenues which demonstrates the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football. United are selling small cubes of last season's Old Trafford turf to fans for £125 ‘This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years. It also proves Manchester United’s enduring popularity and commercial strength. ‘While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.’ Commercial revenue for the year was down £16m and sponsorship revenue by £27.9m, partly due to United having no training kit sponsor following the end of their partnership with Tezos. The club have since signed a record £20m-a-year deal with Betway, as well as replacing sleeve sponsor DXC Technology with SumUp. Retail & merchandising revenue for the year was up £11.9m, and broadcasting revenue by £33.9m due to United finishing third in the Premier League after Michael Carrick replaced Amorim in January. Matchday revenue was down £6.8m due to the club’s shortest season since the First World War. Not playing in Europe and going out of both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle meant that United played just 40 games.
