The very resource being mobilized to save the school is, in the meantime, occupying and potentially damaging the space that school needs to function. Residents watching this unfold are left with a daily, physical reminder of the gap between their aspirations for their children and the economic reality constraining them — a school building slowly becoming indistinguishable from a warehouse, its educational purpose paused indefinitely while it earns its keep as storage space instead.

A Town That Has Already Buried Too Much

Kpolokplah’s current struggles do not exist in isolation from its past. This is a town that carries the weight of Liberia’s civil war within its history, having been the site where several residents were killed during the 1994 massacre — one of many dark chapters etched into Bong County’s collective memory. For a community that has already endured such loss, the slow erosion of its children’s access to education represents not just a present-day crisis, but another entry in a long history of hardship that seems to have outlasted the war itself.

Residents, understandably, see the school closure as part of a broader pattern — one in which promises of post-conflict rebuilding and development have been slow to reach communities like theirs, leaving basic services like education perpetually just out of reach.

A Lawmaker’s Balancing Act

The predicament in Kpolokplah has not gone entirely unnoticed at the political level. Hon. James M. Kolleh, Representative for Bong County Electoral District 2, has publicly acknowledged the education and water challenges facing communities under his watch, responding to reports that span not just Kpolokplah but other struggling schools such as Barsee Kpangbai Public School in Blemeyea, which reportedly operates with just two teachers for its entire student body.

In Kpolokplah, there was no fallback plan, because there was no government presence to fall back on. The PTA was not merely supplementing the school’s teaching staff — it was the entire staffing infrastructure, quietly substituting for a state responsibility that never arrived. When that substitute system broke down, there was nothing behind it to catch the fall.

Rep. Kolleh’s response has focused heavily on Barsee Kpangbai, where he has pledged to work toward deploying two additional teachers, while more broadly promising to assess the needs of other schools across the district — a commitment that, for now, leaves Kpolokplah’s specific staffing vacuum without a direct answer.

He pointed to past efforts, including last year’s distribution of 5,000 armchairs to area schools, and indicated plans to expand on that furniture initiative this year. Whether

such efforts will translate into the one thing Kpolokplah actually needs — salaried government teachers — remains an open question.

On water access, another pressing concern in the district, Rep. Kolleh was more specific about Kpolokplah itself, confirming that the town is slated to benefit from ongoing water projects and promising, in the interim, to repair the community’s existing hand pump. He framed his broader approach as one of continued responsiveness to constituent needs, describing service to the district as central to his mandate as its elected representative.

Waiting for a Callback

What remains missing from this story is an official accounting from the very body responsible for staffing and overseeing public education in the county. FrontPage Africa contacted County Education Officer David Boakai, who answered the call and indicated he would follow up with a fuller response. That callback never came before publication.

In its absence, silence from the Ministry of Education’s local representative stands in stark contrast to the noise Kpolokplah’s crisis has already generated — a community publicly airing its struggle, a lawmaker publicly responding to it, and, at the center of it all, a county education office that has, for now, said nothing at all. For the children of Kpolokplah, still waiting for a return to their classrooms, that silence may prove just as costly as the unpaid wages that emptied them in the first place.

World.title: Liberia: Rep. Benson Urges Boakai to Prioritize Rural Montserrado in 2027 Budget
World.content:
District 17 Lawmaker Seeks Dedicated Funding for Five Historic Communities, Citing Infrastructure Gaps and Alleged Non-Receipt of Development Funds

By Jaheim Tumu

Monrovia — Montserrado County Electoral District 17 Representative Bernard Blue Benson Jr. is calling on President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to give greater attention to the development needs of rural Montserrado in preparing the 2027 National Budget.

In an open letter to President Boakai dated Tuesday, September 15, Benson requested dedicated government funding for five historic communities in District 17: Arthington, Clay-Ashland, Millsburg, Royesville and Cheesmanburg.

He argued that the longstanding challenges facing these communities require urgent and sustained government attention.

Benson emphasized their social, cultural, political and historical significance, while expressing concern that years of inadequate public investment have contributed to infrastructure deficits and limited access to essential services.

The lawmaker also highlighted the economic potential of the five communities, particularly in agriculture, tourism and cultural development, arguing that these sectors could contribute more meaningfully to local and national growth with targeted government investment.

Pointing to the region’s place in Liberia’s history, Benson noted that it has produced four of the country’s 26 presidents. He said this historical contribution underscores the importance of ensuring that the communities receive meaningful development attention.

Among the major concerns outlined in his letter are deteriorating road networks, inadequate educational and healthcare facilities, poor sanitation, limited administrative capacity and a lack of sustained community-development programs.

At the heart of Benson’s appeal is the argument that residents of rural Montserrado should have equitable access to public services and the benefits of national development, regardless of where they live.

Questions Over Development Funds

Benson also raised concerns about the implementation of the District Development Funds (DDF) and Social Development Funds (SDF), which are intended to support development initiatives.

He argued that bureaucratic and political challenges have undermined the effectiveness of these funding mechanisms, limiting their impact on communities in need.

The District 17 lawmaker further alleged that the district has not benefited from DDF or SDF allocations since Fiscal Year 2024, despite what he said were provisions for the district in the 2025 and 2026 national budgets.

The alleged funding gap, he suggested, has compounded the challenges facing communities already struggling with inadequate infrastructure and essential services.

Calls for Targeted 2027 Budget Support

As preparations continue for the Fiscal Year 2027 National Budget, Benson is urging the Boakai administration to translate budgetary commitments into visible development projects across Arthington, Clay-Ashland, Millsburg, Royesville and Cheesmanburg.

He is seeking particular attention to infrastructure and essential public services, arguing that targeted investments could help address persistent socioeconomic inequalities, improve living conditions and expand opportunities in agriculture and tourism.

Benson also maintained that sustained government investment could strengthen public confidence by demonstrating that rural communities are receiving tangible benefits from national development initiatives.

His appeal brings the development needs of rural Montserrado into the broader debate over equitable public investment, particularly for historically significant communities that he believes have not received adequate government support.

The concerns and funding allegations outlined in Benson’s letter have not been independently verified. The administration’s response to his request was not included in the statement provided.

World.title: Liberia: CDC Prepares to Take Cybercrime Law Fight to Supreme Court After Wrato Release
World.content:
Monrovia-The release of political commentator Jerry Nyantee Wrato from police custody has opened a new and potentially consequential legal battle over Liberia’s recently enacted Cybercrime Law, with the Congress for Democratic Change(CDC) announcing plans to ask the Supreme Court to determine whether portions of the law are consistent with the Constitution.

By Willie N. Tokpah

Lenn Eugene Nagbe, Chief of Office Staff to former President George Manneh Weah said Tuesday, September 22 that the CDC’s Executive Committee had instructed its lawyers to institute proceedings before the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the law.

Nagbe said the party’s decision goes beyond Wrato’s individual case, arguing that the controversy raises broader questions about the limits of political expression, criticism of public officials and the government’s authority to prosecute speech disseminated through digital platforms.

“It is not just about Jerry Wrato; it is about a threat to our democracy,” Nagbe said, announcing the party’s intention to challenge the law.

He said the CDC’s legal team would seek to have the Cybercrime Law declared unconstitutional, describing it as legislation that, in the party’s view, could be used to suppress political expression.

The announcement came hours after Criminal Court “B” of the First Judicial Circuit ordered Wrato released from police custody following a habeas corpus petition filed by his lawyer, Cllr. Garrison Doldeh Yealue Jr.

Judge Pape Suah issued the writ Tuesday, September 22, directing that Wrato be released from further police custody and turned over to the Sheriff of the court.

The order followed a challenge to Wrato’s continued detention after police announced that they had completed their investigation and intended to prosecute him on four alleged violations of Liberia’s Cybercrime Act of 2025.

Wrato’s detention followed the circulation of artificial intelligence-generated images and videos appearing to portray Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung in a derogatory manner.

The material surfaced amid controversy over reports concerning Koung’s security screening at Brussels Airport, reports the Vice President has denied. Police subsequently investigated the circulation of the manipulated content under the Cybercrime Act.

But the case took a different turn after Koung publicly appealed for Wrato’s release, indicating that he did not wish to pursue criminal action against him over the material. Police Inspector General Gregory O. W. Coleman nevertheless maintained that the matter could not be resolved solely based on the Vice President’s wishes.

In a September 21 communication to Vice President Koung, Coleman said the Liberia National Police had a statutory obligation to investigate suspected criminal conduct and had resolved to proceed against Wrato.

Police identified four alleged offenses, misuse of devices, cyberstalking, distribution of data messages that incite damage to property or violence, and distribution of harmful data messages.

The offenses were cited under Sections 10.1, 15.1, 18.1 and 19.1 of the Cybercrime Act. Coleman stressed that forwarding Wrato to court would not amount to a finding of guilt and that the accused would retain the presumption of innocence and other constitutional protections.

CDC Challenges the Law

Nagbe, however, said the CDC considers the detention a violation of Wrato’s constitutional rights. He said the party assembled a team of lawyers to defend what it described as the right to political expression and fair treatment under the law.

“The CDC hired a team of lawyers that advocate for fair play, for freedom of political expression,” Nagbe said. According to him, the lawyers viewed Wrato’s detention from Thursday, September 17, through Tuesday, September 22, as unlawful and moved quickly to challenge it through habeas corpus proceedings. The petition relied on Article 21(f) of the 1986 Constitution and provisions of Liberia’s Civil Procedure Law governing habeas corpus.

The court subsequently ordered Wrato’s release. The case is expected to return to court on Thursday, September 24, when further proceedings are scheduled.

Where Does Political Speech End, and Cybercrime Begin?

At the heart of the emerging legal dispute is a difficult concern on how far the state can go in regulating political expression when that expression is delivered through digital platforms. Nagbe argued that Liberians have a constitutional right to criticize and even make fun of politicians, particularly those who voluntarily enter public life.

“If you do not want anyone to talk about you, don’t get in the political space,” he said.

But the police position presents a different legal question as to whether digital material that allegedly crosses into cyberstalking, incitement, harmful communications or other conduct specifically prohibited by law can be treated simply as political speech.

That question has not been finally determined in Wrato’s case. The police have maintained that their investigation is based on alleged criminal conduct rather than the political identity of the person involved. Wrato, meanwhile, remains presumed innocent unless and until a court of competent jurisdiction determines otherwise.

The habeas corpus ruling itself addresses Wrato’s detention; it does not, on its face, constitute a final judicial determination that the Cybercrime Act is unconstitutional or that the underlying allegations against him are without legal merit.

A Bigger Legal Test Ahead

The CDC’s planned Supreme Court action could therefore move the controversy beyond Wrato’s individual detention and into a broader constitutional examination of Liberia’s cybercrime framework.

Such proceedings could require the Supreme Court to examine the relationship between statutory restrictions on digital communications and constitutional guarantees relating to freedom of speech, expression and political participation.

For the CDC, Nagbe said, the objective is clear, to challenge what the party considers an unconstitutional restriction on political expression.

“We will render the Cyber Crime Law unconstitutional,” he declared. Whether the Supreme Court ultimately accepts that argument, and, if so, how it interprets the contested provisions, will depend on the legal challenge, the provisions placed before the Court and the constitutional questions the justices are asked to determine.

For now, Wrato is out of police custody, the police say prosecution remains warranted, and the CDC is preparing to take the broader constitutional fight to Liberia’s highest court. The next courtroom appearance on September 24 could provide the first indication of how the dispute over Wrato’s detention will proceed, even as a separate constitutional battle over Liberia’s Cybercrime Law begins to take shape.

World.title: Liberia Pitches $1B Revenue Milestone, Mining, Energy and Agriculture Opportunities to U.S. Investors
World.content:
Monrovia — Liberia has stepped up efforts to attract private capital from the United States and other international markets, presenting investment opportunities spanning mining, energy, agriculture, infrastructure, manufacturing and digital development at a high-level Liberia Investment Dialogue held on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly.

The investment roundtable, organized by Madam MacDella M. Cooper and co-organized by New Africa Capital, brought together senior Liberian government officials, advisers, private-sector investors and investment intermediaries to explore ways of converting Liberia’s economic opportunities into concrete investments.

Unlike conventional conferences centered on lengthy presentations and panel discussions, organizers structured the session as a direct investment dialogue focused on partnerships, follow-up actions and measurable results.

The message was clear: Liberia is seeking investors prepared to move beyond discussions and into implementation.

Finance and Development Planning Minister Augustine K. Ngafuan presented Liberia’s improving macroeconomic position, describing the country as stable, reforming and increasingly open to private-sector investment.

The International Monetary Fund has projected Liberia’s real GDP growth at about 5.5 percent in 2026, with mining, construction and manufacturing identified among the key drivers. The IMF also reported that inflation averaged about 4.5 percent during the first half of 2026, while the Liberian dollar remained broadly stable.

The government’s recent announcement that domestic revenue collections had surpassed US$1 billion was also highlighted as an indicator of growing fiscal capacity.

President Joseph Nyuma Boakai said the milestone marked the first time in Liberia’s history that domestic revenue had exceeded US$1 billion in a single year without borrowing or foreign aid.

For investors, government officials emphasized that the objective extends beyond economic growth to job creation and expansion of productive capacity through agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, electricity, roads, ports, logistics and digital infrastructure.

A major public-private partnership road project valued at more than US$360 million was cited as an example of the scale of private-sector participation the government hopes to attract.

Mining: Beyond Extraction

Mining emerged as one of the most significant areas of investment opportunity.

The Minister of Mines and Energy outlined Liberia’s established iron ore, gold and diamond industries while pointing to significant areas that remain underexplored because of gaps in detailed geological and geoscientific data.

Investors were encouraged to look beyond traditional mineral exports toward critical and industrial minerals, including tin, tantalum, lithium, rare earth elements, bauxite and coastal heavy mineral sands.

The government also stressed the need to move the mining sector up the value chain—from extraction and export toward processing, beneficiation, technology transfer and local industrial development.

The presentation positioned Liberia’s mineral resources not only as a source of government revenue but also as a potential foundation for broader industrialization.

Energy as a Gateway to Industrialization

Energy was repeatedly linked to Liberia’s industrial ambitions.

The government highlighted a national target of reaching approximately 75 percent electricity access by 2030, supported by an estimated 100,000 new connections annually.

Liberia’s hydropower and river potential, including opportunities along the St. Paul and Sindon River corridors, were presented as part of the country’s broader energy investment case.

Officials, however, acknowledged that expanding generation alone will not resolve Liberia’s electricity deficit.

Significant investment will also be required in transmission and distribution infrastructure to deliver electricity to communities, mines, factories and other major industrial users.

The investment pitch therefore extended beyond power generation to the entire electricity value chain.

Rail Infrastructure Takes Center Stage

Rail infrastructure was another major focus of the dialogue.

The approximately 240-kilometer Buchanan-Yekepa railway was presented as a strategic asset capable of supporting multiple mining operations and broader economic activity.

Government officials said Liberia is moving toward a National Rail Authority model intended to facilitate multi-user access to the railway.

The transition from the existing user-operator arrangement is expected to continue through 2029, with the stated objective of preventing the rail system from being effectively locked to a single mining operator and creating access for multiple users.

The discussion underscored the importance of transportation infrastructure to Liberia’s investment ambitions, particularly in the mining sector.

Agriculture: From Production to Processing

Agriculture also featured prominently in the discussions.

The Minister of Agriculture described the sector as one of Liberia’s largest potential engines of economic transformation, emphasizing opportunities across the agricultural value chain.

The discussions covered land access, agricultural financing, productivity, processing, storage, transportation and market access.

Government officials encouraged investors to look beyond primary agricultural production toward agro-processing and value addition, where greater employment and domestic economic benefits could potentially be generated.

A Push for Private Capital

The New York dialogue comes as the Liberian government intensifies engagement with international investors and development partners during the UN General Assembly period.

The government has increasingly emphasized electricity, infrastructure, private-sector growth and responsible investment as central elements of its development strategy.

The dialogue was therefore intended to serve as a bridge between Liberia’s economic policy ambitions and the international capital needed to finance them.

Among those attending were Amb. Jeanine Coope, Chief Executive Officer of the Liberia Carbon Market Authority; Dr. Emmanuel K. Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director and CEO of the Environmental Protection Agency; Christian Dunbar, Senior Advisor to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai for Investment Financing and Development; Hon. Sekou M. Kromah, Minister of Posts and Telecommunications and Postmaster General; and Dr. Augustine Konneh, Senior Economic Advisor to President Boakai.

For the organizers, the central issue is no longer whether Liberia has investment opportunities, but how quickly those opportunities can be transformed into bankable projects, partnerships, financing commitments and jobs.

With mining, energy, agriculture, infrastructure, manufacturing and digital development all on the table, Liberia’s pitch to American and international investors was a call to move from interest to implementation.

Organizers said the success of the dialogue should ultimately be measured not by attendance, but by how many investment discussions translate into projects on the ground in Liberia.

World.title: Liberia: Chinese Nationals “Brutalize” Liberian Employee as Victim Alarms Over Selective Justice, Illegal Dismissal
World.content:
The accused and the victim

MONROVIA – The Ministry of Labour has launched a probe into reports of an alleged assault on a Liberian worker by two Chinese nationals in Congo Town, outside Monrovia.

By Obediah Johnson

Victim Francis Flomo was allegedly assaulted by his bosses, one Mr. Liu and another unidentified Chinese national at a local Chinese restaurant O’Cake located adjacent the Giant Gym in Congo Town, outside Monrovia.

In a detailed report submitted to the Ministry of Labour, a copy which is in the possession of Frontpage Africa, victim Francis was physically attacked and assaulted by his bosses for allegedly playing with his phone during working hours.

The report claimed that the alleged perpetrators used steel and stick to physically assault defenseless victim Francis.

Police Intervention

Following the alleged assault, police officers riding a motorbike while on their regular patrol were requested by other aggrieved employees to arrest the situation. According to the report, the LNP officers later took the victim and the accused to the Palace Police Station in Swankamore Community, Oldest Congo Town, around the SKD Boulevard Junction, outside Monrovia.

It added that while at the police station, several unidentified Chinese nationals stormed the area with another police officer. “Shortly after, the officer at the Charge of Quarters who was investigating the case allegedly changed his approach. Instead of treating Francis Flomo as a victim of assault, he charged all three persons — the two Chinese nationals AND the young Liberian Francis Flomo — for “Disorderly Conduct” and effectively threw the case out.”

The report maintained that victim Francis suffered a swollened hand as a result of the assault. It disclosed that the victim was immediately sacked by his Chinese bosses immediately after the case was threw out by the police.

It noted that the victim bosses also refused to pay his one month salary. “The central question this incident leaves is: How can two men jump on a defenseless young boy, beat him with objects, and then the victim himself is charged for disorderly conduct by the police?,” it stated.

The report divulged that the incident points to the abuse and exploitation of a Liberian employee by his foreign bosses in Liberia

It added that the situation also denies the victim the payment of his fair wage and a compromised justice system in the Liberian society.

Meanwhile, the victim is calling on government to investigate the alleged use of influence at the police station to turn a clear assault case into a disorderly conduct charge, thereby denying the victim justice.

“The family and community are now calling for a proper investigation into the matter by the Liberia National Police Professional Standards Division and the Ministry of Labour.”

Labour Inspector General Mr. John O. F. Kangbah reportedly led a team of LNP officers at the restaurant late Tuesday afternoon and requested the management to produce the accused Chinese nationals.

But the management reportedly failed to produce the accused. However, the Labour Inspector promised to shutdown the Chinese restaurant if management fails to produce the accused today Wednesday, September 23.

World.title: CBU, UCF sign MoU to build chemistry Laboratory
World.content:
The Copperbelt University and United Capital Fertilisers (UCF), a subsidiary of the Wonderful Group of Companies Limited, have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to undertake the construction of a state of the art chemical laboratory.

The agreement will also support training delivery, strengthen internship and scholarship programmes in chemical engineering, infrastructure, and other initiatives.

Speaking shortly after the signing ceremony, the Deputy Secretary to the Cabinet for Finance and Economic Development, Siakazongo Siakalenge commended the agreement between the two parties, noting that it highly aligns with the government’s economic and development vision through the ‘Growth Zambia Agenda’.

Mr Siakalenge emphasised that the MoU underscores the importance of developing a technologically skilled as well as an innovative human capital base, particularly in manufacturing and human capital with the aim of growing the economy.

“Especially in emerging sectors such as fertiliser manufacturing. Investing in human capital today lays the groundwork for a stronger, more resilient economy tomorrow,” he said.

He has since encouraged exploration of additional collaborations in advanced engineering and manufacturing sectors, which will contribute meaningfully to President Hakainde Hichilema’s developmental vision for Zambia.

In his welcome remarks, the Wonderful Group Chief Executive Officer, Roy Mwamba highlighted that the group is focused on the Grow Zambia Agenda aligned with the government’s vision, citing that the best investment is investing in people.

He mentioned that they had indicated earlier that their Urea fertiliser plant needed about 400 chemical engineers, disclosing that as the company continues to expand in just a few weeks to come the company will hold a groundbreaking ceremony of the expansion of the Amonia Urea plant at a cost of 1.5 billion United States dollars.

“With this expansion, there is a need for greater integration and Copperbelt University will collaborate closely with the group of companies to achieve this vision,” he said.

Earlier prior to the signing of the MoU, Copperbelt University Vice Chancellor Imasiku Nyambe stated that the MoU represents a crucial step in bridging the gap between universities and the industry.

Professor Nyambe commended the government for fostering collaboration between academia and industry, noting that President Hakainde Hichilema has continually championed such developments.

He also expressed gratitude to the Wonderful Group for their significant contributions to the country’s growth through substantial investments to be undertaken at the Copperbelt University.

Professor Nyambe, a beneficiary of industry scholarship further highlighted that CBU students will highly benefit from the increased professional exposure, scholarships and knowledge exchange to be implemented through the MoU.

“Opportunities, all of which will uplift their families, communities and the nation at large, he stated.

He noted that the construction of a chemical laboratory, a lecture theatre, and student accommodation will facilitate easier learning at the institution, emphasising that these developments are made possible by a supportive environment created through government efforts.

And Ministry of Education Permanent Secretary for Technical Services, Kelvin Mambwe, later emphasised that the MoU is highly significant, especially as it aligns with the Grow Zambia agenda.

Dr Mambwe highlighted that it provides students with valuable exposure to practical work opportunities, reaffirming the government’s commitment to education and initiatives that attach great importance to national development.

World.title: ZANACO launches 100m USD bond to support climate projects
World.content:
ZANACO has launched a 100 million United States dollars Medium-Term Note Programme that will support the issuance of sustainability bonds aimed at mobilising long-term capital for green and social projects in Zambia.

British Investment International (BII) offered technical support for the establishment of the bond Framework and has invested USS 15 million on the platform.

The programme will begin with an inaugural US$ 50 million sustainability bond, with further issuances expected over time.

The proceeds will be directed towards eligible projects in areas including renewable energy, climate-resilient agriculture, financial inclusion, affordable housing, healthcare, education and other initiatives with measurable environmental and social benefits.

Speaking at the launch at ZANACO Chief Executive officer Mukwandi Chibesakunda said the bank’s inaugural sustainability bond will go beyond raising capital, with proceeds expected to support climate resilience, economic growth and social development in Zambia.

Dr Chibesakunda said the bond, to be issued under ZANACO’s US$100 million medium-term note programme, has marked a shift from the bank’s earlier commitment to sustainable finance towards execution.

“At ZANACO, our purpose is anchored on our You First philosophy. It is a commitment that places our customers, communities and our country at the centre of every decision we make,” he said.

Dr Chibesakunda said the sustainability bond would create financing opportunities for farmers seeking to strengthen their resilience to climate change, entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) looking to expand, as well as communities in need of critical social infrastructure.

She said the initiative was particularly important amid growing climate-related risks facing Zambia and other parts of the world.

Under the sustainability bond programme, ZANACO intends to channel financing towards climate-smart agriculture, renewable energy, energy efficiency, financial inclusion for SMEs and critical social infrastructure.

And British International Investment (BII) Managing Director and Head of Africa Chris Chijiutomi said the transaction was aligned with BII’s new five-year strategy, which places emphasis on strengthening the local financial system.

“One of the priorities of our new strategy that we launched this year is to help strengthen local financial systems and mobilize more private capital,” Mr Chijiutomi said.

Mr Chijiutomi said development finance institutions such as BII could provide investment, but greater mobilisation of private capital was necessary to expand development financing in economies such as Zambia.

He described the sustainability bond as an important milestone for Zambia’s financial sector and said it had the potential to encourage additional local and international investors and contribute to the development of the country’s sustainable finance market.

Africa.

Meanwhile, British High Commissioner to Zambia Rebecca Terzeon said the transaction demonstrated the UK’s shift towards an investment-led approach to development partnerships.

Ms Terzeon said BII’s investment in ZANACO’s sustainability bond showed how UK-supported development finance could be combined with Zambian institutions to support commercially viable investments while delivering development outcomes.

“This is exactly what the UK means when we talk about donor to investor,” Ms Terzeon said, referring to the mobilisation of finance to help businesses grow, create jobs and strengthen Zambia’s economic resilience.

Lusaka Securities Exchange (LuSE) Chief Executive Officer Nicholas Kabaso said the issuance marked a new chapter for Zambia’s capital markets and described it as the first sustainability bond issued by a Zambian bank.

Mr Kabaso said the exchange would work with stakeholders to develop a pipeline of future thematic bond issuances, simplify the issuance process and standardise reporting and verification requirements.

And Securities and Exchange Commission Director of Policy Development and Market Mateyo Lungu said the transaction was consistent with Zambia’s Capital Markets Master Plan, which seeks to develop innovative financial products and deepen the contribution of capital markets to national development.

Green Economy and Environment Minister Gilbert Siame said government supports initiatives that mobilise capital for climate-resilient and sustainable development.

Dr Siame said sustainable finance is important in financing the country’s transition towards a greener and more resilient economy, adding that the government was working to create an enabling policy and regulatory environment for climate finance.

World.title: Kabwe Court puts defilement suspect on defence
World.content:
The Kabwe Magistrates’ Court has found a 24-year-old man with a case to answer in a matter in which he is charged with defilement.

Kabwe Resident Magistrate Sebastian Mwenya has since put Levy Tebulo on his defence after the prosecution closed its case.

This follows testimony from the State’s final key witness, gynecologist Wisdom Banda of Kabwe Central Hospital, who told the court that he examined the complainant and found an injury to the hymen.

Dr Banda testified that the medical findings were consistent with a penetrative vaginal injury.

After considering the evidence presented by the prosecution, Magistrate Mwenya ruled that the accused had a case to answer and directed him to begin his defence.

“I have gone through the evidence presented by the prosecution and find you with a case to answer, therefore, I put you on your defense,” ruled the court.

The court heard that Tebulo is alleged to have had unlawful carnal knowledge of a girl under the age of 16 between February 3rd and February 14th, 2026, in Kabwe District.

After being informed of his rights, Tebulo opted to give sworn evidence in his defence and indicated that he would not call any witnesses.

“I’m going to give you a chance to go and prepare for your defence, and I wish you good luck,” said Magistrate Mwenya.

The matter has been adjourned to October 1st, 2026, for commencement of the defence case whilst Tebulo remains in custody.

World.title: Masebo’s petition case commences in the Lusaka High Court
World.content:
The petition hearing where former Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Sylvia Masebo, is challenging the election of Annita Kamanga as Chongwe East Member of Parliament has commenced.

Ms Masebo, who stood on the United Party for National Development (UPND) ticket contends in her petition Ms Kamanga’s pre-election campaigns were characterised by conduct that contravened the Electoral Process Act and its Code of Conduct.

Robert Simeza is the lead lawyer for Ms Masebo in the petition case where 20 witnesses have been lined up by the petitioner to testify in court.

Four witnesses have so far testified that they were attacked by suspected supporters of the respondent, who in this case is Ms Kamanga.

One witness testified that he sustained body injuries as a result of the attack and that a medical report was issued at the hospital.

Both, the petitioner Ms Masebo and the respondent, Ms Kamanga, who stoon as an Independent parliamentary candidate, were at Lusaka High Court to follow proceedings.

Ms Masebo polled 6,798 votes against Annita Kamanga’s 16,058 votes in the August 13, 2026 general elections.

Some UPND supporters gathered at the Lusaka High Court grounds to show solidarity to the petitioner.

World.title: Chipangali drug stock stable
World.content:
The Department of Health Services in Chipangali District in Eastern Province has said that clinical services in the district are currently stable with drug availability above 89 percent.

Speaking during a senior management meeting held at the District Administration Office, District Clinical Care Officer Geoffrey Ndhlovu said the 89 percent drug availability in the district reflects adequate essential medicines, essential supplies and vaccines.

Mr Ndhlovu added that three more health facilities have been opened in the district bringing the total number of health facilities to 27.

“We have opened three more health facilities in the district namely Nguluwe, Nyauzi, and Kapatamoyo health facilities which are already providing outpatient health services,” Mr Ndhlovu said.

He however mentioned that the new facilities are not fully operational as they still face challenges relating to inadequate essential equipment and supplies.

“Currently we are not conducting deliveries in these new facilities, because the equipment we have can only support outpatient care,” he said.

He said the department has since requested for equipment through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), noting that the request was approved and awaits funding.

Meanwhile Mr Ndhlovu disclosed that the department has conducted 297 cesarean section surgeries from October 2025 to date.

He said the surgeries were conducted within the district at Muzeyi Clinic.

Mr Ndhlovu reported that all the surgeries were successful without any complications.

“All women who may require advanced care are referred to Muzeyi, so that they wait to deliver safely. So, the facility sometimes has inadequate space. In view of this, we are also lobbying for construction of a mother’s shelter and ablution block so that our mothers are well kept as they wait to be operated on,” Mr Ndhlovu said.

World.title: Zambia, European Union reaffirm longstanding partnership
World.content:
Zambia and the European Union (EU) have reaffirmed their longstanding partnership, underscoring shared commitments to democracy, rule of law, and economic cooperation.

European Commissioner for International Partnerships, Jozef Síkela, has commended Zambia’s standing as a beacon of democracy and encouraged both sides to maintain respect for the rule of law while advancing a forward-looking partnership.

This is according to a statement issued to the media in Lusaka by First Secretary for Press and Public Relations at Zambia’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations, Namatama Njekwa.

Ms Njekwa revealed that the remarks were made during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA81).

She noted that the EU reaffirmed its support for Zambia’s leadership in promoting multilateralism and the rules-based international order, while both parties agreed to deepen cooperation through investment, value addition, and initiatives aligned with the Grow Zambia Agenda.

She added that Mr Síkela highlighted Africa’s critical role in electric-vehicle battery and mineral value chains, with Zambia welcoming the EU’s Global Gateway initiative and development cooperation, including budget support of approximately EUR 110 million.

Ms Njekwa further stated that both sides emphasised that post-election developments should not detract from opportunities to strengthen economic ties.

She indicated that the meeting also reaffirmed collaboration on international peace and security, with both Zambia and the EU pledging to prioritise the consolidation of their partnership.

World.title: Nalolo’s Kaunga Lueti in water blues
World.content:
Nalolo District Commissioner Namatama Mupo has called for an urgent solution to the water crisis that has hit Kaunga Lueti community in Nalolo West Bank.

The media reports that the water reticulation plant at Kaunga Lueti Primary School, which services about 4,000 people, has been non-operational since the first week of September, 2026.

An assessment conducted by Nalolo Town Council after the community reported the matter, established that the pump controller and surge protective device need replacement.

Speaking during an urgent District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) meeting held at her office, Mrs Mupo said water issues are critical and require urgent attention as they affect the community and public institutions such as Kaunga Lueti Primary School, the health post and the police post.

“Water is life and as such, there is a need to tackle water issues with urgency, as delaying would lead to waterborne diseases and possible closure of the school where the water scheme is located,” said Mrs Mupo.

She has since directed the DDMC to write to the local authority to request for funds under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit (DMMU) component so that the water plant can be repaired.

And District Disaster Management Officer Annie Phiri assured the District Commissioner that documents requesting for funds will be prepared and once the funds are available, the committee will ensure that the water plant is worked so that the Kaunga Lueti community can have access to clean and safe water again.

Ms Phiri said the water plant is important as it is the only source of clean and safe water in the area, hence the need to find a solution as soon as possible.

Meanwhile, District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) Muyoba Liwakala said there is a need to set up a committee that will be in charge of the water scheme to ensure regular maintenance and avoid future breakdowns.

Mr Liwakala said the water reticulation facility is a huge investment that needs to be maintained at all times so that it can stand the test of time.

The District Commissioner also called on the Department of Agriculture to intensify El Nino sensitisation meetings so that farmers are well prepared and take preventive measures before disasters strike.

Mrs Mupo said following the rains experienced in some parts of the province, some farmers are confused on whether to start farming or wait for the usual planting period.

Responding to the DC, Acting Nalolo District Agricultural Coordinator (DACO) Patience Munalula said El Nino sensitisation meetings are ongoing and Agriculture Camp Officers are currently engaging farmers on venturing into smart agriculture and what to expect in view of climate change effects.

World.title: Silondwa wins Discover golf title
World.content:
Nkana golfer Kedrick Silondwa survived a three-way countback to win the Discover Insurance Golf Championship at Nkana Golf Club.

Silondwa, off handicap 12, carded 42 points to top a tightly contested field and walk away with a K3,500 voucher and the overall winner’s trophy.

“It’s been a great day of golf and I can only thank Discover Insurance for deciding to spend their fourth birthday with us. We hope to see more of you around. To the players, I wish to thank you as well. It was really competitive and you made me work hard for my reward,” he said after receiving the trophy.

In the men’s category, Sam Mpundu also finished with 42 points to claim top prize on countback ahead of Tashbekov Djurabek, with Frank Masaka third on 35 points.

In the women’s category, Gladys Mudenda won outright with 35 points, one better than Emma Makoni, while Elisa Manjolo was third on 33 points.

In the subsidiary prizes, Mpundu won the nearest-to-the-pin award, Wiaan Le Roux won the longest drive in the men’s section, while Manjolo took the women’s award.

Discover Insurance Vice-Board Chairperson Chisuwo Hamwela said the tournament was organised to commemorate the company’s fourth anniversary and support the Grow Zambia Agenda.

“We are happy to celebrate our fourth anniversary with the business community and it’s been great. But on top of that, we are game for the Grow Zambia Agenda and while it is important to grow the economy, it is equally important to expand growth to other areas,” Hamwela said.

“Nkana Golf Club is doing that with its efforts with the junior golf programme and we are more than happy to supplement that with donations to the junior programme. At this tournament, we held a junior event and donated prizes in the form of school bags and more than a hundred golf balls.”

In the junior chipping contest, Peter Kasongo, Blessing Mambwe and Grace Washeni emerged winners.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 23, 2026
World.content:
UN Chief Says Security Council Remains 'Unjust' Without Permanent African Seat

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has said the lack of a permanent seat for Africa on the UN Security Council is no longer defensible. Guterres made the remarks on Tuesday, September 22, while addressing the opening of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York - his final General Assembly opening address before his term ends on December 31, 2026.

"The Security Council was designed in the aftermath of World War II. But the world has fundamentally changed since then," Guterres told world leaders. He pointed specifically to Africa, saying that most of the continent was under colonial rule when the United Nations was established in 1945. His remarks come amid renewed global momentum around UN reform.



Eleven Killed in Mass Shooting in South Africa's KZN Province

Eleven people were killed and three others wounded after gunmen opened fire inside a residence in KwaMakhutha, south of Durban, on Tuesday night. Police reported that 13 men and a pregnant woman were attending a gathering in the Ziko area when three men arrived and opened fire. Ten victims, including the woman, died at the scene, while another succumbed to injuries in the hospital.

A police spokesperson confirmed that a manhunt is underway. Preliminary investigations indicate that several victims were previously known to Crime Intelligence regarding alleged illegal activities, though further details are being withheld to protect the ongoing investigation.

Niger's Junta Strips Five More Exiled Critics of Nationality

Niger's military junta has stripped five more exiled opposition figures of their citizenship, extending a controversial policy targeting critics of the administration, according to Human Rights Watch (HRW).

On September 17, 2026, junta leader Abdourahamane Tiani signed a decree revoking the nationality of the prominent Nigeriens living abroad. The decree stems from a 2024 executive order establishing a national terrorism database - a tool HRW criticizes for overbroad inclusion criteria, inadequate due process, and heightened risks of statelessness.

"The Niger junta has been depriving perceived political opponents of their nationality without meaningful due process, and contrary to Niger's obligations to prevent statelessness and protect fundamental rights," said Ilaria Allegrozzi, HRW's senior Sahel researcher.

Moroccans Head to Polls as Youth Unemployment Takes Center Stage

More than 15 million registered voters are set to elect members of Morocco's lower house of parliament. Wednesday's vote marks the first general election since a Gen Z-led protest movement brought thousands of young people into the streets last year to demand employment, improved healthcare and education, and relief from the rising cost of living.

Frustrations resurfaced in July when large numbers of young Moroccans attempted to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in search of work in Europe. Consequently, job creation and youth engagement have become central campaign promises across the political spectrum. However, while some young voters see the ballot box as a vehicle for reform, others express little confidence that the outcome will improve their daily lives.

Close 

U.S. to End Health Funding in Zimbabwe After Rejected Deal

The U.S. government will conclude its health assistance programs in Zimbabwe at the end of September following Harare's decision to decline a new bilateral funding model over data privacy concerns. Over the last two decades, the U.S. has played a key role in supporting Zimbabwean public health, including funding antiretroviral drugs (ARVs) for HIV treatment and stipends for healthcare workers.

"Because of that, Zimbabwe has achieved HIV epidemic control, with more than 95% of people living with HIV receiving treatment," said U.S. Ambassador Pamela Tremont, emphasizing that sustaining those gains must remain the primary goal under local leadership.

Ambassador Tremont said the U.S. has updated its global health delivery model around a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) framework requiring co-investment from host nations. Following Zimbabwe's rejection of the bilateral agreement, U.S.-funded health operations are set to wrap up on September 30.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Toll Exceeds 3,700 Deaths
World.content:
More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and "the first encouraging signs of progress" are now being seen.

In an update, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said that in the last 21 days, cases of infection fell by approximately 26 per cent in province of Ituri and by 15 per cent in the province of Haut Uele.

However, over the same period, North Kivu province recorded a 73 per cent increase, clearly indicating that the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has a different transmission profile in the seven affected provinces where it has been confirmed.

"While cases and theft are declining in some provinces, they continue to rise in others," said WHO Regional Emergency Director for Africa, Dr Marie Roseline Belizaire.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Those patterns show the outbreak is still not under control and remain spread across a wide geographic area. One of our greatest concerns is that too many people are still dying before reaching treatment."

Dr Belizaire explained that around one in three new cases of infection are only identified after people have died outside Ebola treatment centres, in the community.

"These are lives that could potentially have been saved through earlier detection and timely access to care," the WHO medic said, adding that every death in the community increases the risk of further transmission among family members, caregivers and others involved in traditional burial practices.

Children at most risk

Although adults account for most confirmed cases of infection, children under five have the highest case fatality rate, at more than 60 per cent, compared with approximately 40 per cent among adults.

Ebola infections in children under 5 are proving very hard to detect because they "can't necessarily explain their signs and symptoms as well as adults, and the presentation (of symptoms) may be confusing," added WHO medic Dr. Catherine Smallwood.

Youngsters also account for a disproportionate share of those dying in the community and in health facilities where Ebola is not diagnosed in time.

"We must do more to identify sick children earlier and ensure that they receive appropriate treatment without delay; early detection save lives," Dr Belizaire stressed, in an online update from Kinshasa.

Ongoing efforts to ramp up the disease outbreak response have contributed to higher success in tracing contacts of infected people, now at almost 88 per cent.

But "too many new infections are still being detected without a known epidemiological link; closing the surveillance gap is essential, and we are to detect cases earlier, trace their contact, and interrupt every chain of transmission," Dr. Belizaire insisted.

Expanding response

The UN agency and partners continue to expand their reach across affected provinces, with nearly 1,400 treatment and isolation beds across 49 Ebola treatment centres. In addition, there are 25 laboratories capable of processing up to 2,500 tests every day.

However, infrastructure alone will not stop the outbreak, she said.

"Our response is no longer simply about the scaling up everywhere; it is about directing teams, expertise, and resources to the areas where transmission is greatest and where the risks are high."

Speaking from Beni in North Kivu, WHO's Dr Smallwood highlighted the "massive mobilization" of responders in recent weeks, in response to the worrying spread of infection in rural areas of DR Congo.

However, although new health centre or Ebola treatment centre beds are becoming available every day, "the big challenge now is finding the partners that can work within those health facilities...The human resources gap is one of the biggest gaps," Dr. Smallwood explained.

The WHO medic underscored the need to shift the response "from the big urban centres of Beni, Butembo and Katwa in North Kivu to the province's remote villages.

"Distances are really long and it takes a long time for patients to be referred into the urban centres," she said. "So, we really need to put priority on decentralising the response to where the cases are into the villages and into the local areas."

Ebola facts

Close 

Ebola disease is a severe, often fatal illness affecting humans and other primates.

The virus is transmitted to people from wild animals (such as fruit bats, porcupines and non-human primates); it then spreads in the human population through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs or other bodily fluids of infected people. It can also be transmitted by contact with bedding or clothing contaminated with these fluids.

The average Ebola disease case fatality rate is around 50 per cent, according to WHO. Case fatality rates have varied from 25 to 90 per cent in past outbreaks.

The first Ebola disease outbreaks occurred in remote villages in Central Africa, near tropical rainforests.

The 2014-2016 Ebola virus disease outbreak in West Africa was the largest and most complex Ebola outbreak since the virus was first discovered in 1976.

There were more cases and deaths in this outbreak than all others combined. It also spread between countries, starting in Guinea then moving across land borders to Sierra Leone and Liberia.

World.title: Malawi: Malawi Puts $1,000 Limit On Cash in Your Pocket
World.content:
Malawians and visitors alike are facing a dramatic new crackdown on cash, after the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) slapped sweeping restrictions on the physical possession and movement of foreign currency -- with anyone caught holding more than $1,000 without central bank permission now at risk.

Under the astonishing new rules, anyone physically carrying more than US$1,000 -- roughly K1.75 million -- or its equivalent in another foreign currency, must first secure the blessing of the central bank, or risk falling foul of the law.

The eyebrow-raising restrictions are laid out in the Foreign Exchange (Limit on Physical Possession of Foreign Currency) Notice, 2026, quietly issued by the central bank on September 7 and published in the Malawi Government Gazette on September 18.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Anyone attempting to take or send more than $1,000 out of the country will now be forced to prove the cash was purchased from an authorised dealer -- or otherwise obtain explicit permission from the RBM before crossing the border.

It doesn't stop there. The central bank has also clamped down on how much Malawi kwacha can leave the country without its say-so.

Cross-border traders will be permitted to carry kwacha equivalent to up to $5,000, but ordinary travellers face a far stingier cap -- just $100.

The dramatic tightening of the rules comes as Malawi grapples with a punishing foreign exchange shortage and a booming black market in forex, with authorities apparently determined to choke off unofficial cash flows once and for all.

Travellers, businesses and everyday citizens dealing in foreign currency now find themselves under far greater scrutiny, particularly when large sums of cash are involved.

The RBM has left no room for ambiguity, making clear that any foreign currency exceeding the new threshold simply cannot be carried across Malawi's borders without the correct paperwork or central bank sign-off.

The crackdown lands against the backdrop of Malawi's long-running forex crisis, which has left the country starved of hard currency, disrupted access to vital imports, and piled pressure on the wider economy.

In effect, the central bank has handed itself sweeping new powers to monitor exactly how much physical foreign currency is leaving Malawi -- and to demand answers over where that money came from.

For everyday travellers, it's the eye-catching $1,000 possession threshold that will raise the most eyebrows, while cross-border traders must now operate within a separate $5,000 kwacha limit.

The bombshell new rules mark a major escalation in Malawi's battle to rein in foreign currency flows, as authorities scramble to contain a forex crisis that shows little sign of easing.

World.title: ‘Miracle on the Hudson’ hero Sully Sullenberger reveals Alzheimer’s warning signs he missed years ago
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger, the former airline pilot celebrated worldwide for safely landing US Airways Flight 1549 on the Hudson River in 2009, is taking on a new mission to raise awareness about the early signs of Alzheimer’s disease.

Sullenberger, who was diagnosed with the disease in August 2025, spoke on "Good Morning America" alongside his wife, Lorrie, to share their personal experience with the condition.

The couple revealed several subtle shifts in routine and behavior that began surfacing several years before he received an official medical evaluation.

'MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON' HERO CAPTAIN 'SULLY' SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER'S DIAGNOSIS

Reflecting on the timeline leading up to her husband's formal assessment, Lorrie Sullenberger noted that small adjustments in everyday life slowly pointed toward a bigger shift.

"A lot of what I think people see in the news are late-stage Alzheimer's symptoms. And so in the very beginning, they are so subtle. And my advice to someone would be, it's what's unusual for your person," she shared, emphasizing how early symptoms often manifest gradually rather than abruptly.

TV NEWS ANCHORMAN REVEALS HE HAS ALZHEIMER'S DURING FINAL NIGHT HELMING BROADCAST

Public understanding of Alzheimer’s disease frequently focuses on these late-stage symptoms, such as pronounced memory loss, severe disorientation or difficulty managing basic daily routines. However, medical experts say early-stage cognitive decline can be much harder to spot.

"One of the first things I noticed was that it was harder and harder to remember people’s names, even people we knew," Sullenberger said. "That’s still an issue. Just forgetting things that I normally wouldn’t. Or repeating myself, not realizing that I just said that an hour ago."

Early indicators of Alzheimer's often present as mild cognitive impairment or subtle changes tailored to an individual’s normal baseline, according to health resources like Cleveland Clinic.

These can include misplacing everyday items, mild difficulty finding the right words during conversations, subtle changes in mood or executive function, or taking slightly longer to complete familiar tasks.

CLICK HERE TO 

Because these early shifts often mimic normal signs of aging, loved ones are usually the first to notice small anomalies in behavior.

"I’ve gone through harder things than this before," Sullenberger said in the interview.

The former pilot may be best known for successfully performing the "Miracle on the Hudson" in January 2009.

After US Airways Flight 1549 suffered a dual engine failure following a bird strike shortly after taking off from New York's LaGuardia Airport, Sullenberger drew on decades of flight experience to glide the Airbus A320 onto the frigid Hudson River, where all 155 passengers and crew survived, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The emergency landing made Sullenberger an internationally recognized public figure and became known as the "Miracle on the Hudson."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Lorrie Sullenberger noted that family members should trust their instincts when something feels off, advising that the key lies in identifying "what's unusual for your person."

"I’ve gone through harder things than this before."

The Sullenbergers stressed that acknowledging potential early symptoms and seeking evaluation can profoundly impact a patient’s journey. While there is no cure for Alzheimer’s, early detection allows individuals and families to explore emerging treatment options, join clinical trials, adopt lifestyle modifications and plan for the future.

"An early diagnosis is so critically important," Sullenberger said. "If you have doubts, get tested. Because the sooner you act, the more options there are, the better the outcome is likely to be."

World.title: America's best national parks for fall revealed — plus the NPS director's personal picks
World.content:
Year after year, the Great Smoky Mountains are America’s most-visited national park. Turns out, fall might be its most impressive season.

A new study ranking the best national parks for an autumn getaway put the Smokies at No. 1, ahead of Acadia, Shenandoah, Rocky Mountain and Grand Teton.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The research, conducted by Sudoku Bliss, analyzed National Park Service visitation data from September through November between 2021 and 2025, along with Google ratings and reviews. Great Smoky Mountains earned the top overall score after welcoming nearly 19 million fall visitors over that five-year span.

And if you're looking for a second opinion, the acting director of the National Park Service happens to agree.

During a recent interview with OutKick OutDoors, Jessica Bowron named the Smokies and the Blue Ridge Parkway when asked where she'd send someone chasing fall colors.

6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK

"I would send them to the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a close partner being the Great Smoky Mountains National Park," Bowron said. "Two really incredible parks to see the fall colors."

Great Smoky Mountains leads the fall rankings

The Smokies finished well ahead of the rest of the field in the study, with a fall score of 94.7.

Acadia National Park in Maine ranked second at 86.6, followed by Virginia's Shenandoah National Park at 76.0, Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado at 74.1 and Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming at 72.9.

The rest of the top 10 included Yosemite, Zion, Yellowstone, Cuyahoga Valley and New River Gorge.

HERE'S HOW TO DO THE SMOKY MOUNTAINS WITHOUT TRAFFIC AND CROWDS

And the rankings weren't based on visitor totals alone.

The study weighted total fall visits, total visitor hours, Google ratings and the number of reviews containing autumn-related language. Shenandoah, for example, had fewer visitors than several parks ranked below it, but 18.4% of its Google reviews mentioned fall — the highest share among the top 10.

So while the Smokies won on sheer popularity and overall score, the list includes everything from classic East Coast leaf-peeping destinations to red rocks and wildlife-heavy Western parks.

More of the Blue Ridge Parkway is coming back

Bowron also shared some good news for travelers planning a trip along the Blue Ridge Parkway this fall.

"Just within the next few weeks, we should be reopening additional sections of the parkway that were hit by Hurricane Helene just two years ago," Bowron told OutKick OutDoors. "We're really excited to get that work wrapped up and see visitors back on that parkway."

For anyone planning a fall road trip through the region, that's certainly worth keeping an eye on.

Want something a little less obvious?

If your idea of a relaxing fall weekend does not involve joining everybody else in America at the Smokies, Bowron also offered a more under-the-radar option.

Her pick: Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park.

And this wasn't just an answer pulled from a list.

"I was there just yesterday, actually, we went for a hike on the C&O Canal with my husband and my daughter," Bowron said.

She highlighted the more than 100-mile towpath running from the Washington, D.C., area into Western Maryland, with opportunities to hike, bike and branch off onto other trails along the way.

"I don't know that folks recognize what an incredible resource that is," she said.

That might be the better play for travelers who want fall scenery without traffic and crowds.

Don't sleep on national parks in winter

Fall gets most of the attention this time of year, but Bowron said winter opens up a completely different set of possibilities.

For warmer-weather trips, she pointed to places like Death Valley, Mojave, Everglades and Saguaro — parks that can be far more comfortable once summer temperatures disappear.

And for travelers who actually want the snow, there are plenty of options for that, too. The Rockies offer snowshoeing and cross-country skiing, while Utah's Bryce Canyon National Park is a great place for winter hiking, snowshoeing and skiing among its snow-covered red rock formations.

Bowron warned, though, to check park websites for road closures, weather conditions and available facilities before you go.

"Days are going to be shorter. Conditions are going to change," Bowron said. "They're going to be very different from what you might expect in the summer."



So don’t be sad your summer vacation has come to an end. Because for the national parks, now is when things start getting really good.

A Massachusetts restaurant owner allegedly beat two teenage dine-and-dashers and pointed a gun at a larger group that gathered after he chased the pair down when they skipped out on their bill last week, authorities said.

Nadim Kashouh, 62, chased the teens – a 17-year-old girl and Javonnie Lee, 18 – after the pair darted out of Nadim’s Downtown Mediterranean Grill on Friday evening without paying their $92.40 bill, the Boston Globe reported.

JIMMY JOHN'S EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF OPENING FIRE ON CAR, SHOOTING 14-YEAR-OLD GIRL IN LEG: POLICE

Kashouh, an immigrant from Lebanon who came to the United States in 1990, allegedly grabbed the girl's phone and demanded they pay. He then elbowed the girl and punched Lee in the face, the Springfield Police Department said.

NYC ALLEGED DINE-AND-DASH INFLUENCER PEI CHUNG EVICTED FROM LUXURY APARTMENT AS SHE SIT SIN JAIL

"He maintains his innocence and says he acted in self-defense. As this matter moves through the legal process, Mr. Kashouh looks forward to the opportunity to fully address the facts and circumstances surrounding the incident," the post states.

"Having just celebrated over 25 years serving the Springfield community, Mr. Kashouh is incredibly grateful for the many clients, guests, friends, and community members who have reached out and continued to support him and Nadim’s," it continued. "I have known Nadim to be respectful, fair, calm, and incredibly hardworking," Maureen Pinette, who worked for him between 2012 and 2014, wrote on Facebook. "I've watched him deal with difficult situations and difficult people, and I have never known him to be someone who simply loses his cool."

"I see so much of Nadim in both of his children—the love, the loyalty, the work ethic, and the way they show up for the people around them," she added. World.title: Christian nurse says Oregon hospital tried to force employee group to go ‘interfaith’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Christian nurse at Oregon Health & Science University Hospital (OHSU) says administrators initially refused to approve her employee group unless she removed prayer, Bible study and other religious activities and changed it from a Christian group to an interfaith organization.

Suzie Logue said she created the group in early 2025 after connecting with other Christian employees who wanted a place to pray, study Scripture and encourage one another during difficult shifts. She says OHSU told her the group could be approved only if it removed its religious elements and said it could not use hospital resources or campus buildings.

"I naturally wrote back and said, ‘No, we're a Christian group. We would like to be allowed to pray and do Bible study and do these other worship activities using campus resources,’" Logue told Fox News Digital in an interview on Tuesday.

CHRISTIAN COP IN UK SUSPENDED FOR ASKING QUESTIONS ABOUT ISLAM DURING DEI TRAINING WINS SETTLEMENT

Logue said the hospital told her the group couldn't use any campus resources or campus buildings even when other religious groups were being allowed to do so.

"When I said, ‘What policy are we citing here? Why can't we do this?,’ I was met with silence," Logue said. "And when I kept pushing over the weeks, they wrote back to me and said, ‘Well, your charter is being reviewed now by hospital legal,’ and that is when I reached out to First Liberty."

CONNECTICUT BARS NATIVITY DISPLAY IN STATE CAPITOL BECAUSE IT'S 'RELIGIOUS,' LAWSUIT THREAT SAYS

Logue said she was shocked by what she viewed as the hospital’s casual handling of the situation. She said other religious employee groups were permitted to use campus facilities for prayer and worship, while she received little explanation for why the Christian group was treated differently.

After Logue contacted First Liberty Institute, the organization sent OHSU a demand letter. Logue says the hospital ultimately approved the group as Christian and allowed it to use hospital resources for prayer and worship.

CHRISTIAN SCHOOL CHAPLAIN WINS SETTLEMENT AFTER FIRING OVER LGBTQ SERMON

Logue says the group has since grown rapidly through word of mouth, giving Christian employees a support network inside the hospital.

"Part of the reason I wanted to start the group is because, I was connecting with other Christians at the hospital," Logue said. "As you can imagine, Portland and working in Portland can be a pretty tough place to be a Christian. And I was starting to connect with other Christians just in my daily work, and they'd say, ‘Oh my gosh, it's so nice to know there's other, other Christians here. We should try and get together sometimes just for encouragement.’"

"And so what we've seen come out of this group, it's interesting because even despite the challenges we faced getting this group started, it has grown exponentially, a lot of, by word of mouth, because we lack some visibility, but, a lot of people find that there's more light, they feel like when they go to their shift because they know there's someone they can connect with mid-shift if they have a really difficult patient situation," she said.

Cliff Martin, senior counsel at First Liberty, told Fox News Digital in a statement on Wednesday that, "Federal law mandates that employees of all faiths be respected in the workplace. Even so, OHSU displayed a clear pattern of discrimination and hostility toward Ms. Logue's Christian employee resource group by denying them visibility on the company website, companywide messaging, equal stipend payment, and fair descriptions of religious holidays."

Martin added, "We are happy to say that since July, the issues have mostly been resolved, and the Christian resource group should receive the same support every other group receives."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In a statement to Fox News Digital, OHSU said, "Employee Resource Groups are OHSU-sponsored and employee-managed groups. ERGs provide opportunities for career development, social support, networking, mentoring, community participation, cultural awareness and employee engagement. There are 15 ERGs at OHSU, including the Christian ERG, which was formed in 2025."

"Per OHSU policy, any group of at least three employees may request to be considered to form a new ERG," the hospital continued. "Emerging ERGs must identify potential goals of the group and craft a mission statement. The mission statement and goals must be reviewed and may need to be adapted to align with OHSU policies prior to approval."

The hospital added, "Each ERG operates with institutional support, and recognition entitles access to institution-owned or - controlled facilities for meetings and events, in accordance with policy. To maintain recognition, an ERG shall serve to build a positive and inclusive environment, and remain in compliance with OHSU policies."
