World.title: Who is skipping the UN General Assembly — and why
World.content:
Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, Friedrich Merz, Giorgia Meloni and Mahmoud Abbas are among more than 50 leaders who won't make it to the UN General Assembly. Their reasons range from illness and domestic affairs to holidays.

Few world leaders would miss a stage like the United Nations General Assembly. Donald Trump, Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Emmanuel Macron are among those in New York for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly — or UNGA81 for short — where the speeches from the green marble lectern make headlines around the globe.

That makes the no-shows all the more surprising. Here is a look at some of the leaders staying away — and why.

Germany: Friedrich Merz

The German chancellor, in his second year in office, would like to be much more present on the international stage and has described himself as a "foreign-policy chancellor." But domestic politics have been keeping him busy. Three German states held parliamentary elections in September and Friedrich Merz is under more pressure as chancellor and leader of the Christian Democrats (CDU) than ever before. In Saxony-Anhalt and Berlin, the CDU was firmly voted out of office, while in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern it failed to enter the state parliament at all — a first since the founding of the Federal Republic of Germany.

Merz is in crisis-management mode at home and seems to want to prevent his opponents from planning a revolt in his absence. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul will speak in his place.

Not the time for foreign trips: Chancellor Friedrich Merz Image: Fabrizio Bensch/REUTERS

Italy: Giorgia Meloni

Italy's prime minister is in a considerably stronger position than Merz but has said she needs to deal with domestic matters this week. After the NATO summit in early July, Giorgia Meloni said she had just returned from several international summits and had to tackle various issues, including some pending within Italy. She pointed out that Merz had also been absent in 2025 - she too is sending her foreign minister, Antonio Tajani.

Keeping her focus on domestic affairs: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni Image: Stefano Costantino/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance

South Africa: Cyril Ramaphosa

The South African president has also just attended an international summit — the BRICS summit in India. He said he would not attend the UN General Assembly for health reasons: medics advised him to take time to rest and recover. His office did not disclose details about his condition. South Africa will also be represented at the UN lectern by Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola.

Resting after a busy travel schedule: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa (pictured here with Indian Minister Jayant Chaudhary) Image: ANI

Egypt: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi

Along with Africa's largest economy, the second- and third-largest economies on the continent are also not sending their presidents to New York: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi is being represented by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly. Al-Sisi's office did not give a reason for his absence. During his first years in office, from 2014 onward, he regularly attended the UN General Assembly. In 2020, the event was held online because of the coronavirus pandemic and the following year it was a hybrid event, to which al-Sisi sent a pre-recorded video message. He has not attended since the General Assembly returned to in-person meetings.

Another BRICS participant: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi (second from left) is not going to New York Image: India's Ministry of External Affairs/Handout/REUTERS

Nigeria: Bola Tinubu

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu is the third influential African leader to miss this year's UN General Assembly. His spokesman was quoted by Nigerian media as saying the West African country would be "fully and effectively represented" by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Tinubu, meanwhile, is on vacation: He spent time in the UK in late August before traveling to France.

On vacation instead of at the UN: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu (front) with Vice President Kashim Shettima Image: Mubarak Aliyu

India: Narendra Modi

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is relatively rarely to be seen at UN General Assemblies. He last took the podium in 2021, since when the world's largest democracy has consistently sent Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar instead. According to Indian media outlets, Modi was reportedly listed as a speaker at this year's gathering before his plans changed. Why he decided not to attend is not known.

Unexplained absence: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Image: Alexander Kazakov/Sputnik/REUTERS

China: Xi Jinping

Chinese President Xi Jinping's absence is under international scrutiny this year. As this year's "High-Level Week" takes place, Xi will also be in the US but he will not be going to New York. Instead, he will head straight for Washington, some 300 kilometers away, for a full state visit, including a White House gala dinner and a military parade.

Although Beijing has not framed it this way, the timing suggests that Xi is prioritizing great power diplomacy over the United Nations' multilateral forum. Xi and Trump have serious bones of contention, including over trade relations, artificial intelligence and Taiwan's security situation.

Washington instead of New York: Chinese President Xi Jinping Image: Indian Foreign Ministry/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

Russia: Vladimir Putin

Russian President Vladimir Putin has also rarely stood at the iconic podium so it comes as little surprise that Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will once again speak for Russia this year. Putin ordered this by decree — and didn't offer a reason for his absence.

Skipping the General Assembly as usual: Russian President Vladimir Putin with Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov Image: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/REUTERS

Palestinian territories: Mahmoud Abbas

Mahmoud Abbashas clocked up far more UNGA experience than any of those listed above. The president of the Palestinian Authority (PA), who has been in office since 2005, was a regular until Donald Trump's second term.

But last year, the Trump administration denied him a diplomatic visa and has done so again this year.

Yet, under the 1947 UN Headquarters Agreement, the United States is committed to facilitating access to UN headquarters for foreign representatives. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, for example, is still due to speak in New York, despite the US having recently bombed Iran.

President of the Palestinian Authority Mahmoud Abbas appears on a screen at the 80th United Nations General Assembly Image: Jeenah Moon/REUTERS

In the case of the Palestinians, the US State Department recently said it was extending sanctions "that deny visas to members of the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Palestinian Authority." Abbas plans to address the assembled heads of state and government by video message, as he did last year.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
World.content:
The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

The socialist Left Party, which won the Berlin election on September 20, was the only major party on the ballot that said it would implement the results of Berlin's 2021 referendum, when 57.6% of Berliners voted to expropriate the apartments owned by real estate companies that own more than 3,000 units.

But the federal government has said they won't let it happen. So is it even possible? And how did we get here? DW explains:

What did the Left Party say about expropriation?

The Left Party was one of the main supporters of a successful, years-long grassroots campaign called "Deutsche Wohnen & Co. enteignen," ("Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen").

Deutsche Wohnen is a major property developer that owns over 140,000 units across Germany, and 100,000 in Berlin alone.

The campaign and the Left Party argued that by expropriating this and a handful of other major companies like it, the Berlin government could put some 270,000 apartments in Berlin into public ownership, and make them available at affordable rent prices. Other estimates put the number at around 240,000.

The argument struck a chord, as surveys showed that housing and rent prices were the biggest concerns for Berlin voters in the recent election.

Some 25% of rented property in Berlin is already in public ownership, through state-owned companies like Berlinovo. The expropriation measure would likely push that up to over 30%.

Berlin has space, so why is housing so expensive? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The 2021 referendum — what was the question and what came out of it?

The original referendum, held in September 2021, asked Berliners to vote yes or no on a five-point plan:

- Socializing the apartments owned by the major property companies

- Administration of the properties by a public-law entity

- Administration of the properties with participation from both city officials, renters, and local communities

- Ban on any re-privatization

- Compensation for the property companies "significantly below" the market value of the property

The referendum did not oblige the state government — at the time a coalition of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), the Greens, and the Left Party — to immediately implement the plan.

Instead, the then-SPD Mayor Franziska Giffey put together a 13-person expert commission, including former justice ministers and constitutional law experts. This was given the task of establishing whether the plan conformed with the German constitution, or Basic Law, and how the compensation could be organized.

In 2023, the commission concluded that expropriation was legal and possible, though budget questions still needed to be clarified.

By then, a new conservative-led government, headed by the Christian Democratic Union's (CDU) Kai Wegner, had been voted into office, and announced that it would not expropriate any real estate companies, regardless of what the commission said. At the same time, it emerged that the Berlin CDU was receiving hundreds of thousands of euros in donations from property companies.

Instead, the government said it would draw up a socialization law that would define the conditions for the socialization of property, while ruling out expropriation. A draft law was completed in December 2025.

The Deutsche Wohnen Enteignen campaign rejected this idea as pointless, and had in the meantime gathered legal experts to draw up its own expropriation and socialization law, and promised to start another campaign to force a referendum to implement that.

The legal basis for expropriation: Articles 14 and 15 of the German constitution

The original campaign founded its plan on articles 14 and 15 of the German Basic Law.

Article 14 says that, while the right to property is guaranteed, "expropriation shall only be permissible for the public good."

Article 15 states: "Land, natural resources and means of production may, for the purpose of nationalization, be transferred to public ownership or other forms of public enterprise by a law that determines the nature and extent of compensation."

As far as the campaigners are concerned, the law they have drawn up covers those two bases.

But, while Article 14 is implemented often enough (for example, when the state wants to build a new highway), Article 15 has never been implemented at all. It is new legal territory, and no one is quite sure what would happen if it were tried.

Some legal experts say the plan would contravene European law. Housing companies would almost certainly fight the measure in court and demand more compensation than the government is willing to offer.

Business Beyond: The global housing crisis To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

'Not happening' — Chancellor Merz vows to prevent expropriation

Chancellor Friedrich Merz responded to the Left Party's election victory immediately by promising to draw up a federal law banning state governments from expropriating property.

"It's not just about banning something here in Berlin," Merz said at a press conference in the aftermath of the Berlin election. "It's about sending a clear message to international investors, which is: There is no expropriation of private property in Germany."

However, it's unclear whether the federal government has the power to impose such a law. Germany's Constitutional Court once ruled that the federal government cannot pass a law simply to prevent a state from governing in the issues it wants.

What now?

The Left Party still has to enter into coalition negotiations to form a government in Berlin. Its most likely coalition partners are the SPD and the Greens, and given the opposition from the federal government and the massive controversy over the issue, the expropriation plan could become a major sticking point.

Whatever happens, the Left Party itself acknowledges that expropriation and socialization would take a while to put into practice, and it would be even longer before it had a measurable effect on Berlin's overall rents.

In the meantime, it has drawn up a number of laws that it hopes will tackle the problem more quickly, such as a rent cap.

In any case, Berliners themselves appear to have gone a little cold on the idea. Despite the Left's electoral success, a recent poll by infratest-dimap found that only 37% of Berliners are still in favor of expropriating real estate companies.

Edited by Rina Goldenberg

World.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
World.content:
Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

The third Asian Games gold medal looked as convincing as the first two, even if Yu Zidi insisted that: "It didn't feel easy at all. It was quite challenging."

On Wednesday, the 13-year-old Chinese swimmer broke the Games record for the third time to add the women's 400 meter individual medley title to her golds in the 200 meter medley and 200 meter butterfly. The three medals add to a bronze she won last year at the World Championships.

Even two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics, talk is turning to a potential rivalry with Canada's Summer McIntosh, 20, who herself finished fourth in the 2020 Olympics at 14 and won a world title at 15. As well as their remarkable talent, the pair's youth has raised some questions.

"The first reaction you have when you see something like this is you think, wow, there's a big career ahead," three-time open water swimming world champion Leonie Beck, of Germany, told DW.

Summer McIntosh is the only person to have swum faster than Yu Zidi in the 400 meters individual medley Image: Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press/picture alliance

"But I think maybe this is the problem. People around [the athlete], or maybe the media can create this pressure on a young talent. But just because you're really good and fast at this age, doesn't mean that your whole career will continue like this."

Early success is not always sustained

Beck has already retired from elite competition at 29 and swimming is a sport where athletes often peak early. Katie Ledecky, of the US, and Japan's Kyoko Iwasaki both won Olympic gold at 15 and Japan's Yumeki Kojima, 17, has been a home favorite at the Asian Games, winning a gold and silver in the pool.

While the temptation is to think of Yu as a prodigy, Beck said that to reach the level she has also requires extraordinary dedication and sacrifice.

"My first international competition was in 2011 [at age 14]. At that stage already, I was training eight times a week. You wake up at 5 a.m., by 6 you're in the pool, out at 7:30 so you're in school at 8:00, school until 1, going home, eating, maybe doing some homework, going back in the water training at 3. Then one hour of dry land [training], then in the water again and coming back home at 7 (p.m.). I had this when I was young too."

Leonie Beck won three world and three European titles Image: Oliver Weiken/dpa/picture alliance

Yu, who was discovered by chance by a swimming coach at a water park aged 6, admitted in an interview with state media Xinhua at an event in China in January that the workload takes its toll.

"Being in class all day and still having to train was really tiring," she said. "Sometimes I was so tired I could fall asleep even while eating."

While, for Beck, the sporting success made such struggles worthwhile, not all athletes who dedicate their childhoods to their sport reach the pinnacle. The German swimmer added that putting educational, physical and mental support structures in place is critical for sports that allow under-18s to compete.

"Sport psychology should start at a really young age because it should be normal, the same as physiotherapists," she said. "Especially at a young age, where sport should be also fun."

World Aquatics rules state that the minimum age for international championships is 14 but exceptions can be made for those fast enough, like Yu. While swimmers peak earlier than athletes in other sports, teenagers at the top level are not so unusual.

In football, Lamine Yamal won the Euros with Spain at 16, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, of India, made his debut in cricket's Indian Premier League at 13 and Nadia Comaneci, of Romania, became the first gymnast to be awarded a perfect 10 in the 1976 Olympics in Montreal aged 14.

Neither are young athletes a modern phenomenon. Dimitrios Loundras remains the youngest ever Olympic medallist, winning a bronze with the Greek gymnastics team in 1896.

While support structures in sport are improving, challenges remain, according to Rosemary Purcell, who played a part in the International Olympic Committee's (IOC) review into youth development ahead of the Paris Olympics in 2024.

"There are pretty stark differences between what we see in the community and in these elite youth athletes," Purcell told DW during those Games.

"Some sports do have a higher rate of eating disorders and body image disturbance in young athletes, but conversely, they may have lower rates of depression and anxiety than we would see in the community."

If you're good enough, you're old enough?

In general, sporting bodies tend to take the approach that if an athlete is good enough, they are old enough. Beck said, allied with the right support, this approach is correct.

"Every athlete has completely different development. Why should you take away the success of a young athlete just because she's young and successful in that age? In my opinion, you should give her the possibility to be successful at that age because maybe, who knows, in a later stage of her career, she will be not that successful. It's not just a solution to say: 'look, you're that age, you're not able to compete.'"

But she also cautioned that because success won't always last, young elite sportspeople should be helped to find a plan away from the pitch, pool or mat, something she struggled somewhat with post Paris 2024.

"You have this idea that, ok, I want to reach the Olympic Games, win this medal. So you have a structure of where to go, what to do. And at one point it's gone and you're like, ‘ok, but now what am I doing with my life? What do I want to reach? What are my goals?'

"It's really, really important that people are starting to think that, 'hey, we are also human beings and you should do something to have a life after the sport because the sport is not endless.'"

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Sánchez carga contra Ayuso y Almeida por la “tragedia social” del desahucio de Maricarmen: “Están más preocupados en comprar aticazos”
World.content:
El drama del desahucio de Maricarmen, de 87 años, ha generado una gran conmoción especialmente entre sectores progresistas, que apuntan al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez por no haber sido capaz de frenarlo. Preguntado por este asunto en Nueva York, en la habitual rueda de prensa durante la cumbre de la ONU en Nueva York, Sánchez ha responsabilizado directamente a la Comunidad de Madrid y el Ayuntamiento de Madrid, en manos del PP, contra los que ha cargado de forma dura porque cree que podían haber impedido el desahucio o buscar una solución alternativa y no han hecho nada. “El desahucio de Maricarmen es una tragedia social que no podemos aceptar como país”, ha arrancado el presidente, que llevaba preparado un largo discurso sobre este asunto que genera mucha tensión especialmente a sus potenciales votantes. “Hay que decir que hay dos administraciones competentes en la protección de personas vulnerables como Maricarmen, el Ayuntamiento de Madrid y la Comunidad de Madrid, que están mas preocupados en comprar aticazos de 200 metros de terraza pero han hecho caso omiso a una tragedia social que debería ser resuelta”.

Ante la pregunta de qué va a hacer el Gobierno, Sánchez ha insistido varias veces en que “no descarta nada”, pero no ha aclarado a qué se refería y después ha explicado que para cualquier movimiento debe contar con el Congreso, donde el escudo antidesahucios se ha rechazado dos veces con los votos de Junts, PP y Vox. “Si el parlamento hubiera aprobado el real decreto ley que el Gobierno llevó, hoy no tendríamos la situación que está viviendo Maricarmen, que ha estado 70 años pagando religiosamente su alquiler”, ha insistido.

Sánchez ha pedido a sus socios que reflexionen para aprobar un decreto de vivienda que sigue bloqueado en la negociación con Junts y Podemos, que tienen posiciones incompatibles. “El Gobierno va a dar una respuesta a esta tragedia social, pero pido altura de miras para sacar adelante este decreto de la vivienda. Mirando de manera más amplia podemos contribuir a resolver el problema de la vivienda. Necesitamos la ayuda del Parlamento para que un caso como el de Maricarmen no vuelva a suceder ni en Madrid ni en ningún otro lugar de España”, ha insistido.

Pero Sánchez sobre todo quería cargar con Isabel Díaz Ayuso y José Luis Martínez Almeida. “No olvidemos de quién son las responsabilidades, de ayuntamientos y comunidades autónomas. En Madrid tenemos a alguien que se vanagloria de que los fondos buitre pueden comprar las viviendas de protección. Estamos en política para que estas tragedias no sucedan. Esto no tiene color político. Esto es luchar contra la injusticia, contra la exclusión. Frente a la falta de compromiso de determinados gobiernos, tenemos que regular a nivel estatal. El Gobierno de España hará lo que esté en su mano para resolver este problema. No se puede soportar un desahucio de estas características por parte de un fondo buitre en una administración que se vanagloria de su entendimiento con los fondos buitre. Se compran un aticazo y no son capaces de mover un dedo por Maricarmen”, ha rematado.

El ministro de Cultura, Ernest Urtasun, de Sumar, ha exigido este miércoles que el próximo martes se lleve al Consejo de Ministros el Real Decreto Ley de Vivienda que, de haber estado en vigor, dijo, hubiera evitado el desahucio de Maricarmen. Sánchez ha insistido en esa idea, ha dicho que hay que “modificar la ley y reforzar la ley frente a estos casos” y ha asegurado que si el real decreto, tumbado en el Congreso, se hubiera respaldado antes del verano, “esto no habría pasado”, en referencia al desahucio de la mujer madrileña.

Sánchez ha calificado de “normal” su saludo con la presidenta venezolana, Delcy Rodríguez, este miércoles en el plenario de la Asamblea de la ONU. No ha comentado la decisión del juez Peinado de abrir juicio oral contra Begoña Gómez, y tampoco ha abundado sobre el escrito del expresidente socialista José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero dirigido al juez que lo mantiene investigado en el caso Plus Ultra, aunque le ha renovado su “apoyo”. Repreguntado sobre Zapatero, acerca de si debería entregar las joyas saudíes a Patrimonio Nacional, el jefe del Ejecutivo ha señalado: “Vamos a ver en qué se traduce esto, cuando tengamos esos datos, les daré respuestas”.

Sobre la crisis migratoria en Ceuta, Sánchez ha asegurado que ha hablado con varios líderes europeos y también de otros estados fuera de la Unión Europea: “Creo que sobre todo lo que he encontrado es mucha empatía, no solamente para con España, sino también para con estos migrantes”. El presidente ha destacado la inversión del Estado en la ciudad autónoma. “Son 80 millones de euros antes de que finalice el año, estamos hablando del 4% del producto interior bruto de Ceuta”, ha subrayado.

También ha habido preguntas sobre la situación de Marruecos. Sánchez ha destacado el dispositivo de Marruecos desplegado al otro lado de la frontera ante un nuevo aviso de salto mayoritario este miércoles por las elecciones en este país. La idea que ha trasladado el presidente es que Marruecos ahora sí está controlando la situación. Sánchez ha suavizado su tono con Rabat y se ha centrado en lo positivo, su colaboración, y no en los errores en el control de la frontera de los que habló este martes en una entrevista con la CNN. “Quiero recordar que en las Cortes expliqué que Marruecos ya el 30 de julio empezó a dar respuesta a la crisis que vivíamos con despliegue de fuerzas armadas y policías”. Además, ha destacado, el país norteafricano hizo lo mismo el 15 de agosto, ante alertas de una nueva avalancha. ”Cuando he dicho que hemos pedido datos y acciones al Gobierno de Marruecos, me estoy refiriendo a esto, no a nada nuevo", ha precisado el presidente.

Antes de su encuentro con los medios, el presidente del Gobierno ha intervenido en el Foro Latinoamérica, España y Estados Unidos en la economía global, organizado por la Cámara de Comercio España-Estados Unidos. Y aun antes, ha compartido acto como invitado principal del alcalde neoyorquino, Zohran Mamdami, junto a otros líderes progresistas. El regidor socialista ha destacado la subida del salario mínimo como una de las medidas más destacadas del Ejecutivo progresista español.

World.title: La buena cara de la industria cosmética española
World.content:
El sector del cuidado personal y la belleza, que aporta el 1% del PIB y emplea a 50.000 personas, se alza paulatinamente como una industria puntera en España y en el mundo. Sin embargo, su futuro pasa por superar tres grandes desafíos: hacer productos más sostenibles, combatir las falsificaciones y mantener las exportaciones en un clima internacional adverso

LICO Cosmetics Estefanía Ferrer Fundadora y directora ejecutiva Laboratorio de ingeniería cosmética nacido en Sevilla y concebido como una compañía nativa digital. Cantabria Labs Juan Matji Presidente Laboratorio farmacéutico español especializado en productos para el cuidado de la salud de la piel

La industria de la cosmética no tiene que maquillar sus cifras para demostrar su éxito. Así lo cree Óscar Mateo, director de Conocimiento y Estudios de Mercado de la Asociación Nacional de Perfumería y Cosmética (Stanpa). El informe más reciente de la asociación, que integra a más del 90% del sector, en torno a 300 empresas, asegura que en los últimos cinco años, el negocio ha crecido un 44% y ha duplicado sus exportaciones. Este es un ámbito económico amplio que aglutina la fabricación de productos para la higiene personal, el cuidado de la piel y el cabello, el maquillaje y hasta los perfumes. Precisamente estos últimos constituyen, en palabras de Mateo, el buque insignia del sector, gracias al peso de compañías españolas como Puig, cuya presencia trasciende nuestras fronteras.

El otro pilar es el cuidado de la piel, para el que la industria ha adoptado el nombre en inglés: skincare. Debe su crecimiento al interés cada vez mayor por mantener una piel sana y con buen aspecto. Lo dice Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, una compañía farmacéutica que fabrica productos, tanto cosméticos como medicamentos, para el cuidado de la piel. “Antiguamente las cremas eran para un cierto grupo de mujeres que contaban con recursos económicos, hoy se ha democratizado”, explica el empresario en un nuevo capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

El auge del sector también obliga a afrontar una nueva lista de desafíos que aparecen por el camino como poros abiertos. Entre ellos, destacan la búsqueda de fórmulas más sostenibles sin perder eficacia, la protección frente a las falsificaciones y la lucha contra la llamada quimicofobia, término con el que Estefanía Ferrer, ingeniera química y fundadora de LICO Cosmetics, describe la desconfianza que ciertos ingredientes generan en la población. Ferrer, cuya marca nació en el entorno digital, comparte conversación con Matji en este episodio del pódcast. La charla entre ambos empresarios sirve para conocer mejor sus historias y desgranar un negocio que enfrenta un futuro fresco y radiante.

“El ‘skincare’ está aquí para quedarse. Antiguamente era para un cierto grupo de mujeres con recursos económicos, pero hoy se ha democratizado” Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, sobre el ‘boom’ de la cosmética en España

Las fortalezas Una industria que avanza con paso firme y se expande por el mundo

Una industria en expansión. El sector de la cosmética y el cuidado personal avanza a un ritmo moderado, pero sostenido. Ha pasado de representar el 0,9% del PIB español al 1,03% en los últimos cuatro años. Entre las razones de su consolidación se encuentran el desarrollo de una cultura del cuidado de la piel y el cabello y el bienestar personal, con una mención especial a los cosméticos para el rostro y la fotoprotección solar, que empieza a consumirse de manera notable fuera del verano.

Potencia exportadora. España vende cada año más productos al extranjero y ya supera a manufacturas emblemáticas como el aceite de oliva, el vino y el calzado. Además, España es el segundo exportador mundial de perfumes, solo por detrás de Francia.

Con buena reputación. La industria española produce bajo uno de los marcos regulatorios más exigentes del mundo: el europeo. Además, trabaja constantemente para crear formulaciones más seguras. Para ello invierte de media el 3,4% en I+D+i. La media general de las empresas españolas de toda la economía es el 0,9%, de acuerdo con el Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE). Esto permite adaptarse mejor a los cambios en el mercado. En los dos últimos años se ha reformulado uno de cada tres productos, de acuerdo con Stanpa.

Distribuida por el territorio. Aunque Cataluña, Madrid y la Comunidad Valenciana concentran gran parte de la producción, Stanpa destaca que existe bastante descentralización, como demuestran las empresas protagonistas del vídeo, con sede en Sevilla y Cantabria.

“España compite bien internacionalmente con el ‘skincare’. No tenemos nada que envidiar a los coreanos, que están tan de moda ahora” Juan Matji, presidente de Cantabria Labs, acerca del buen estado de salud de la industria española

Los desafios Un sector que se esfuerza por garantizar la seguridad de sus productos y por reducir su impacto ambiental

Adaptarse a una regulación cada vez más compleja. Los productos y los procesos tienen que responder a nuevas exigencias europeas sobre ingredientes, seguridad, información al consumidor y trazabilidad.

El reto continuo de mejorar en sostenibilidad. Las empresas se enfrentan a varios desafíos para reducir su impacto en el medio ambiente.

Limitar el uso del plástico y mejorar las posibilidades de reciclaje de sus envases

Reducir el consumo del agua en la fabricación de sus productos, así como desarrollar metodologías para medir y reducir su huella hídrica

Encontrar ingredientes biodegradables que no impacten en la naturaleza, sin perder la eficacia

Mantener la competitividad internacional. Permanecer como el segundo exportador mundial de perfumes se transforma en un desafío en un escenario internacional complejo por las tensiones comerciales, los conflictos políticos y el aumento de los aranceles. En 2025, las exportaciones a Estados Unidos cayeron un 13% por el impacto de los aranceles, de acuerdo con Stanpa.

Combatir las falsificaciones. La compra de buena parte de los productos, como los perfumes o la cosmética de alta gama, resulta aspiracional y se enmarca en el lujo accesible. Por eso, son uno de los principales objetivos de los falsificadores. Y estas copias pueden no cumplir los requisitos europeos de seguridad y etiquetado.

Luchar contra la desinformación. El consumidor cada vez está más formado, aun así, se ha extendido a través de internet la idea de que cuantos menos productos químicos tenga una crema o un perfume, mejor será para la salud, un fenómeno que se conoce como quimiofobia, ya que se da por supuesto que los ingredientes químicos pueden ser perjudiciales para la salud. Pero hay que tener cuidado con esa información, resalta la fundadora de LICO Cosmetics. Los materiales que componen un cosmético siempre son químicos, tanto si proceden de una planta como si se sintetizan en un laboratorio. Y deben ser seguros para el consumo humano, algo que se encarga de garantizar el Comité Científico de Seguridad de los Consumidores (CCSC, por sus siglas en inglés).

World.title: Escribir el futuro desde España: “Podemos ser una gran potencia tecnológica europea”
World.content:
Ruth Díaz, directora para España y Portugal de Amazon recalca el grado de digitalización del país en la última década y media y el papel que, gracias a las energías renovables, a la presencia de centros de datos y a agentes como AWS, puede jugar en los próximos años

Habla

Las vistas despejadas desde la undécima planta de este rascacielos madrileño casan a la perfección con la claridad con que discurre y se expresa Ruth Díaz, directora general de Amazon para España y Portugal: “Esta es una empresa plenamente española. Con 30.000 trabajadores, más de mil de ellos ingenieros, somos uno de los diez máximos empleadores del país. Aquí se han puesto en marcha iniciativas piloto que ahora se aplican por todo el mundo. Ya se han invertido 25.000 millones desde 2010, y se van a invertir otros 33.700 para expandir los centros de datos en Aragón en la próxima década, con los que se prevé que se generen 6.000 empleos más. No se puede arrancar a esta empresa de España”.

Cuenta Díaz en esta entrevista del espacio Hablan las marcas, con motivo del 50º aniversario de EL PAÍS, que el potencial de crecimiento es enorme: porque España es un gran productor de energías limpias y, gracias a ello, Amazon podrá cumplir su objetivo de cero emisiones netas para 2040, porque el comercio digital representa aquí todavía solo un 8% y, sin embargo, el último año ya han conseguido entregar más de 190 millones de paquetes antes de 24 horas, y hay mucho margen todavía para flexibilizar y personalizar esas recepciones; porque la implementación de herramientas tecnológicas como la IA en la empresa española está siete puntos por encima de la media europea, porque, según defiende, ella ha sido testigo de “cómo lo extraordinario se volvía cotidiano” en estos últimos 15 años, y eso es justamente lo que espera que siga ocurriendo: “Limitaremos el tiempo que las personas pierden en otras tareas para que puedan dedicárselo a sus familiares, amigos y seres queridos”.

World.title: Soy mayor de 65 años y voy a vender mi vivienda habitual. ¿Podría hacer una segunda venta más adelante y estaría exenta de tributación?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. Tengo 66 años y voy a vender mi vivienda habitual, que tiene mayor valor que la que compro. Sé que puedo optar por varios modos de exención del incremento patrimonial. En el caso de que pasado unos años quisiera vender la casa, ¿podría volver a eximir plusvalías, siendo vivienda habitual y mayor de 65 años, pero siendo una segunda venta? A. Gómez

Respuesta. Está exenta de tributación en el IRPF la ganancia patrimonial obtenida por una persona mayor de 65 años como consecuencia de la transmisión de su vivienda habitual, sin que sea necesario reinvertir el importe obtenido en la adquisición de otra vivienda ni en ningún otro producto.

A estos efectos, se considera vivienda habitual aquella de la que el contribuyente sea pleno propietario y en la que haya residido de forma efectiva y continuada durante un plazo mínimo de tres años.

Por tanto, si se cumple este requisito, cualquier ganancia patrimonial obtenida con la venta de la vivienda habitual, con independencia de su importe, estará exenta de tributación en el IRPF, aunque no se reinvierta total o parcialmente el importe obtenido en otra vivienda habitual.

Asimismo, un mismo contribuyente mayor de 65 años puede beneficiarse de esta exención en más de una ocasión, siempre que cada una de las viviendas transmitidas tenga la consideración de vivienda habitual en el momento de la venta. Para ello, será necesario que haya residido en la nueva vivienda de manera efectiva y continuada durante un período mínimo de tres años.

En consecuencia, también podría aplicarse la exención a la ganancia patrimonial generada por la venta de una nueva vivienda habitual adquirida con posterioridad, aunque se trate de una segunda transmisión de vivienda habitual realizada por una persona mayor de 65 años.

No obstante, esta exención se refiere exclusivamente a la ganancia patrimonial en el IRPF. Es decir, no está exento del Impuesto sobre el Incremento de Valor de los Terrenos de Naturaleza Urbana (plusvalía municipal), que también se devenga con motivo de la venta y debe liquidarse ante el ayuntamiento correspondiente, aunque se trate de la vivienda habitual de una persona mayor de 65 años.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: 10 experiencias en el Matarraña para sacarle todo el jugo a la comarca aragonesa en septiembre
World.content:
Pedalear por la vía verde de la Val de Zafán, caminar por el Solo Sculpture Trail, dormir en un antiguo molino de papel y más pistas en esta zona de la provincia de Teruel que es tierra de cañones y, sobre todo, de buitres

Wikipedia dice, todo el mundo repite —incluida la IA—, y será verdad mientras no se demuestre lo contrario, que el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del planeta es el Matarraña. Este afluente del Ebro, de casi 100 kilómetros de longitud, ha dado nombre a la comarca en la que Teruel se funde y confunde con Tarragona y Castellón, y ha labrado las rocas calizas de los Puertos de Beceite, donde nace, como si en vez de agua pura llevara carburo de silicio verde, abrasivo y cortante a más no poder. Aparte de fabulosos cañones y de pozas que piden a gritos bañarse hasta bien entrado el otoño, este rincón del noreste de la provincia de Teruel tiene muchas otras cosas que sorprenden al viajero.

La primera es que aquí no hablan como los demás turolenses, sino chapurriau, una variedad aragonesa del catalán cantarina y cadenciosa que, a los forasteros, salvo que sean de las provincias de al lado, les suena a valenciano. Matarraña —o Matarranya, como lo escriben también— es un no parar de sorpresas. Tomen nota de estas 10.

Más información 24 horas en Ayamonte, la ciudad de Huelva donde vivir uno de los mejores atardeceres de Europa

Penetrar en la comarca siguiendo a un tren loco

Por Matarraña pasó un tren hoy difícil de explicar, que iba de La Puebla de Híjar a Tortosa, del norte de Teruel al Bajo Ebro, y que pretendía llegar algún día hasta la orilla del mar. Un loco sueño ferroviario que duró 30 años (de 1941 a 1971) y que dejó este abrupto y solitario rincón del mapa aragonés lleno de puentes inútiles y de estaciones en mitad de ninguna parte.

Se esfumó el tren, pero su itinerario y su espíritu insensatos permanecen en la vía verde de la Val de Zafán. Una buena manera de hincarle el diente a la comarca es echarse a pedalear desde la que fue la estación de Valjunquera con las bicis y los guías de Senda. Salvo en un par de túneles, que no se ve nada, se va descubriendo un paisaje cada vez más ordenado de olivos y almendros y una luz cada vez más mediterránea. Hay una parada obligada en el alto viaducto que hay a 9,5 kilómetros del inicio, para saludar al río Matarraña. Al otro lado, en otra antigua estación, se halla el muy recomendable hotel La Parada del Compte.

Comer lo que comió Picasso

Pedaleando por una vía verde llana no es que se haga mucho ejercicio, pero hambre sí que se hace. Para calmarla, no hay mejor opción en toda la comarca que Fonda Alcalá. Ubicado en Calaceite, miembro de la Asociación Los Pueblos Más Bonitos de España, por esta casa de comidas algo más que centenaria —data de 1922— han pasado García Márquez, Álvaro Cunqueiro, Francesc Català Roca, Paco de Lucía, Serrat… No en este orden, lógicamente. El que no pasó, pero sí comió lo que aquí se hace, fue Picasso. Les perdius de Picasso, las perdices que le guisaron en esta casa y le llevaron enlatadas a Francia en 1967, y las judías blancas de Beceite con sardinas de cubo son dos platos legendarios, fundamentales. Pero el chef Ignacio Alcalá se inventa todos los días otros más excitantes y divertidos, que es lo que aprendió a hacer en las cocinas de Neichel y Can Roca.

Hacer senderismo en una galería de arte

He aquí sin duda lo más flipante de la comarca, naturaleza aparte: Solo Houses, una hermosa finca campestre de 200 hectáreas en el municipio de Cretas, donde llevan 13 años materializándose como naves alienígenas casas alucinantes de arquitectos de vanguardia que se pueden alquilar desde 850 euros por noche y donde pronto lo hará un hotel de habitaciones circulares exentas, con vistas al bosque diseñado por Smiljan Radić, Premio Pritzker 2026. Obviamente, alojarse aquí es solo para amantes de la arquitectura y gente con pasta.

Una mujer pasea entre esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, en la localidad de Cretas. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

El resto debe contentarse con ver los ovnis de lejos, paseando entre las vides de la bodega Venta D’Aubert y las esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, un circuito creado por los propietarios de todo esto, los galeristas Christian Bourdais y Eva Albarrán, para exponer al aire libre y vender obras que tampoco parecen de este mundo. Se tarda hora y media en ver las 20 esculturas y solo cuesta cinco euros. También se puede visitar la bodega y catar cinco de sus vinos por 25.

La bodega Venta D’Aubert. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Asomarse a la vecina Tarragona por un desfiladero

Si pasear por un sendero de pago entre esculturas carísimas parece algo pijo y rebuscado, en el pueblo de al lado, en Arnes, podemos hacerlo en un lugar verdaderamente salvaje, el desfiladero de Els Estrets, y bañarnos en las aguas inmaculadas del río que lo atraviesa —un afluente del río Algás, que a su vez lo es del Matarraña—, sin pagar un euro. Al llegar al aparcamiento donde arranca la senda, descubriremos estupefactos Les Gronses, unas formidables moles anaranjadas donde pululan escaladores, cabras monteses y buitres leonados.

El desfiladero de Els Estrets, en la vecina Terra Alta de Tarragona. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Y nada más echarnos a andar, un cartel que dice: “Parc Natural dels Ports”. Estamos en Cataluña, concretamente en la Terra Alta de Tarragona. Otro cartel advierte que el baño solo está permitido en el Toll Blau (el charco azul). Allí veremos dos o tres humanos y, más adelante, si es que se dejan ver, alguna nutria y la libélula Macromia splendens, en peligro de extinción. Mucho más fácil de observar, libando en las lavandas, es la mariposa Cleopatra. El desfiladero se recorre, yendo y volviendo por camino evidente, en un par de horas.

Dormir en un antiguo molino de papel

Vistas desde el hotel La Fábrica de Solfa, en Beceite. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Beceite, además de un bonito pueblo, con muchas de sus casas colgadas sobre el encañonado río Matarraña, es el campo base ideal para explorar la comarca, porque está cerca de su paraje más deseado —el Parrizal, donde nace aquél— y porque hay un hotelito familiar que es un hotelazo. La Fábrica de Solfa, que así se llama, fue un molino de papel: con la fuerza del río se trituraba ropa vieja y se obtenía la pasta necesaria. Ahora es una fábrica de actividades: todas las que se cuentan en este reportaje y algunas más. De amorosos cuidados que prodigan Javier y Alberto Moragrega a los que llegan exhaustos después de hacerlas. Y de ricos platos: el recapte de fesols de Beceite, el ternasco de Aragón, las texturas de té de roca y todo lo que se sirve en el restaurante Marca al Agua. Tampoco se desayuna mal, viendo a las nutrias jugar en el río saltarín. Lo único malo es que aparecen al rayar el sol, así que hay que madrugar.

Darse un baño de multitudes y otro en un ‘fish spa’ natural

A solo tres kilómetros de Beceite se encuentra el Parrizal (o Parrissal), el desfiladero que nadie que visita esta comarca deja de admirar y recorrer, a tal punto que hay que reservar online para evitar mayores aglomeraciones de las que ya se forman sobre las tablas de dos palmos de ancho que hay instaladas en las paredes verticales del cañón, a buena altura sobre las aguas impolutas del recién nacido Matarraña. Avanzar nadando por el propio río, que sería lo deseable para librarse del sudor propio y de los atascos, está prohibido.

Pasarelas en la senda del Parrizal. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Donde sí está permitido mojarse y remojarse es en La Pesquera, en las pozas que forma el río Ulldemó, afluente del Matarraña, a tres kilómetros también de Beceite. Comparadas con las de otros ríos de montaña, estas aguas de hipnótico color verde jade son hasta cálidas. Y mucho más relajantes: metes los pies y acuden docenas de diminutos barbos y madrillas a limpiar tus células muertas. Esto es ictioterapia y La Pesquera, un fish spa natural, sin kimonos ni musiquillas new age.

Remar con el último sol en el pantano de Pena

Kayak al atardecer en el pantano de Pena. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

A la misma distancia de Beceite que el Parrizal y La Pesquera, está el pantano de Pena, uno de los más antiguos de Teruel (de 1930) y el único de la cuenca del Matarraña. Si hubiera muchos pantanos, no sería el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del mundo. Ir allí a navegar en kayak al atardecer es una de las actividades que recomienda y organiza La Fábrica de Solfa. Desde el hotel se llega con una bici eléctrica en un cuarto de hora y, después de rodear el embalse en media más, se embarca y se rema hasta el centro para admirar cómo el penúltimo sol se duplica en la cabecera y el agua se vuelve de oro. Girando luego el kayak en redondo y apuntando con la proa hacia el noreste, se ve cómo los últimos rayos iluminan la Caixa, una cumbre que a los matarrañeses les parece que tiene forma de caja de caudales y por eso la llaman así. Si remando y girando se vuelca accidentalmente, o adrede para refrescarse, no pasa nada: aquí está permitido el baño.

Asistir al banquete de 500 aves carroñeras

José Ramón Moragrega entre buitres en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

En la sierra de Arca, donde está la Caixa, anidan multitud de buitres leonados. No es solo que allí hay cortados rocosos idóneos para ellos. Es que al pie de la montaña, en una masía de Valderrobres, vive José Ramón Moragrega, que lleva más de 30 años alimentándolos. Todos los días, Buitreman —así le llaman— sale a las 9.15 con una carretilla llena de pulmones de cerdo y la vuelca ante una muchedumbre expectante de estas enormes carroñeras. Hasta 500 de ellas se reúnen para compartir de muy malos modos este desayuno, formando una monumental tremolina de polvo, chillidos e iracundos aleteos. Todo puede verse y fotografiarse en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol, una masía que es también un formidable hide, con grandes ventanales orientados a los cuatro vientos para no perderse nada, desde el momento en que Buitreman vuelca la carretilla y se aparta a toda velocidad de sus pequeños de picos afilados como cuchillos —por eso va con casco, porque más de una vez ha salido descalabrado—, hasta cuando aparecen los alimoches para disputarse las migajas de la tragantona.

Al despedirse de los visitantes, Moragrega les confía casi entre lágrimas su delicado estado de salud y que sus niños pueden quedarse pronto sin desayuno si alguna entidad pública o privada no asume la gestión del observatorio, que es también alojamiento rural. Es un negocio rentable, asegura.

Vuelta a las rocas huesudas del Masmut

Muchos buitres leonados que desayunan en Mas de Bunyol pasan el resto del día haciendo la digestión en las Rocas del Masmut, en Peñarroya de Tastavins, donde hay una importante colonia de ellos. El PR TE-157, uno de los Senderos Turísticos de Aragón, bien mantenido y señalizado, invita a rodear este manojo de peñas anaranjadas de más de 100 metros de altura, similares a los Mallos de Riglos, cuyo nombre se cree que viene de los masmuda, una tribu bereber que quizá estuviera asentada aquí cuando España era musulmana.

Es una ruta circular de poco más de tres horas, cuatro si el senderista se desvía a los tres kilómetros para subir al mirador del Masmut. Situado a 500 metros de las rocas y a similar altura, es un buen lugar para verlas como las ven los buitres, asomando como las falanges de un gigante muerto y enterrado bajo la costra caliza del Matarraña.

Un pícnic regenerativo para despedirse del Matarraña

La última sorpresa de esta ruta llena de ellas la puede dar Tel·lúric, una masía centenaria del municipio de Ráfels cuyos nuevos propietarios no es que respeten la tradición agrícola de los masos, de estas catedrales civiles del campo matarrañés, es que van un paso más allá. O un paso más acá, porque trabajan la tierra con tal cuidado que no solo no se agota, sino que se regenera. Los olivos, los almendros y las viñas que atiende Sorin Dragoman no son soldados invasores de ejércitos cuadriculados, sino pacíficos hermanos de los pinos, las carrascas, el tomillo, el romero, el té de roca y el poleo.

Con todo lo que aquí se produce (vinos, aceite y almendras con certificación ecológica y de agricultura regenerativa) dispuesto sobre un mantel a cuadros, y también con las carnes a la brasa que salen sin parar de la cocina, se organizan unos pícnics delante de la masía que son una manera estupenda de despedirse del Matarraña. El águila culebrera sobrevuela los cultivos de Tel·lúric sin sospechar que son cosa de humanos.

World.title: “Facade politics” is making far-right ideas acceptable: AIVD
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Far-right organisations are using euphemistic terms such as “remigration” to establish racist and discriminatory ideas in mainstream debate, the Dutch security services have warned.

The intelligence agency AIVD and the national counter-terrorism co-ordinator said “façade politics” was designed to mask extremist ideas by expressing them in more palatable language.

Groups such as White Lives Matter, the Active Club Dietsland and the Greater Netherlands Student Union (GNSV) had emerged in the last 10 years under the banner of “identitarian resistance”, itself a euphemism for white supremacism.

“In reality many identitarians are convinced of ‘white superiority’ and show an aversion to other cultures and religions, as well as white people who think differently such as feminists and LGBTI+ people,” the agencies said.

Far-right groups are also infiltrating demonstrations against asylum seeker centres, organising international conferences and influencing political parties.

The right-wing parties JA21, Forum voor Democratie, Geert Wilders’ PVV and the the BoerBurgerBeweging took 30% of the vote between them in last October’s general election. All used the term “remigration” in their election manifestos.

Weekend riots

The report was published after a weekend in which 300 people gathered for an anti-immigration protest in The Hague organised by a group calling itself Wij Zijn Het Volk (“We are the people”).

Protesters made Nazi salutes, chanted anti-Semitic slogans and carried banners with messages such as “blanke mannen vooraan” (white men first).

The demonstration was cancelled after rioters clashed with police who ordered them to remove their face masks. Altogether 24 people were arrested. It was the second year in a row that an anti-immigration demonstration on the city’s Malieveld triggered violent confrontations with police.

The AIVD estimates that “several hundred Dutch people” are involved in right-wing terrorist activity and there is a real chance that some will resort to actual violence.

But they also said the groups were at undermining the democratic system “by stealth”, using social media platforms such as TikTok and X to spread extremist ideas.

“The effect in the long term can be greater than a terrorist attack,” the report said.

World.title: Dutch to return to Eurovision Song Contest in 2027 after boycott
World.content:
The Netherlands will return to Eurovision in 2027, after pulling out this year over the participation of Israel.

Dutch public broadcaster NPO has taken over the reins after broadcaster AVROTROS announced earlier this year the country would not send a participant.

“The Song Contest was originally founded to bring people in Europe together. to bring together after the Second World War. We are seeking that connection again now,” Jet de Ranitz, of NPO’s executive board, said in a statement.

The Netherlands was one of five countries that refused to enter last year’s competition in response to the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, although the contest in Austria was still shown on Dutch TV by public broadcaster NPO. Ireland has said it will stay away again in 2027, with Spain likely to follow suit.

The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) has since changed its rules to ban winning countries from hosting the following year’s event if they are involved in a “sensitive geopolitical situation” that affects the “security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region”.

World.title: Freelancing in the Netherlands? First get your tax sorted!
World.content:
Setting up your own business or going it alone as a freelancer takes a lot of time and energy, and it is easy to forget some of the things you need to do. For example, if you are considering becoming a ZZP’er, how can you make sure you keep on the right side of the taxman?

Dealing with BTW

One of the first bits of paperwork you will be confronted with if you go into business in the Netherlands is dealing with BTW — omzetbelasting, or value added tax. “What people often forget is that they do have to submit their VAT return every three months even if they have only just started in business,” says Andra Radu, from Taxmo, an online bookkeeping and tax platform for freelancers, which largely focuses on helping internationals.

“Your first VAT deadline can arrive sooner than you expect. Starting a business doesn’t necessarily mean you have three months before you need to think about VAT. Depending on when you register, the VAT quarter may already be underway. And even if you haven’t made much money yet, you may still have a return to submit.”

Using a smart bookkeeping software, like that developed by Taxmo, means you can produce and send your invoices, keep a record of suppliers and upload the invoices they have sent you, calculate your personal expenses, and deal with your VAT and your income tax on one all-encompassing platform. You don’t even have to fill in the tax office’s own forms because Taxmo does it for you.

Understanding tax terminology

For many internationals, the difficult part isn’t running the business itself, it’s understanding the language and administration around it. You must file a VAT return if you are registered as an entrepreneur with the tax office (and have been assigned a VAT number starting with NL), if you are a ZZP’er — or freelancer — or if you are running a VOF, BV, or eenmanszaak (partnership, limited company, or sole proprietorship).

The jargon can seem incomprehensible and Dutch tax terms, unfamiliar deadlines and different rules for different types of clients can make a relatively simple freelance business feel much more complicated than it actually is.

Tax rules for freelancers

One rule freelancers may not be aware of, for example, is the KOR — yes, more jargon — the small business ruling, which, simply put, means that if you book annual turnover of less than €20,000 a year, you may be able to avoid dealing with VAT altogether.

Qualifying for the KOR doesn’t automatically mean it’s the best choice for your business. If you have significant business expenses, being unable to reclaim VAT on them can make a difference. It’s also worth thinking about how quickly you expect your business to grow rather than looking only at your turnover today.

“Business expenses are another area where new freelancers can easily get confused,” says Andra. “Keeping track of invoices, receipts and expenses from the beginning makes life much easier when it’s time to file, particularly when you’re still learning which costs actually count.”

Cross-border VAT

As an international freelancer, you may well have clients in other countries, and that’s something you’ll need to sort out too when keeping on top of your taxes. “This is particularly relevant for internationals, who often continue working with clients outside the Netherlands after setting up here,” Andra points out.

“You might have a Dutch client, an EU client and a US or UK client in your first few months of freelancing. How you handle VAT can depend on where the client is based, whether they’re a business or consumer and what you’re selling, so it isn’t always as simple as adding 21% to an invoice.”

File your tax returns yourself

Of course, smart software cannot solve all problems. There will always be situations where professional advice is useful, particularly as a business becomes more complex. But freelancers with relatively straightforward businesses don’t necessarily need to outsource every VAT return or routine piece of administration.

“Becoming a ZZP’er does not mean you need to understand every part of the Dutch tax system yourself or hire an expensive accountant for every filing,” says Andra. “Our platform has been designed specifically for the Dutch situation, to make sure you can do as much as you can yourself. We are all Dutch taxpayers even if we don’t speak the local language, or at any rate not much. Paying tax is not something you can avoid, but you can make it as easy as possible.”

Find out here how Taxmo helps freelancers handle bookkeeping, VAT and income tax in the Netherlands, without having to become Dutch tax experts themselves.

World.title: Military police investigate death of Dutch woman in Aruba crash
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Military police are investigating the death of a 23-year-old Dutch woman after an all-terrain vehicle overturned on the Caribbean island of Aruba.

Local police initially said Kimberly van Ardenne, from Rotterdam, was driving the vehicle when the accident happened on Sunday, September 13, but her family said they had heard conflicting accounts.

Relatives have posted an appeal on Facebook appealing for witnesses to the crash, which happened at 3pm.

Two male naval officers were with Kimberly in the car at the time, one of whom was a friend she was staying with on the island.

The Dutch military police force (Koninklijke Marechaussee) said it was investigating the crash because it involved armed forces personnel. The force has pledged to “get to the bottom” of the incident.

Several tour guides are said to have witnessed the incident, according to local news website Aruba.nu, some of whom said they had seen the vehicle make a “manoeuvre” just before it overturned.

“Not a daredevil”

One family member told NOS Kimberly was not a keen driver. “You’d describe her as more of a cautious person than a daredevil. We can’t understand how this could have happened if she was behind the wheel.”

The family’s lawyer, Peter Schouten, told RTL Nieuws he was making his own enquiries on behalf of the family.

“We are investigating whether there is any question of liability, whether this is a case of reckless driving and whether anyone has made false statements,” he said.

“We already have a lot of information from social media, but we are still looking for witnesses.”

The family has asked anyone with information to contact them through the Facebook post or via Whatsapp on +31 6 40580456.

World.title: Fire fighters investigating a gas leak turn out to be the cause
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

When the residents of the Brabant town of Oisterwijk smelled the pungent odor of gas on Wednesday, they called their local fire department, who turned out to be the culprits.

Fire fighters spent the morning searching for a gas leak to no avail. Together with gas provider Enexis, they tested levels throughout the town but could not find a source, only the smell.

Meanwhile, back at the fire station, staff discovered a canister of THT was missing. The chemical is added to gas, which is naturally odorless, to so that people can smell any leak immediately.

The cannister had been accidently thrown out and had spent the morning in the back of a garbage truck, which was making its rounds.

“We were able to have a laugh about it for a moment,” firefighter Ronald Blokpoel told Omroep Brabant.

Residents may continue to smell gas for a time while the chemical dissipates. The fire depart warns there is no danger to public health.

World.title: Mourners claim diabetic man who died under arrest was “murdered”
World.content:
Around 150 people joined a funeral procession on Wednesday for a man who died while being detained by police who stopped him while searching for a stolen fatbike.

The body of 51-year-old Alfredo Goeloe was carried in a white coffin in a carriage drawn by two white horses to the Zuiderbegraafplaats in Rotterdam, 10 days after he collapsed while being pinned to the ground and handcuffed.

Friends and relatives who followed the coffin carried banners with slogans including “samen tegen onrecht omdat we om elkaar geven” (united against injustice because we care for each other).

One of the mourners, Yenci Vargas, told Nieuwsuur: “He was murdered. I’m not talking about racism, but he was murdered by the negligence and stupidity of the police.”

Another, Marsha Mabosa, said: “Last month we were out in a café and he asked me to dance the bachata. He was a very good dancer. And now we have to miss him in a way that is very unjust.”

Stolen fatbike

Goeloe was stopped by police while riding a fatbike through Rotterdam on the evening of Saturday, September 12.

Police initially said he was suspected of stealing the bike, but later changed their story to say he had been stopped because he was riding too fast. Just before Goeloe’s arrest a fatbike had been reported stolen by a couple aged around 40.

Goeloe tried to run from police when they tried to arrest him for not carrying ID. His family said he had borrowed his sister’s bike to go out to get medication for his diabetes.

He was chased down and passed out while he was being restrained on his belly. Video footage showed he cried out that he had diabetes and was in pain as he lay on the ground.

Official complaint

Goeloe’s family have filed a criminal complaint against four police officers. Lawyer Gerard Roethof said they viewed it as “a case of manslaughter, or in any event severe assault with fatal consequences.”

Jan Schalkwijk, a lawyer with Control Alt Delete, an organisation that monitors racial profiling in the Netherlands, said the use of force by police was excessive.

“The officers were far superior in number, according to reports he was unarmed, and he could have been approached with less force,” Schalkwijk argued.

Restraint guidelines

But Jaap Timmer, a political scientist at the VU university in Amsterdam who specialises in police use of force, said there was no indication from the film footage that the police had failed to follow protocol.

He said police guidelines said people should be pressed against the ground for as short a time as possible when under arrest, but it was unsafe to let them stand up before they had been handcuffed.

“I understand the police were looking for a fatbike and this man was riding too fast. That could be a reason to ask his identity,” he said.

“He then ran away fast and resisted his arrest. That has nothing to do with ethnic profiling, but with the man’s behaviour.”

World.title: Road safety institute weighing up zero alcohol limit for drivers
World.content:
The Dutch Road Safety Research Institute has released a new study on reducing the drug and alcohol limit for drivers to zero, finding it would probably decrease road accidents but would increase pressure on the police.

SWOV looked at the policy in eight countries with limits lower than the Netherlands, which is of blood alcohol level of 0.05% or 0.02% for those who have been driving for less than 5 years.

The risk of accidents is already elevated at the 0.05% level, the report says. Other countries, including Norway and Sweden, set the level at 0.02% for all drivers.

“An absolute zero limit is considered to be a simple and unambiguous standard that leaves less room for interpretation of what is still permissible and what is not,” the report says, and would improve road safety.

However, lowering the limit will lead to more work for police but also testing facilities. It can be difficult, especially with cannabis, to properly detect the levels, especially with saliva tests.

“Particularly for THC and cocaine, concentrations or metabolites can remain detectable long after the immediate effects have disappeared,” the institute wrote, which would create legal problems for criminal prosecutions.

World.title: Water used to put out waste plant fire contaminated with PFAS
World.content:
Firefighters used water contaminated with PFAS chemicals to put out a blaze at a waste processing plant in Gelderland that was operating illegally.

Aalden municipal council said the water would have to be pumped out of the sewage network to prevent it polluting drinking water supplies, because the purification system is not able to filter it out.

The blaze in Dinxperlo, a village on the German border, burned for several hours on Monday night after a large pile of wood chippings caught fire, covering an area of 20m by 30m at its height.

Firefighters pumped water from Het Blauwe Meer, a nearby recreational lake that has been closed to swimmers since 2024 because of high levels of PFAS. Most of the water subsequently drained away into the sewage system.

The council said it was investigating the impact, but there was no reason to avoid drinking tap water. “At the moment there are no consequences for the use of the sewage network by residents,” a spokesman said.

Police are also investigating the fire. The waste processing plant was shut down in November 2025 on the orders of the council for “serious breaches of environmental regulations.”

No permits

The operators burned large quantities of waste that they did not have permits for and mixed different types of waste that should have been separated, the council found.

Recent studies found that high levels of PFAS are present in Dutch drinking water supplies, particularly in western areas where the water is taken from rivers that have been contaminated by agricultural use.

PFAS chemicals are widely used in pesticides, packaging and products ranging from waterproof clothing to non-stick cooking pans.

They are known as “forever chemicals” because of their high durability, but have also been linked to illnesses such as cancer, diseases of the immune system and complications in unborn babies.

The public health agency RIVM has called for a total ban on PFAS in pesticides by the EU, a move also supported in Germany and the Scandinavian nations.

World.title: Poland and Belarus seek thaw in relations as foreign ministers meet for first time in a decade

The foreign ministers of Poland and Belarus have met for the first time in a decade, as both sides indicated that they are open to thawing their long-frosty relations. The two countries have regularly clashed in recent years, in particular over Minsk’s alliance with Moscow, the migration crisis Belarus has engineered on the Polish border, and the persecution of Belarus’s ethnic Polish minority. Warsaw, meanwhile, has supported the Belarusian democratic opposition. However, on Tuesday this week, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski confirmed to reporters that he had met with his Belarusian counterpart, Maxim Ryzhenkov, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Sikorski said that the initiative had come from the Belarusian side. “When a neighbour wants to unfreeze and improve relations, Poland is the first to reach an agreement,” said Sikorski, quoted by broadcaster RMF. “This is a first, introductory meeting, but meetings with other ministries and at other levels are also taking place,” he added, noting that Poland will also “soon be opening a new embassy building in Minsk”. When asked what topics had been discussed, Sikorski said that they had included the border situation and regional security. Asked if he had requested that Belarus not allow Russia to fly drones and missiles through its territory, he said that this was discussed “among other things”. The last known time that the Polish and Belarusian foreign ministers met was in October 2016, when Belarus’s Vladimir Makei visited Witold Waszczykowski in Warsaw. Sikorski said that this week’s meeting with Ryzhenkov had been possible because the situation on their shared border – where Belarus has since 2021 encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants, mainly from Asia and Africa, to cross into Poland – is now “more normalised”. Poland has installed physical and electronic barriers along the border, sent thousands of armed officers to guard it, and has banned asylum claims by migrants who cross irregularly. Following those measures, the number of attempted crossings has fallen dramatically this year. Sikorski also noted that relations have been improved by Belarus’s recent decisions to release political prisoners, including Polish ones. Most prominent among them is Andrzej Poczobut, a leader of the Polish community in Belarus, who had been imprisoned on trumped-up charges for five years. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Minsk’s recent actions have provided “more freedom and greater reasons to try to stabilise relations”, said Sikorski. “A snowdrop can bloom if the weather is favorable.” Belarus’s foreign ministry continued that metaphor in a post on social media on Wednesday, sharing a photo of Sikorski meeting with Ryzhenkov and writing that “snowdrop diplomacy is a nice restart”. “But we’re in it for the harvest,” added the ministry. “Let’s plant an orchard – it needs nurturing every year, not once a decade. Minsk is ready to host.” Last year, Belarus called for “dialogue” with Poland in order to “reduce the risk of armed clashes” amid a military build-up around the border. However, it also issued a formal protest to Poland over a demonstration in Warsaw organised by exiled opponents of Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko. .@sikorskiradek, snowdrop diplomacy is a nice restart. But we’re in it for the harvest. Let’s plant an orchard 🍎 – it needs nurturing every year, not once a decade. Minsk is ready to host 🇧🇾🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/WSN5n4uOtE — Belarus MFA 🇧🇾 (@BelarusMFA) September 23, 2026 News of Tuesday’s meeting was criticised by Stanisław Żaryn, who served as spokesman for the Polish security services under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government and later as an advisor to President Andrzej Duda. In a social media post, he said that Sikorski and media outlets are “forcibly pushing us into another reset with Belarus (and perhaps even with Russia)”. However, “Belarus chose its strategic path long ago and won’t turn away from Russia”, he added. He asked if Poles are meant to forget about the death of Mateusz Sitek, a Polish soldier killed by a migrant from a group trying to force its way over the border from Belarus. His suspected killer, a Moroccan national, is believed by Polish prosecutors to still be in Belarus, which has refused to extradite him. Should “we just move on as if nothing happened regarding Belarus’s involvement in the war against Ukraine and the intelligence war against Poland?” continued Żaryn. ⚠️Radosław Sikorski spotkał się z Szefem MSZ Białorusi. Media już piszą o „przełomie”, a Sikorski zapewnia, że „Polska jest pierwsza do zgody”. Na siłę wtłaczają nas w kolejny reset z Białorusią (a być może i Rosją). Na czym mają polegać przełomy i „zgoda” w stosunkach z… pic.twitter.com/DZ41wSgjL0 — Stanisław Żaryn (@StZaryn) September 23, 2026 Francišak Viačorka, a leading figure in the exiled Belarusian democratic opposition, also expressed scepticism in an interview with Polish newspaper Fakt. “We believe that the authorities in Minsk cannot be trusted,” he said. “Of course, when the authorities communicate with Western partners, they promise that everything will be fine, that they want dialogue, but then their words fail to match their actions.” “I understand that Minister Sikorski is doing everything to protect Polish interests and the sovereignty and security of his country, but I think that in Minsk they see it differently.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Russian military helicopter violates Polish airspace
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and may be updated as further details emerge. A Russian military helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace on Wednesday morning, the operational command of Poland’s armed forces has announced. The incident is the latest in a series of airspace violations by Russia, which have also involved drones and, most recently, a missile. It follows recent warnings by the Polish government that Moscow has been planning further “provocations” intended to test NATO’s defences and unity. ❗️ Informujemy, że 23 września br. o godz. 11.08, na północ od miejscowości Braniewo, doszło do krótkotrwałego naruszenia przestrzeni powietrznej Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej przez śmigłowiec Mi-8 Sił Zbrojnych Federacji Rosyjskiej. Śmigłowiec wykonywał lot z Obwodu Królewieckiego.… pic.twitter.com/afULQdSeTc — Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ (@DowOperSZ) September 23, 2026 On Wednesday afternoon, Polish operational command announced that, shortly after 11:00 a.m. that day, an Mi-8 helicopter belonging to the Russian armed forces had briefly entered Polish airspace near the town of Braniewo, after crossing from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The helicopter did not travel further than 300 metres into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds. In response, the Polish military scrambled fighter jets and placed ground forces on standby. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defences,” wrote operational command. At the time of writing, Russia has not commented on the incident. Today’s violation appears to be the first publicly reported instance of a Russian military helicopter crossing Poland’s land border. Last year, in two separate incidents, a Russian Su-24 bomber and a naval helicopter flew over Poland’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. In 2023, two helicopters belonging to the armed forces of Belarus, a close ally of Russia, briefly entered Polish airspace before crossing back over the border. On one night in September last year, around 20 Russian drones entered Poland over its eastern borders amid Russian attacks on Ukraine. Polish and allied forces shot down some of them, while others hit the ground without causing casulaties. In July this year, a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a significant explosive payload entered Polish airspace before landing in a field in eastern Poland. The object that crashed in the Lublin region on Thursday was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a "significant amount" of explosive material. The missile was "potentially very dangerous,” Poland's defence ministry confirmedhttps://t.co/NoqZwIcaWp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 In recent months, Poland and other NATO countries have been warning of Russian plans to carry out further “provocations” intended to test the alliance’s defences and unity, saying that they could include border and airspace violations. In recent weeks, Poland has regularly intercepted Russian aircraft that have flown close to Polish territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. This month, Russian drones have repeatedly hit targets in Ukraine close to the Polish border, including a passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw. Just last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that, according to intelligence sources, Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental.
